I see so many reviews and hear from so many people, that this game is pay to win. I think the reason these people think that this game is pay to win is simply because they have not put enough time into it to understand enough to be competitive. Every single thing in this game that can be used to kill someone is buyable through "certs", the in game currency that you earn by doing everything and anything in the game. (A few weapons with different camo patterns will be locked behind a real money door. However, these weapons are always just clones of other weapons that are able to be bought with certs. Like I said, the only difference is their camo pattern.)
However, all weapons in the game can also be aquired with real money to speed the process up. This is why people think this game is pay to win. They are wrong. This game is only pay to look good. Nearly all cosmetic items are locked behind the real money door. (There are a few cosmetics you can receive by completing directives, which are just challenges, and that only require you play the game and do various activites.)
The final reason people say this game is pay to win, membership. Most free to play games have some form of membership and this game is no exemption. Yes, members get increased xp gain which in turn means increased cert gain, as well as a passive cert gain, plus 500 station cash ( real money) per each month you are a member. This is all well and good, but recent changes to the game decreased the overall difficulty of gaining certs, especially for new players. The learning curve dropped alittle because of this. An extra training continent was also added to help new players get adjusted to the game.
SO in conclusion. All weapons can be bought with in game earned currency, cosmetics are what you pay real money for. The learning curve was reduced with recent additions to the game. The membership does give you bonuses, but a dedicated non membership player now has a much easier time gaining certs than they once did.

Gonna write this as a series of tips for new players rather than as an actual review. I think my hours speak to my love of this game.
For all you people out there who haven't tried this yet: WTF is wrong with you! it's free. At least try it and form your own opinions of it.
That being said, here are a few tips for getting into PS2:
-give it some time. Learning the mechanics of a game this size along with a large learning curve can be frustrating, so give yourself time to adjust
-Find a community. Planetside can get really lonely fighting by yourself, so I highly suggest playing with friends. If you don't have any friends (like me), find an outfit (clan) full of people you enjoy playing with. The only reason i have not quit this game at the 200 hour mark is because i enjoy playing with the community I joined early on.
-No gun is inherently better than another on a single faction, and the starting guns are the most balanced in terms of stats. I see a lot of new players spend their first certification points on new guns. This is possibly the WORST way to spend your experience. Invest in upgrading a vehicle or class abilities, focus on what you enjoy doing. Once you're comfortable playing with what you have invested in, then you can branch out and explore the strengths and weaknesses of other weapons
If you at least consider these points during your initial hours with planetside, your experience in-game will be immensly better, and you'll stick around for a bit longer than you were initially planning :)

One of the best games of its type to come out. It's by no means finished, but the mods help a lot. The MAIN FEATURE of the game is the ability to cusomize how many settlers you start with (up to 10), and what gear and weapons they will have. Resources are customizable as are multipliers (faster aiming, walking, etc., etc.)
That is the one feature that many games lack. The ability to customize your playing field.
It's a very tough game on the harder "how it was meant to be played" level, but you can choose an easier level. You can even disable events, one, or all. I think this is where the game shines. You also have a mod called PREPARE CAREFULLY which many players want as a core feature. The mod allows you to remove negative traits and even advance any skills to the max. You can either cheat this way, or avoid clicking "reset character" 10,000 times until the right combo appears. Naturally you will want to balace the points so you don't create super settlers and actually cheat, but you can if you wish too with the mod. You don't have to do any of this, obviously.
The game works pretty darn good. It's stable (win 7, very powerful PC--that's just what I have, I'm sure it will work well with less powerful PCs). The pathing is okay. I think the walking speeds need some adjustment, but overall the experience is quite good.
I do think to $30 price tag is a bit much for an alpha game. However, this alpha game plays very well and it has many features. Updates, I've heard, are a bit slow in comming, but since I purchased it there were 2 in about 3 weeks.
It has great replayablility because of the customization. Watch some Youtube vids to get a feel for the game. I think it's a good buy, even at the $30 price tag.
If the indie developer comes through with the extra features that the players wants this may well become one of the legendary games.

For all you people out there who haven't tried this yet: WTF is wrong with you! it's free. At least try it and form your own opinions of it.
That being said, here are a few tips for getting into PS2:
-give it some time. Learning the mechanics of a game this size along with a large learning curve can be frustrating, so give yourself time to adjust
-Find a community. Planetside can get really lonely fighting by yourself, so I highly suggest playing with friends. If you don't have any friends (like me), find an outfit (clan) full of people you enjoy playing with. The only reason i have not quit this game at the 200 hour mark is because i enjoy playing with the community I joined early on.
-No gun is inherently better than another on a single faction, and the starting guns are the most balanced in terms of stats. I see a lot of new players spend their first certification points on new guns. This is possibly the WORST way to spend your experience. Invest in upgrading a vehicle or class abilities, focus on what you enjoy doing. Once you're comfortable playing with what you have invested in, then you can branch out and explore the strengths and weaknesses of other weapons
If you at least consider these points during your initial hours with planetside, your experience in-game will be immensly better, and you'll stick around for a bit longer than you were initially planning :)

Dear god... This game made me cry, and I watched my cat die without doing that.
I will tell you the story of Valence, Colby Valence.
Valence had two friends who escaped the "problem" on the spaceship above Ragnarok; Dean, the healer, and Margerett, the Scientist. They LOVED eachother. (valence married to marg and dean their son) After a WONDERFUL defensive perimiter was set up, in an amazingly lush section of the forests, Raiders attacked. A small group of 3, but armed nonetheless. One had a Rifle, the next a club and the last one had 'nades. Valence was very brave, strong, and smart.. But he was also foolhardy, taking risks when he didn't need to; In the middle of the battle, after the Raider with 'nades died, he decided he wanted a prisoner. Dropping his gun, Valence charged in to the battle with fists flying. By now, Marg had picked up the 'nades that the Raider dropped, and was pulling back her arm to throw them when Dean ran in to save his Pa. Marg, being a Colonist on Rimworld, couldn't stop her arm from throwing the 'nade at the raiders-who were next to the now unconscious Valence!-and ended up blowing Dean up as he was running away with his father in arms. Deans body protected his pa's, but the shrapnel had hit him all over his body, and he was now bleeding out. Marg's 'nade had killed the final two Raiders, and as she ran towards her son, she realized it was too late to save him. He had died protecting his father.
When Valence awoke from his concussion - the result of a club to the face - he found an insane Marg holding nades about to kill him. He wouldnt have time to knock her out, nor could he reason with her. He knew what had to be done; taking aim with his rifle, which was beside his bed, he shot her in the forehead, between and above the eyes.
Valence went insane for a while after that, not responding to what he knew he had to do.
After he came back to his senses, he buried his son, his wife, and all the Raiders in graves he had dug with his own hands.
After this, Val wasnt ever happy, never content, and barely able to keep sane. After a couple months of being alone, Val' got a distress call on the beacon he had built. It read "Help me, I am being chased by a bunch of Raiders! I will join your colony if you can repel them." Naturally, Val' was still foolhardy. He knew he probably couldn't handle all of the Raiders, even with help from mystery man. He said he would help, and that the person could refuge in his colony. When the person arrived, Val' was so shocked that he became HAPPY! IT WAS HIS FATHER, SEMYON! Val' had no time to talk however, as the Raiders charged his meager defenses. His two deadfall traps got the first one, and the next two died by his rifle. However, there were many more. Val' knew what had to be done to save his father. He grabbed the grenades that Marg had tried to kill him with - crying in the process - and threw a grenade at his foot. The Raiders, being stupid, didn't realize this, and continued running at him. He died in a giant explosion, taking all the remaining raiders with him.
Semyon, Val's father, died of heatstroke soon after, leaving the colony empty. Another wave of settlers came, and seeing Val and Sem, decided to build a memorial. The memorial and the colony stand to this day. The End.
This is all true, and all possible in game. it is a wonderful, satisfying game that offers MANY different things to do. This story is just one play that I have going. Rimworld is honestly one of the best games I have played, aside from Half Life two.
Please buy this game, the price tag may seem a big scam for a game that looks like the screenshots, but its not.
Every dollar is well spent, and though the game gets frustating, its a GOOD frustrating. The game is difficult, or easy, or hard, or medium, or anything in between. the sense of accomplishment, the feeling of happiness after building that particular part of your futuristic castle, finishing your spaceship against all odds, having like 8 colonists all tasked with different things to do- cook, build, repair, grow, harvest, mine, medicine, wardening your prisoners, etc. - all of these are wonderfully fun. There are also MODS, YES MODS!
If you don't get this game, you are a pleb, and don't read reviews for info.

This is not just a puzzle game, it is a true sci-fi. That is to say it does not just have a science fiction theme but explores science fiction ideas. The puzzles themselves are great; each challenge helps prepare you for the next but new puzzles can still have you struggling for one key pice of inspiration. They both build off and subvert previous expactations and should never be taken at face value. While puzzles will often be clearly deliniated thinking outside the box will yield rewards.
The puzzles are only half the game though. Exploration, discovery, mystery; these things permeate through every aspect of the game. Plot critical and non-critical questions will be asked, choices will be made, and diversions are plenty. Despite the PC being mostly alone this game has a wealth of interesting charcters.
The main game has a great story. Though I would have tweaked the premise and ending a bit that is solely due to my creative tastes. The DLC is definitely worth picking up and I am glad I had bought it because by the end of the main game I was clamoring for more. The DLC set up a few interesting ideas that could have been use to spice up the ending, and it seemed like the philosophical lessons were preparing us for some hard decision making, but only one of those ideas was really followed through with.
The Talos Principle has earned its spot as one of my all time favorite games, I highly recommend it.

Our tale begins when a group of 3 crash landed on a mostly barren world one day.  With her was a middle aged architect and a "computer" (researcher). This is an incredibly interesting and visually beautiful puzzle game. The story elements and themes are very fascinating, even if they aren't presented in a highly engaging way. If you're a fan of history or classic literature (wink wink), you'll probably appreciate the unique/modern take on these themes. I went into this game knowing absolutely nothing about it other than that it was a puzzle game, and I think that's the best way to play it. There are a ton of Easter eggs in almost every map that encourage you to explore the amazing scenery, even outside of the puzzles themselves.
There are a few things that stop the game from being great. For one, the game feels a bit padded out when it doesn't really need to be. By shaving off a few hours or introducing a final game mechanic, I think the game would feel less far tedious towards the end. It wasn't tedious enough for me to stop playing, but it was getting close to the edge of becoming annoying. Sometimes it was hard to tell what game mechanics would work and what wouldn't (especially when they introduce the last few mechanics) and requires a bit of trial and error. Finally, a lot of the puzzles just weren't very hard and, frequently, just comes down to busy work or trial and error. But, there were definitely a few that stumped me for a while.
Otherwise, this game is very good. Highly recommend if you're into puzzle games.

Squad is slowly becoming the only shooter I spend way too much time in. I've become enveloped in the community and every update has me logging another 15-20 hours. This game, however, can't be played like CSGO or COD. Communication accross squads is a necessity to a sucessful round. The large scale enviorments makes using your map to locate and call out targets extremely useful, and allows for these amazing seiges of compounds, and many a great memory with my squads. Now this game is still in alpha so itn has it's share of glitches, but you head to the JoinSquad subreddit or their forums, the devs are extremely responsive and passionate about their game. I had an issues with ground textures for buildings popping in strange, and within minutes I had a response from a developer. Major updates come every 1 or 2 months, and the next update the vehicles are finally schedule for release, which should finally give a purpose to antitank roles. But as of writing, there are no vehicles and when they come should completely change the way these large scale ground battles commence. Some have commented that the visuals of this game are lackluster, and to that i would tell you to look at any other early access title. These titles are far from finished and you should be fully aware of that before you buy. Visual assets are going to change, new maps going to be added, and with the soft launch of the SDK recently we should start seeing mods for this relatively soon.
I've heard some people try to compare this game to MILSIM titles like arma, and this game really isn't a MILSIM, in the same way that arma is. Arma's controls and UI tends to be overcomplicated to the extent of nearly mapping every key on your keyboard, where as Squad is fundamentally more like the Project: Reality, with a focus on communcation and teamwork. To me, It's comparing apples and oranges, both games fill specific niches in the gaming market. Really, I reccomend both but for 2 different reasons.
So, if you're OK with the state of the game right now, I reccomend you pick it up while it's on the summer sale. I'll see you on the battlefield squaddies =)

TL:DR : This game is not for everyone and has many difficult facets to work around, but ends up being one of the most impressive accomplishments in gaming. The HD re-release does wonders to breathe new life into it, and the DLC is decent, but not enough to warrant a pre-sale purchase.
I have to confess something. When I originally got this game many years ago, I didn't like it. I thought it was boring, long, uninteresting,♥♥♥♥♥♥poor graphics, you name it. To be fair, I was a pre-teen just starting to get into RTS and this was my first base-construction, turtle-mechanic RTS. But, I had this and Command and Conquer: Generals. The little kid me went for Generals because it's awesome in every way. I also had Age of Empires III coming out sooner on my end rather than later for some of the original purchasers of this game. That was the game that stole my heart.
But I always wanted to revisit this game eventually because it was something everyone I talked to about raved about. Granted, all these people were a few years older than me, but it confused me. I thought it was the video game equivalent of molasses.
And, actually, it is. It's sweet and full of amazing surprises, but it's all thick and slow as heck. If you're a younger gamer, looking for something fast-paced, I actually would recommend something like the Command and Conquer games. Those will get your insanely sugar-rushed mind to work. But if you truly want an immersive, impressive gaming experience, this is the game for you.
GAMEPLAY
Okay, so you've got x-amount of resources, a couple of workers, and a scout. GO! That's every skirmish. It gets old. Fast. Get some friends and be trolls on the diplomacy. Set it to "Island" and build a beautiful city on an island and strip-mine all the resources. Play the missions and spam all the cheats so you can just run around and destroy things.
Versatility is the name of the game, and this game has a lot of it. It is most pronounced in the aforementioned missions which, in my humble opinion, comprise the best the game has to offer. I have spent more of my life than I can admit to playing the El Cid misisons (sidenote: SO MUCH FUN!). The voice acting is strong, the maps are amazingly well made, and the stories are more or less accurate to real history. If you just want to do this for the singleplayer aspects, than this is definitely a purchase for you.
On the other hand, if multiplaying is your way of life in gaming, I'm not entirely convinced this is the best game to multiplay as an RTS. It is certainly ubiquitous enough to be well-recognized, but tends to be less on the impressive side at times.
One last note: The HD version increases the unit cap to 500. Just imagine 500 swordsmen spamming a small map.
Haven't tried it yet, but I came close! *sigh*....I'll wait until I've done it to brag....
GRAPHICS
Awesome. Just awesome. It's like buying a Blu-ray remaster of an old 1950s movie. It just really looks so good you almost forget how old it really is. I have no complaints or suggestions here. I will reiterate that the younger of you all might not be receptive to this as much. If this is the case, I would highly recommend Age of Empires III (I'll review that later, 'cause there is a lot to be said on that topic).
CONCLUSION
10/10 easily. Being older, smarter, and less judgemental of older, less-flashy things, I have found great joy in replaying some of these missions again. Squad is slowly becoming the only shooter I spend way too much time in. I've become enveloped in the community and every update has me logging another 15-20 hours. This game, however, can't be played like CSGO or COD. Communication accross squads is a necessity to a sucessful round. The large scale enviorments makes using your map to locate and call out targets extremely useful, and allows for these amazing seiges of compounds, and many a great memory with my squads. Now this game is still in alpha so itn has it's share of glitches, but you head to the JoinSquad subreddit or their forums, the devs are extremely responsive and passionate about their game. I had an issues with ground textures for buildings popping in strange, and within minutes I had a response from a developer. Major updates come every 1 or 2 months, and the next update the vehicles are finally schedule for release, which should finally give a purpose to antitank roles. But as of writing, there are no vehicles and when they come should completely change the way these large scale ground battles commence. Some have commented that the visuals of this game are lackluster, and to that i would tell you to look at any other early access title. These titles are far from finished and you should be fully aware of that before you buy. Visual assets are going to change, new maps going to be added, and with the soft launch of the SDK recently we should start seeing mods for this relatively soon.
I've heard some people try to compare this game to MILSIM titles like arma, and this game really isn't a MILSIM, in the same way that arma is. Arma's controls and UI tends to be overcomplicated to the extent of nearly mapping every key on your keyboard, where as Squad is fundamentally more like the Project: Reality, with a focus on communcation and teamwork. To me, It's comparing apples and oranges, both games fill specific niches in the gaming market. Really, I reccomend both but for 2 different reasons.
So, if you're OK with the state of the game right now, I reccomend you pick it up while it's on the summer sale. I'll see you on the battlefield squaddies =)

Bought this game expecting a light hearted first person shooter where I could kill nazi's and enjoy life. I got that, BUT NO ONE SIGNED ME UP FOR THIS FEELS TRIP!!!!
This game has put more effort into it than most games ever have. What I did not expect from a Wolfenstein game is how perfect and immersive the story is. I won't spoil it for you, but the story was much appreciated and had me on the edge of my seat the entire time. The characters are extremely fleshed out. Don't get me started about how they developed the Nazi's... They captured what it would be like if they won the war. They generally make you hate them, not that you already don't, but they've fleshed out the enemy more so than others, giving you reasons to hate their guts throughout the story, building up that they are unstoppable and that you have little chance, but you keep going anyways. THIS IS ALL IN A WOLFENSTEIN GAME. Extremely unexpected, but VERY much appreciated!
Gameplay wise is your standard shooter, that remains faithful to the Wolfenstein series. It strays far away from stereotypical shooters now a days, such as Call of Duty. You can dual weild anything in the game. Yes, even assault rifles, shotguns, and snipers. Unrealistic? Yes. Fun? You bet. Besides, if you want a realistic game, don't purchase a game where there are Mecha Nazi Dogs and Cyborg Nazis... Back to the gameplay, it's a first person shooter with RPG elements. You can gain traits by doing specific things. The traits range from useful things such as highlighting commanders on the map, extra headshot damage, and Extra damage while dual weilding. The gunplay felt fantastic and the action is high paced. Difficulty wise? You'll have trouble if you don't play it smart. You can run and gun, or you can use stealth. But on higher difficulties, Stealth is a must, which I don't really like so much. Because in the higher difficulties the Nazis have pin point accuracy, and can shoot you from across the map with an assault rifle and you can't even hit them with a sniper rifle. There is no multiplayer, but the singleplayer campaign makes up for it by how fleshed out and long it is. It took me about 9-10 hours to complete it. Another thing I love about the difficulties are the old school names. Very easy is "Can I play? Daddy?" Easy is "Don't hurt me!" Normal is "Bring Em On!" Hard is "I am death incarnate!" and very hard is "Uber." By the difficulty settings, you can tell the game respects and appreciates the old Wolfenstein games. There is no regenerating health in the game, you have to find health kits to heal and also armor kits to increase armor, which soaks the damage you take. You are rewarded by exploring by finding health kits, ammo, and there are plenty of collectables. Another thing I love what they did, is the destructable cover in areas. You get a laser cutter in the game at some point, and you are able to cut through things to either gain access to new areas, or open metal crates to find ammo and armor.
This was a very good and fantastic game, with plenty of unexpected, but appreciated concepts added in that I very much enjoyed. I reccommend this to old-school FPS players, and if you are a Wolfenstein fan? You should of already bought it.

Most fun I've had with a game in a while, here is my story, of my first crashlanders. This was 7 hrs of gameplay...
Three people crash land from a colony ship into a desert. A Mother, A soldier Son, and a Doctor who is a pacifist. The son naturally becomes the leader and the three struggle a lot for food. Through this time nothing much of interest happens except the gradual build of a settlement and a visitor from another one. The three are loving life, with two houses, a mess hall, and also a frequent number of cargo drops. It doesn't stay this way for long though, soon the raiders come.
The Mother and Son decide to bare arms in their fight against their enemy the Cutlass Pirates, and this time, they only send one, a scout with a club. The mother and son rush in, sort of barbaric style, not really knowing what they are doing, because neither of them have fought on such a small scale. The Pirate puts a good beating on the son, but the duo wins in the end. The three decide that this isn't going to be the last time that this happens, so they build a small hospital. The Son decides that this would be a good idea, to name the settlement, to get everyone's hopes up, so they choose the name HomeLand.
A day or so after their first fight, an old man comes into sight of HomeLand. This man was a mute in his childhood, and was a stay-at-home father in his later years, and without too much success in his life, he was a pessimist. The group decided to let him in anyway though, on account of him being an excellent cook. He always was finding himself in a daze, or sometimes just plain confused, and not able to cook for the group, which led to some minor food shortages. As this would happen, HomeLand would still get raided once and a while, but only two pirates would come at a time. The duo found that the best way to deal with them was by building sandbags to use as cover while in the middle of a firefight.
Just after their third firefight though, something strange happened, an escape pod dropped from the sky. The Son decides to take the best rifle and go check the escape pod to see if there are any survivors, and sure enough, there is a former sex slave busted up and injured in the front. So the Son drags her back to the camp and into the Hospital, and they heal her up right away. Meanwhile the duo build a room for them to lock her in to while they persuade her to join them. No one could persuade her though, so they unlocked her door then kicked her out.
Just as they lock her in though, a young woman comes by, who was a former politician, seeking shelter from a group of Cutlass Pirates who are right on her tail. The group decides to let her in on account of negotiation skills, as the Mother and Son teach the old man, and the Politician how to fight. Just as the Four of them get behind the cover of the sandbags, four Pirates come over the horizon. The battle that ensues is an epic one, bullets are flying, people are shouting, and bodies are dropping. One of the enemy Pirates was smart enough to flank us and catches the Politician with a bullet and she goes into shock. The Doctor runs up quickly during the firefight to drag the Politician to safety as the Son covers her killing the Pirate that flanked them. The Mother than is able to hit and kill another Pirate that was trying to hide behind a rock, and after that the other two started to flee, and HomeLand showed them mercy.
The Politician was taken care of and became part of HomeLand and there was a party thrown in the honor of the battle that was won. The Old man as per normal ran the entire settlement out of all of it's food, and without any animals left to hunt, the group of five was left to a dire decision. With all of the fresh bodies around them from the battle of that day and the day before, the decided that cannibalism was the only way that they could survive. This took the biggest toll on the group, more than the hunger itself. Everyone fell into a deep depression.
The Old Man was the first to go insane, he went berserk and started to wave his pistol around. He shot the Doctor and the Mother in the Legs, and the son shot him right in the skull after that. The Son and the Politician dragged the two to the infirmary, where they performed makeshift surgery, as they ran out of medical supplies long before that. The Doctor pulled through quite quickly, but it wasn't looking so good for the mother. The Son fell into a darker depression than ever and went to the west mountains and went beserk. The rage of probably losing his mother overcame him and he went into a bloodlust. The Politician had fallen in love with the Son within the past couple of days since the party, so she tried to persuade him to come back, but the second he saw a figure coming up the mountain he gunned her down and immediately felt the weight and regret of what he had done.
He thought that he would go and put an end to the Doctor's life as his mother was probably already dead, but has he reached the tunnel that leads to HomeLand, he saw his mother standing there, and a calm immediately fell over him. His mother was alive... but as the two returned to the village, they saw the Doctor's body lying on the sickbed in the Hospital. She died from a stomach virus that they all overlooked.

As the two finished burying their friend from the beginning they heard gunshots. A group of three raiders was just past the town limits, and they were all armed to the teeth. The Mother and Son decided that they would give their Settlement, their Livelihood, their - HomeLand, one final fight. The two rushed in guns blazing, the first Pirate immediately shot the Son in the chest and he went down. The Mother emptied a magazine into that guy and he went down. She reloaded and than got halfway through another into the second Pirate before the third Pirate shot her in the chest as well, both of them were down. The two remaining Pirates left the two there to bleed out slowly as they burned their HomeLand. The last thing both of them saw, was everything they built up, burning to the ground.

Never have I Played a game that is actually so incredibly fun to fail at. The story this game delivers is different and interesting every single time. Let me give you a run down on my first playthrough experience.
We begin with Nakamura, a Herbalist by trade. Alcoroux, an artist. And finally Andrei, a defector. They exit their escape pods and begins our journey. We gather, we hunt, we build we prosper, one day a newbie arrives to join us, Cody welcome to Pine Views my friend. Over the next while we have many vistiors we trade and expand and try to give our humble aboad more comfort and defenses too, we fight off many raiders and some even join us. Andrei's dog dies, and she is heart broken. but continues on, next day the raiders come again, this time stronger than before! we take many hits and one of our new members is down, the raiders take him! Cody tries to stop them but gets his leg blown clean off. We never saw our kidnapped friend again, presumably he was eaten or sold into slavery. Nakamura makes a peg leg for Cody, life isn't the same but he keeps going. All are sad about our lost comrade, but Pine Views fights on. Days and days go by until one day raiders decide to lay siege! they begin setting up a mortar and sandbagging the area. What do we do?? most of the buildings are still wooden, we won't stand a chance against a mortar attack! we must act. Immediately our 3 best shooters (also our original colonists) , Nakamura, Andrei and Alcoroux launch an assault! 3 v 7 at least, but with tactical strategy we pulled it off! we killed 4 and the rest retreated! victory!, we returned to rest and heal to come back and take the mortar and supplies for our own base! oo what is this? grenades! excellent take them aswell!. The stress has built up and Nakamura has a mental break! dropped his sniper rifle and wandered aimlessly for a day. But returned home, we set up our Mortar on the North side and equip the new weapons. Unable to find Nakamura's sniper rifle I give him the grenades. We are a stronghold to be reckoned with! Our only prisoner escapes amongst the chaos but we track her down and drag her back to the compound. I feel accomplished, like at us now, Pine Views has faced lose but come so far, life is good. Until.. the raiders come back in full force!! Armed to the teeth they begin their assault on the south, wait.. the south? but the mortars on the north side!!! It won't reach them!! too late they are at our door and the chaos begins the group splits up and attacks from multiple sides! Cody attacks a lone raider with his mace and takes him down but is shot from the side! Another raider blows a hole in the side of the bunker with what looked like a rocket launcher, Andrei fires on him but he falls back a bit, another runs at Andrei and attacks her melee style!, Nakamura comes to the rescue! armed with.... THE GRENADES!!! he lobs one at her attacker and they're both down in the explosion, Alcoroux panics and runs inside, the raiders make it to the north of the base, nows our chance they're in range quick Nakamura to the mortar!! He's too late, they're there, again he throws a grenade! hurting one but not killing, so he throws another! and kills him but destroying our mortar at the same time!. 2 of the raiders open fire on Nakamura and kill him and another takes Cody and runs! all are dead but Alcoroux and the prisoner still in our cell. Alcoroux gives chase to rescue Cody but is too late, they're gone. Badly wounded and bleeding out severely and infected he returns to his bed to rest, he is the only one left, no one to give him treatment. Unable to feed himself he suffers in extreme pain for a day and then snaps and goes bezerk, he runs outside with his gun in hand, but theres no one left to kill? just the prisoner who has also got a muscle parasite infection now and no one to treat her. Alcoroux wonders around looking for something to hurt, something to kill. He finds a Turkey, he opens fire and the Turkey attacks back!! he eventually kills it but not before it wounds him even further and he is now bleeding out more than before, still enraged he wonders a bit more before falling into a heap where he laid for hours, no one to help him. The last colonist of Pine Views, fallen amongst his dead comrades, bleeds out on the ground and dies. Pine Views is no more.
Honestly, one of the most fun, roller coaster rides of a game ever!!. I failed, I lost, but it was so much fun doing it!. The concept of this game is amazing, it's a sim style game with a Prison Arhitect style of building and design. But, really, you're managing the colony but not controlling it completely. The colonists all have different backgrounds, relationships, skills and interact with each other differently. And the AI chooses scenarios to hit you with to both challenge you and your colonists, but also give you and exciting and interesting story. You don't know what will happen next!
The game is early access, but well developed currently with a great modding community by the looks too. The developer seems hard at work and have seen multiple bug fixes day after day. The price is quite high, but I decided to buy it anyway and give it a shot. And I don't regret it!!. If this story of my playthrough sounded funny/interesting then you won't regret it either

The Talos Principle. A philosophical science fiction puzzle game made by the developers of Serious Sam. I really like it.
The game looks so beautiful and it runs pretty darn well. I have RX 480 and i7 2600k and I've set everything to the max, solid 60FPS or even 144FPS if I had that kind of monitor. It also probably has the largest amount of graphics and physics settings of all games I've ever played and I've played a lot of games. You can change everything from transparency anti-aliasing to ambient occulsion precision.
Gameplay. The character movement is superb. It's like in Source games (eg. CS:GO), moving the camera with mouse is presice as laser beam and walking and strafing around with WASD just feels so good.
And then two main points in the whole game and in this review.
Firstly. Puzzles, they are excellent like in Portal 2 and in its modification, Portal Stories: Mel. At first, they are pretty easy but still fun to do. Things will get slowly harder and harder, but don't get me wrong, hard =/= frustrating, it's still fun! As you progress you will unlock new puzzle tools and a lot more complex puzzles in different locations all around the world.
Secondly, its story. Like I said, it's a
puzzle game. I don't want to spoil too much but the game makes you think more about artificial intelligence in general, faith, the meaning of life and yourself. At first you probably just think that you are in some kind of a heaven (or hell?) where some god speaks to you and is about to give you an eternal life if you can prove your faith to him and bla bla. But it's so much more than that. When you advance, you'll start to find pieces of information about the past, other people and things that have happened. Maybe it's not heaven after all, it's something much much worse (or better). But let's not spoil too much. Just buy it and start playing. You will get hooked, you can't stop playing.
Oh, and did I already mention that there are absolutely no loading times anywhere!
tl;dr One of the best puzzle games I've ever played. It's like Portal 2 (and Portal Stories: Mel). A really really good puzzle game with strong story and it's well ♥♥♥♥ing optimized. There's a free demo too!

I'll just put it bluntly, this is my favorite shooter of all time. The first 2 Max Paynes are good but this one takes the cake. I have so much fun everytime I decide to play the campaign. The physics engine makes every gunfight fun as heck and makes each kill extremely satisfying. This is the best incarnation of bullet time I've seen in a game, coming from the series that coined the term in gaming. The story has dark themes of greed and betrayal all over, and while debateably the weakest plot of the series, it is still a great story. However, the characterization of Max is the best thing about the game. His inner monologue is grimly intriguing and is extremely well written. You really do feel for him as you get a sense of his age through the controls and the video feed back effects representing the culmination of drugs and alcohol in his system. The only complaints I really have are that the cutscenes really should be skippable, but for me it's a minor complaint for an incredible game. This game has also aged very well for being 5 almost 6 years old now. Sadly, the multiplayer is pretty much dead but it was really fun while it lasted. One of my all time favorites and a game I will definitely reccomend. Now if only Rockstar would make fourth Max Payne...
(Oh yeah, the soundtrack is also really, really good. Health did a fantastic job with the score.)

I have spent more time playing Wolfenstein 3D than some of you have been alive.  I've played Spear of Destiny and Return to Castle Wolfenstein and I've enjoyed them all.  Why then am I unable to recommend this game?  One word: checkpoints.
Others have complained about the linear nature of the game.  While I won't go so far as to say that it's on rails, it definitely controls where you will go and what you will see.  There is little sense of exploration in this game, but that is not the reason for my negative feeling toward it.  The story is entertaining and the AI is sufficiently challenging.  However, the developer's insistence upon using checkpoints in a PC game is inexcusable.  This game is obviously designed for the console market first and the PC market second.
Several times I have attempted to poke around and check things out, only to click on something that I did not realize was a transitional trigger resulting in my leaving the map altogether, completely unable to return (no, you CANNOT load old check points).  That is pathetic.  Considering the noble pedigree of this series, this is a sad, sad state of affairs and for this reason I cannot recommend it to others.

In all honesty, while I do not like the Pay to Win aspect of Vehicles, and I do wish that you could earn Certs faster, it is honestly not a bad game as long as you have a decent setup in terms of hardware, your wits about you and you're not participating in big battles. (If you are, you can still fight, just try to avoid the main combat, it's literally a no-mans land situation. World War One all over again)
Just keep your wits about you, check your surroundings and practice snap shooting.
What's really important is that you know to run to cover the second you come under fire, it increases your chances of survival and gives you more time to plan out your next move.
And MOST IMPORTANTLY, unless you have decent backup, don't pick a fight you know you wont win. If you encounter someone who has better equipment or is in their niche (IE, if they're good at flying and in a fighter), either get out of their sight and/or relocate, there are other fights that will end better for you.
And please, don't listen to those naysayers who say that Planetside 2 is pay to win. Just follow my advice, which came from personal experience, and trust me, you will be able to hold your own against P2W players.

This game is slowly dying and losing its player base. Sadly, there are a lot of good reasons this is happening: lack of support from daybreak, a flawed cert system, and ridiculous vehicles.
The vehicles in this game are too numerous and are clearly pay to win. Its really bad game design to give starter players no way to take down air units. (since I first posted this review the light assault has been given an AA gun, it takes 11 hits to kill an ESF, 25 to kill a valk, 25 to kill a lib, 84 to kill a galaxy; not good but a step in the right direction) A sunderer takes 5-6 rockets from the starter missile launcher, that's literally all the ammo you can carry, meanwhile you have to hope you aren't going to die or that someone isn't repair the sunderer.
On top of all this there isn't an inherent vehicle limit in the game like other FPS games which spawn only a set number of vehicles in each side. Literally everyone can spawn a vehicle or a max suit. Sure, the vehicles cost nanites but nanites regenerate so quickly that you can basically chain pull Maxes and vehicles as long as you aren't suicidal with them. This leads to prolonged stalemates until one side gets a big zerg.
You might be tempted as a new play to use your own vehicles to beat their vehicles but paid/unlocked weapons for vehicles are almost all so much better than the stock weapons. Newer players be warned, I can't even begin to describe the joke that is watching an unupgraded lightning try to kill any other vehicle with unlocks. It might have changed but I almost ran out ammo trying to kill a sunderer using the basic lightning and it wasnt even being repaired. Maxes are similar. Its pretty much universally agreed that maxes should specialize, not just be mediocre at two things but guess what you get on the stock max? Two guns good for two different things.
Infantry weapons are actually okay since stock weapons are generally the best all rounder weapons. Still, almost all fights involve a vehicle presence, the exception are bio labs fights but those are usually campfests and explosive spam, not exactly great infantry combat. If you can get past all that, guess what the main method for taking bio labs is? Maxes... great the infantry-vehicle hybrid. If you somehow find a good infantry fight wihtout a bunch of vehicles or maxs you are still subject to all sorts of mandatory upgrades like heavy assault shield and nanoweave armor. The general consensus is that its only 2-3 shots difference but thats a significant difference in TTK. Older players already have the advantage of general skill, gunplay, and map knowledge. Why do they also need to be able to tank 2-3 extra shots?
People get really upset when you mention pay2win since you can technically grind forever and not spend a dime. I mean that's technically true but at a certain point the grind is so high that it is essentially pay2win. 130  in game hours in at BR50, I still haven't gotten  enough certs for even half the "standard" upgrades.
Let's add up the upgrades people generally expect you to have when you play a class. (amounts are approximate) If you don't have these unlocks then you are basically not able to fill an expected role for that class.
HEAVY ASSAULT:
~1000 - Ground to air launcher for heavy
~1000 - shield upgrade for heavy
~1000 - nanoweave armor
~300 - foregrip, scope, etc...
MEDIC:
~1000 - medic tool upgrade
~500 - revive grenade
~500 - grenade belt
~1000 - utility upgrades
ENGINEER:
~1000 - engineering tool upgrade
~1000 - anti vehicle turret for engineer
~1000 - spitfire turret
~300 - vehicle mines
~300 - foregrip, scope, etc...
MAX:
~1000 - anti infantry weapon unlock for max
~1000 - anti vehicle weapon unlock for max
~1000 - anti air weapon unlock for max
INFILTRATOR:
~1000 - bolt action rifle for non-NC infiltrator
~1000 - SMG for infiltrator
~500 - cloak upgrade
~200 - straight pull bolt, scope, etc...
LIGHTNING
~1000 - lightning non-standard weapon (2000 if you want both AP and HE)
~1000 - lightning armor
~750 - utility
MBT
~2000 - MBT tank AP and HE
~1000 - heavy tank ability
~1000 - heavy tank armor
SUNDERER
~2000 - repair sunderer
~200 - ammo sunderer
~2000 - stealth
This doesn't include light assault and the other 10+ vehicles in the game. It also assumes you dont get many new weapons. A lot of people will argue that you don't really need some of these upgrades but it really limiting if you do.
No C4? You HAVE to play heavy assault to deal with vehicles and a sunderer can absorb literally every single rocket you are carrying and still live.
No AP round? Good luck killing an enemy tank with the C75.
No bolt action rifle? Well, the enemy sniper can one shot you with a headshot, you can't.
No dual weapons for max? I hope you like being mediocre at two things.
Low level repair sunderer? Well, you can field repair but your tank is going to lose against the tank with the max repair bus near it.
An argument can be made that you can focus on one class at a time an can get most of the necessary upgrades with your starter certs. This is true but that means you really only get to play one class effectively. Its weird to here someone say that you should focus on one class at a time then later chastise you for not using another class to counter what the enemy is doing. If multiple different classes and vehicles are needed to counter each other then you really can't just focus on unlocking one class at a time.
The grind gets a lot slower after you no longer get your beginner certs and if your initial unlocks were bad you're probably better off starting over. They claim you can refund your certs at BR15 but thats only for certain unlocks. I got to BR50 on my main character but haven't even unlocked more than 1/5 of the stuff in the list above. Some of the stuff isn't unlocked with daybreak cash but the weapons can be bought so that leaves more certs for the things you can't straight up buy.
Another issue with this game is generally bugginess and the need for client side hit detection. Client side hit detection is a necessary evil for a game of this scale but this leaves lots of room for hackers to abuse and for laggy wtf deaths. You thought you were in cover? Well that guy with high ping had you standing out in the open on his computer. There was a rampant bug where players were editing the hitboxes on enemies and it took almost a year for daybreak to fix it. Bugs in the game are numerous, the most notable one on the date of this review is the random flipping of cores. This basically can result in random 5 victory point swings. Since you need 20 to take a continent this is anything but minor.
This game could have been great but the unlock system makes newer players have an even bigger disadvantage than they normally would and the grind is insanely high. In battlefield I got almost all of the necessary unlocks within 40-50 hours of gamplay. 200 hours into planetside 2 and I still don't have the max upgrades, sunderer upgrades, MBT upgrades, and I have unlocked 1 gun, an upgrade for the lightning tank. Clientside hit detection, lag, and daybreak's generally lack of support lead to many frustrating situations. The vehicle system is filled with pay to win weapons and it is fairly easy for players to chain pull vehicles if they aren't suicidal with them. On my own account my K/D jumps from 1.8 to 5.8 when I'm in a vehicle and just with an upgraded lightning, I haven't even started with aircraft.
If you do try this game be sure to do it with friends or try to join a decent platoon. If you decide to lone wolf try to avoid directly fighting vehicles and aircraft as much as possible whether you're on foot or in your own vehicle, you're just going to lose unless the other player is also new. This game is slowly but surely losing its player base and it will continue to dwindle unless daybreak gives it some much needed support.

This game is the first one I've ever played that made me want to rage quit before I'd reached the start menu. An unskippable useless cutsceen plays the first time you load up that drags on and on and on and gives you no useful or interesting character information. I was so angry when I finally reached the menu that they had forced me to watch it that I quit and it took me months to even come back and try opening the game again.
Once I did, I was sorely disappointed.
I loved the first two Max Payne games. I've replayed them multiple times and loved the noir story and the ridiculous bullet time action that lets you dive into a room and see how many bad guys you can kill before you hit the ground. Truly something I find just fun.
In Max Payne 3 as I started trying to pull off my favorite moves I realized that my aiming reticle is snapping to a grid instead of smooth scroll around the screen which at times makes head shots impossible as it is litterally bouncing from one side to the other of the enemies head. They clearly made little effort in this console port to PC. Then there are the "events" that railroad you to take certain moves like pointlessly and dangerously breaking through a window and sliding down a roof towards a host of bad guys. No choices or tactics possible, oh and you have make a tricky shot before you reach the bottom or you lose, and by the way the reticle problem, makes the shot frustratingly difficult.
Now guess what you failed. If there was any sort of cinematic cut scene before you died you now get to watch the ENTIRE THING without being able to skip it. Oh and some of those cut scenes are minutes long and drop you straight into a firefight. What you died again? LET'S WATCH THE WHOLE POINTLESS CUTSCENE AGAIN! Becuase why would you want to start over at the end of the cutscene when the action starts instead of watching 2 minutes of pointless drivel?
I wanted to like this game, badly. I even persevered through everything I wrote above to make sure I was giving it a fair shake but after several levels I was exhausted of fighting the poor interface, poor cut scenes, uninteresting game play, poor graphics compared to what a PC can handle, and the crushing disappointment of seeing how horrifically bad the series had been mangled.
Do not buy this game. Do not play this game even if someone gave it to you for free. Save yourself, go find a good game, or even a decent one to spend your time on.

Client side hit detection is a necessary evil for a game of this scale but this leaves lots of room for hackers to abuse and for laggy wtf deaths. You thought you were in cover? Well that guy with high ping had you standing out in the open on his computer. There was a rampant bug where players were editing the hitboxes on enemies and it took almost a year for daybreak to fix it. Bugs in the game are numerous, the most notable one on the date of this review is the random flipping of cores. This basically can result in random 5 victory point swings. Since you need 20 to take a continent this is anything but minor.
This game could have been great but the unlock system makes newer players have an even bigger disadvantage than they normally would and the grind is insanely high. In battlefield I got almost all of the necessary unlocks within 40-50 hours of gamplay. 200 hours into planetside 2 and I still don't have the max upgrades, sunderer upgrades, MBT upgrades, and I have unlocked 1 gun, an upgrade for the lightning tank. Clientside hit detection, lag, and daybreak's generally lack of support lead to many frustrating situations. The vehicle system is filled with pay to win weapons and it is fairly easy for players to chain pull vehicles if they aren't suicidal with them. On my own account my K/D jumps from 1.8 to 5.8 when I'm in a vehicle and just with an upgraded lightning, I haven't even started with aircraft.
If you do try this game be sure to do it with friends or try to join a decent platoon. If you decide to lone wolf try to avoid directly fighting vehicles and aircraft as much as possible whether you're on foot or in your own vehicle, you're just going to lose unless the other player is also new. This game is slowly but surely losing its player base and it will continue to dwindle unless daybreak gives it some much needed support.

After spending about 30 hours playing the game so far (with no end currently in sight), I have to say I am very pleased with my overall experience. At first I was very undecided whether I should purchase the game seeing as it's still in alpha, but am I ever glad I decided to make the purchase. It feels like a very full game with tremendous possibilities. I have not personally encountered any noticable bugs or crashes that MANY of us are familiar experiencing with alpha titles
Essentially you start off as either a trio who has crashlanded, a lone survivor, or a simple tribe of 5 people (Custom scenarios are also available) and you try to survive by building a colony. It's that simple. That being said, simple doesnt mean easy.. EVERYTHING will try to stop you.. whether it is a gang of raiders, pirates, a mad rat, an injured boomalope that was WAY too close to your base, starvation, hypothermia, heatstoke, mental illness.. basically anything and everything. Build your base and try to outsmart those pirates.
There are a few modes represented by "narrators". These "narrators" pick which events will happen, at a certain rate and pattern. The game will be different depending on which narrator you choose. Cassandra Classic has a traditional, linear experience where pirate raids and events happen slowly at first, but eventually amount to massive, difficult raids as the game goes on. Phobe Chillax is an easier experience where there is much more time in between raids and is a "friendlier" gaming experience at low difficulties. Finally.. Randy Random.. Ah.. Good Ol' Randy. If you want a little spice/excitement in your game, pick Randy. You never know whats gonna happen when you pick Randy. I felt Randy's wrath once. Randy decided a raid of pirates consisting of 5 members equipped with shotguns and rifles was an EXCELLENT idea 20 minutes into my lone survivor colony. Buck died a quick death... F*ckin Randy.
This game is very similar to Dwarf Fortress in many regards and and you will feel the sting of the slight learning curve if you go into this game without any DF or similar experience, but after watching a quill18 video or two, the rest will should come easily enough. Don't get discouraged if your colony gets destroyed.. I've never had a colony last more than 6 hours (I do not claim to be an expert gamer though). Guys this game has a lot of depth, I'm currently at ~30 hours of gameplay and I'm usually learning a thing or two at every game session.
Now. There ARE some small things that make me scratch my head from time to time. For example, If you have a pet and he is bonded to a person and there is a pirate raid, your pet will actually follow you into battle and will be shot... almost guarenteed, but these are little things and Tynan (Game Dev.) actively listens to fans and constantly implements updates. He does not plan very far ahead into the future in terms of the games development (which I find is good.. Lower chances of getting carried away) and plans on staying focued on the colony/sim experience.
I STRONGLY recommend this game for any fans of  strategy/base-building/survival genres. (extreme bonus if you like all those genres) Sorry If my review wasn't the greatest.. I don't write many of them but thought this game really deserved one.
Pay full price. Support Tynan. I would personally buy the Pirate King pack to support Tynan if I could afford it (Yes, I would actually be willing to drop $250.00 to play this game, now knowing how good it is). He has done an AMAZING job. You will not regret it.

If you liked the base-building of "Prison Architect", but wanted to be a castaway survivor in a frontier planet fighting beasts, gangs of pirates and the very elements themselves, this is the game for you. They say it reminds one of Firefly, and that's not far off the mark. I've gone days with nothing troubling happening, and then suddenly your power blows, and a rabid turtle attacks and kills a wandering boomrat and now you're trying to stop a wildfire that's sweeping through your pastures, threatening your fields and you're trying desperately to get your crops in while praying for rain.
An example of how things can suddenly go off-kilter. Playing as "Winter" Steel, we were minding our own business, with the colony struggling to hunt and get our first crops in for the season. Suddenly a pirate raid hit from the Fire Whips, but it turns out their leader is Winter's father, Jake. We fought and won, but Winter, their best hunter and doctor, was knocked unconcious during the fight. She gets taken to her room to recover, but her father is captured, and barely holds onto life for a day, before his wounds kill him. The secondary cook, as it turns out, had some experience in cannibalism, so ate most of Jake raw, made meat pies out of the rest, and fed them to Winter, while she recovered. When she was mobile again, she had not just eaten and killed her father, but now had to live down the stigma of not having a grave to bury him in.
Winter went a little insane. She wandered around in the rain unconsolably for a couple days, her friends trying to keep the place together wihtout their best hunter and planter. She dropped her rifle somewhere (where a passing pirate stole it, I assume), and then stripped naked and stood in the rain in the back pastures, until she finally got back off her knees, got dressed again and began lending a hand. But she spent a lot of time in the graveyard, looking at all the pirates she had killed over the last few seasons, and her wandering made her sick with an infection. She wandered off on another hunting trip, when a rampaging man-hunting rhinocerous gored her, before being put down by the perimeter sentry guns.
Once more sick and dying of an infection, her friends tried to console her, and nurse her through the sickness, but there was no medicne, and WInter was their best doctor. She mostly recovered, but as a fragile shell of herself, wandering through her days, doing what was needed, but never recovered her soul. She spent more and more time in the cemetary, and finally died of a heart attack next to her own granite sarcophogus.
Here lies Winter Steel. Murdering depressed cannabilisitic warrior of the Rimworld frontier. I think she and Alison Reynolds are my two spirit animals.

If you've come looking for a game review, you've come to the wrong place. But if you came here looking for a delicious guide to cooking an amazing home made ravioli, you've come to the right place!
You will need:
to 6-1/2 cups all-purpose flour
6 eggs
3/4 cup water
2 teaspoons olive oil
SAUCE:
1 can (28 ounces) crushed tomatoes
1-1/2 cups tomato puree
1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese
1/3 cup water
1/3 cup tomato paste
3 tablespoons sugar
2 tablespoons minced fresh basil
1 tablespoon minced fresh parsley
1 tablespoon minced fresh oregano
1 garlic clove, minced
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/4 teaspoon pepper
FILLING:
1 carton (15 ounces) ricotta cheese
2 cups (8 ounces) shredded part-skim mozzarella cheese
1/3 cup grated Parmesan cheese
1 egg, lightly beaten
2 teaspoons minced fresh basil
1 teaspoon minced fresh parsley
1 teaspoon minced fresh oregano
1/4 teaspoon garlic powder
1/8 teaspoon salt
1/8 teaspoon pepper
First things first, you'll want to mix your dough and wrap it up tightly in plastic to rest. Meanwhile, you can prepare your filling. You'll want to use about one tablespoon of filling for each ravioli; if you're comfortable eyeballing the amount, you can use a pastry bag (or a ziplock bag with one corner snipped off) since it's a little faster and neater. Otherwise, just grab a measuring spoon and keep it on hand.
Finally, if you don't have a ravioli maker, you should keep a pastry brush and a small bowl of water to seal the dough further down the line. Some people use egg whites instead of water, and if you have extra lying around, that's fine; it's just not necessary. If you do have a ravioli mold, though, then just a rolling pin (or a bottle of wine♥♥♥♥♥rolling pin) will suffice.
Once all your tools are within easy reach, it's time to start rolling that dough. To keep it from drying out, work with just a quarter of your dough at a time, keeping the rest under plastic or a kitchen towel. Roll it out to just thinner than 1/16th of an inch—usually the second-to-last setting on your pasta machine. (You may be tempted to roll it even thinner. Don't—you'll wind up with a less balanced ratio of filling to dough and, after boiling, a far less aesthetically appealing plate.) Ideally, the dough should be almost the full width of the pasta roller, between four and five inches across. Then lay the dough out on a large, flat surface lightly dusted with flour (semolina flour is ideal, since it won't make your dough gummy if it gets moistened, but all-purpose is perfectly fine) and cut it in half. Each quarter of dough will make approximately twelve ravioli.
From here on out, the steps will differ based on whether you're using a ravioli maker or working by hand (if you have a stamp, follow the by-hand directions as well).
If You're Using a Ravioli Maker...
Place the metal base of the ravioli maker in front of you and lay your first sheet of dough on top.
Then, take the plastic mold and gently press down to form depressions in the dough. You want to work relatively quickly, so that your dough doesn't have an opportunity to dry out and become brittle. If you press too hard and the dough tears, simply ball it back up and roll it through the machine again.
Once you have even depressions in the dough, place approximately one tablespoon of filling in each depression. Try to avoid getting filling outside the depression, since the flat perimeter is what our second sheet of dough will adhere to. You can gently wipe away excess with your your finger or a small towel if need be.
Gently rap the mold on the table to help remove any air bubbles.
Next, lay the other half of your sheet of dough over the surface of the mold, pressing with the flat of your hand to push out any extra air. Then take a rolling pin and run it over the surface of the dough until the ridges beneath become visible. At this point, you can flip the mold over and gently peel it away.
If you find that some ravioli are stuck to the mold, try rapping one edge against the table—any remaining pasta should come loose. At this point, you can place the ravioli on a sheet tray, wrap it in plastic and freeze it for later use. Otherwise, if the dough is sufficiently perforated to pull apart, go ahead and do so. It's possible, though, that you'll need to use a ravioli cutter to slice them into individual pieces.
Cover your ravioli with a towel to keep them from drying out and repeat with your remaining pieces of dough.
If You're Working by Hand...
Again, you should have one quarter of your dough rolled out and cut in half, so that you have two pieces of dough roughly 15 inches long and five inches across. Cover one sheet with a towel to keep it from drying out.
Fold the first sheet along its midline to make a light crease and then re-open it. Working so that your filling is approximately one-and-a-half inches in diameter and half an inch apart, place six even heaping tablespoons along the lower half of the dough. (Note that the photos below picture smaller amounts of filling spaced more widely apart than the instructions indicate. You're actually going for something that looks more like the spacing on the mold, pictured in the previous section.)
Moisten the dough lightly with your water and pastry brush...
And then fold it over along the crease, pressing from the folded point outward to remove excess air.
Gently pat the dough down around each lump of filling to create a seal.
And finally, use the fluted side of the ravioli cutter or a stamp to slice your ravioli into even squares.
Cooking Your Ravioli
Now, all that remains is tossing your ravioli into a pot of water at a low boil, and cooking for approximately three minutes, or until slicing into one reveals no starchy line in the center.
Serve your ravioli in the sauce of your choice—I personally find that a great filling often requires little more than a drizzle of olive oil and perhaps some chopped herbs. Tahdah!

Fast paced, arcadey shooter with a surprisingly poignant campaign.
Wolfenstein The New Order plays as well as you expect, it is a fast paced, balls to the wall run and gun shooter. You can opt to use stealth in certain situations but for the most part the pacing is incredibly fast, and gameplay wise it is good without any surprises.
The real draw and surprise was the story, which actually packs quite a punch. The characters are colorful but brought to life with strong voiceacting and animations, and give real weight to the campaign. The game doesnt shy away from Nazi brutality, and gives you a lot of motivation to want to gun down your enemies. There is also some really terrific writing in terms of the dialogue, particularly from Blazkowicz who has some truly dark and poetic monologues.
Overall, while the run and gun nature isnt usually my style, you can play the game however you choose, and the strong story makes this one of the better FPS campaigns in recent memory.

Basically, Talos Principle is a first-person puzzle chamber game in the tradition of Portal. There have been a lot of puzzle chamber games since Portal, but it has been incredibly frustrating how many of those games just want to copycat portal. The Talos Principle is the breath of fresh air you've been waiting for in the genre, though, since it is a first person puzzle chamber game with completely original puzzle mechanics and a completely original concept. The only real overlaps with Portal is that it's sci-fi, there are robots, and sometimes you have to put a cube on a button.
The vast majority of the puzzles in TTP are laser-connecting puzzles, where you have to move/place connector nodes to guide different color lasers from an origin point, around corners, through windows, etc, to a receptor. You can also split lasers into multiple beams at each connector node. There are certain restrictions, such as being limited to one color laser passing through a connector at a time and---most importantly---laser beams cannot ever cross, regardless of color, as they will disrupt each other. This is where the game being in three dimensions comes into play, since you can place the connectors at different elevations to prevent your lasers from crossing or to connect a laser beam over a wall.
You will of course have all sorts of other toys to play with, such as jammers (placable objects that can jam a single electronic device in play), fans (blow things around), duplicators (create a clone of yourself to help yourself co-op a solution), and many more.
The individual puzzle chambers in TTP are very satisfying in and of themselves, but true hardcore puzzle enthusiasts will be even more gratified in hunting down the game's secret stars. These are "secret" objectives in the game that often require you to think far outside the box. These puzzles encourage you to experiment with the mechanics in the game in a way that "games the system", so to speak, such as finding a way to get on top of a wall you were not "supposed" to get on top of, or finding a way to direct a laser beam from puzzle chamber #1 over a wall, through the hub, and into puzzle chamber #3 where it was never "supposed" to go, etc. The stars require a lot of patience, a keen eye for detail, and some thinking outside the box.
That being said, I was rather unsatisfied with two (and only two) of the star puzzles. There is at least one star puzzle that you will not be able to solve unless you have a phone that can read QR codes. I really dislike when games do this (it was a terrible idea in FEZ as well, but FEZ at least provided an alternate route, whereas TTP does not), and I could write an essay on the reasons it's an awful idea, but I'll spare you the bloviating here. The other star was the Sphinx riddle, which I didn't like because A) It takes vagueness to a whole new level, and B) The solution takes some special exceptions to the game rules the player has otherwise learned. Both of the aforementioned stars also cannot even be SEEN by the player, as they are hidden behind secret doors, so you can waste loads of time just running around pointlessly trying to figure out where they even ARE. (And not finding them, of course). Every other star in the game, however, is very visible to an observant explorer, and can be obtained with clever use of the normal game rules you have learned.
Another thing games in this genre often try to copycat is GlaDOS. Thankfully, TTP doesn't copycat here either. Instead you have Elohim, who is this really arrogant and sanctimonious dckhead that talks about how brilliant he is all the time. I turned down the voice volume to zero just because I couldn't stand him talking all the time. HOWEVER. The writing in the game is actually pretty good. You can interact with the story by reading the texts available at the computer terminals (some of which are in obvious places, some of which are hidden away in remote places). Some of the terminals also involve chats where you are asked questions. The whole point of the underlying story and these texts is that you are physically a robot but are trying to determine who you are, why you exist, why you are here. More importantly, you are trying do determine whether or not you are human, what it means to be human, why it even matters whether or not you're human, what the point of being human would be, and so on.
These "chats" you have are basically Socratic dialogues in the most literal sense. It is exactly the sort of annoying thing people used to hate Socrates for---i.e. asking you one question after another in a deliberate attempt to show you that you don't know what you're talking about. Your computerized interlocutor will present you with a philosophical question like one of those described above and then give you some multiple choice answers. This can be frustrating because it's just not good philosophy to limit the possible answers from your interlocutor this way. This is a method of "poisoning the well" as they say. BUT, while I found this frustrating at first, it turns out that the game is aware of this, is doing it intentionally, and it is somewhat plot related. There are also options available to dodge these poisoned wells and other argumentative traps for players more well-versed in philosophy and/or argument.
All in all, TTP is an extremely satisfying game that I find it very hard to say anything negative about. I give it the highest possible recommendation. Using my own scale below, I give TTP a hearty seven.
6) A good game that is worth the full price.
5) A pretty good game worth checking out--especially if discounted.
4) A fairly good game, but I'd recommend buying it discounted.
3) Not great, but a few redeeming qualities. Only buy if heavily discounted.
2) Only worth checking out if you are dangerously curious.
1) Avoid at all costs.

So much stuff done right for such a cheap game!
1. The Good.
- lots of weapons to use, from pistols to chainsaws and tesla guns;
- plenty of buildings from palisades to turrets and mines to place in order to help you survive - and make zombies go boom!
- RPG elements (can pick traits to improve like reload speed, extra health, health regen, etc.)
- resource management - money and ammunition are all important

- multiplayer with still plenty of active people online
- The music - albeit the game has only 2 relatively short music tracks, I love them both. The Main Menu music has that ERA/Enigma vibe, and the combat (level) music is heavy metal kind of the XBlades 1 type.
2. The Bad.
- repetitive
- only 1 map
- only 2 music tracks
The Conclusion:
An amazingly good game for 49 cents in my opinion, perfect to fool around with to relax and break the everyday tedium, or as a nice filler between your crazy good AAA games. Even if you're a huge cheapskate and think that 49 cents is still money, deduct 24-30 cents from the steam trading cards that you will sell and you get a perfectly fine SP/MP experience for just 19 cents. That's cheaper than a chewing gum, for God's sake. Get this game, have some fun, and maybe come play online with the others as well!

Another Day in Rimworld.
Explosion rocks the colony compound walls as a conduit wire short circuits, starting a small fire. Emmie wakes up from the shockwave to beat the flames out, only to greet a berserking John by receiving a swift knee to the face, destroying her nose. The local militia rouses from the screams, trying to shuffle off the dizzying effects of moderate exposure to toxic fallout, and rushes across the compound to Emmie's aid. John kicks a door open, Emmie shrieking the garbled rimworld dialect equivalent of "kick his teeth out" before she passes out from shock. John gets no such warm treatment: the militia open fire with their pistols and survival rifles and shred the disgruntled colonist's arms, torso, and eyes.
John's dead. Five colonists left.
Emmie's engulfed in flames as the fire reaches the blades of leaves from nearby strawberry bushes, and quickly spread across the entirety of the wooden wall. Her last reactions were mixed anguish and unbridled rage, claiming that she'd be back again, as her psychosis takes her to the void. The flames take her to ashes, though, so fat chance on that.
Night falls as the militia, having recently drafted a researcher who can't stop his hands from shaking as he grips his rifle, scrambles to beat the flames out. Batteries only stored enough energy to power one turret for 30 seconds, or the compound's turret gallery for about, let's say, five seconds.
The pirates terrorizing the rimworld decide this is an opportune moment to attack... from afar.
Another Day in Rimworld.

One day an angry monkey attacked my camp and my band of tribespeople had to fight him off, thus injuring the monkey's shoulder. After seeing the monkey in pain and incapacitated, Camblar decided he would help the monkey. A day or so later Camblar names the Monkey Baldy and he becomes the tribe's best friend/mascot.
Time passes and Camblar develops a crush on Trout, a gatherer, and they share their feelings of love as the tribe continues to expand there village. However the tribe failed to plant crops earlier in the year and suddenly the food is running out. As everyone stuggles to survive and find a way to get more food, Camblar is taken ill with some sort of plauge due to malnutrition. For the next few days Camblar can do nothing but rest in bed while the rest of his tribe is scrounging the jungle around them for berries and animals to hunt. Trout tries her best to tend to Camblar, bringing him food and medicine, and Baldy sleeps curled up next to him every night...but he doesn't seem to be improving...
As Trout goes out on an ill-advised hunting mission with her friend Scorpion, the healer, her thoughts still dwell on her love, Camblar. Unfortunately her fragile state leads her to sustain a nasty scratch on her leg from a capybara, and soon after as she lies in a bed next to Camblar, trying to recover, she develops an infection. Things are looking grim and the herbal remidy supplies are running out, so Grey does the only thing he can do and builds a statue with some marble they had cleared away earlier. He creates a fair likeness of Camblar and Trout, symmetrically lying next to eachother in bed. In hopes of raising their spirits he puts the statue right next to their beds.
But hope is not lost! Camblar's condition seems to be improving, as though he has developed an immunity to the plague! As he recovers he starts to do everything he can to help Trout, who is still bedridden; he cleans, he hunts, he builds, and he brings her food every day. And amazingly, Trout begins to recover as well, surving the infection some how and regaining her strength. The tribe can now celebrate at last as the crops are almost ready to harvest, everyone is in good health, and Baldy the monkey helps keep everyone happy.
All is well in the village of Antioch.
[...]
Until there's a heatwave and everyone dies of heatstroke in their beds because they don't know how to swim, except for poor poor Camblar, whoose heat tolerance and non-violence meant he survived long enough to watch all his friends and loved ones die. Finally, depressed and alone (except for Baldy), went out into the jungle and got bitten by a cobra.
A raider comes to the empty village and sets the crops on fire, incapacites Baldy, and leaves.
And then a panther finishes Baldy off and eats him.
And at last, Camblar dies.
The End.
