I decided to buy this game after  looking for a milsim game to replace arma 3.. What a find!
Communication is key in this game. Without a mic expect to die.. It takes a few games to master the basic then even longer to master each different role. Unlike armour 3 where everyone is a bit immature and there are too many lone walves I find most people in this game work together and co-operate.
The squad system in brilliant. You can communicate by radio with your squad or to the leaders of the other squads with a different channel. you can also communicate just with nearby players. Keeping the comms on these levels allows brilliant teeamwork I have not yet experienced in any game. If you have good squad leaders thew game flows amazingly.
Individual roles in the squads are great. I played squad lead on my second day in the game. It is such hard work and you have to be openning the map every few seconds but when you're co-ordinating well and leading your team properly it is so so rewarding. I only got a few kills because i spent so much time co-ordinating, relaying, marking and communicating but i didn't even care. I don't even think I'd have cared if we lost just because if felt so well played anyway. Other roles include medics who are absolutely vital in a good squad (once your medics are down your screwed haha), General infantry (a stroing class that will make up most of a squad), Marksman who will need to take out long range targets, Grenadiers and Automatic riflemen. When you get a term who can work together in these roles it plays so smoothly. in my last game I watched whilst my automatic rifleman draw fire and suppressed and the marksman picked them off.
The Graphics for this game are good, not great, but its alpha. I didn't have any major frame drops playing this game. With most of the settings maxed out I got 75fps (my monitors refresh rate) on an R9 290 and FX-6350. It seems all the AMD issues previously plauging the game are be swiftly corrected. the game can take a while to load but it is nothing major and not a massive time to wait considering a game is a minimum of 30 mins. There are a few in game glitches where soldiers have appeared to be floating and i have on one occasion had a weapon do no damage to an enemy at 5m range. considering the game is still in alpha I am impresserd that these are the only complaints i have with it. I have had not a single freeze or crash.
I would 100% recommend this game to someone wanting a proper team based tactical shooter. You have to work for your kills but in this game you don't care about your kills, all that matters is the next objective. I will be spending many hours playing this! Well worth the money.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is a game about killing as much Nazis as possible. You are a one-man army against an overwhelmingly intimidating Nazi force. I won't spoil any of the story, since the game doesn't have multiplayer and relies on its plot to satisfy, which it does very well.
The game generally gives you 2 ways to approach each situation: Stealth or Mayhem.
STEALTH - Sneak up behind enemies and dispatch them with your combat knife, or pick them off from a distance with your suppressed pistol. You can even throw your knife, accounting for ballistics. Among other methods, this is one way to KILL EVERYONE.
MAYHEM - Whip out BOTH of your assault shotguns and dual-wield them, blasting away and mowing down your foes. Then pull out your assault rifle to cripple them and finally, toss a grenade to blow your enemies to pieces. That's another way to leave a trail of utter destruction wherever you go and KILL EVERYONE.
Apart from the chaotic gameplay, the story truly impressed me and the amount of detail and work that goes into creating this immersive world is flooring.
Very, very highly recommended.

4 years after release the devs still add features and work on improving the game. The game is far away from what they promised us back in the days (intercontinental lattice for example) but it still is the only massive online multiplayer shooter out there. I have looked hard for alternatives but I still haven't found anything quite like it.
Features:
*A persistent game world in a sci-fi-setting - there are no rounds or matches. The fights carry on on a large scale
*Objective driven gameplay - it's mainly about capturing and defending bases
*Fight as infantry, hitch a ride, drive a tank or use aircraft
*The xp based progression system keeps you going for a long time. You can get stuff done right from the start though
*The F2P model is ok - you can get a lot of fun out of the game without spending money
It's free to play. Try it now, spawn into a massive battle, get instakilled and ... "Welcome to Planetside" :-)
Some advice for beginners:
*Check some of WRELs tutorials on Youtube to get you going.
*The game can be a bit intimidating at first. Join an outfit (aka guild) to get into the game quicker. If you ask nicely you will get help! The community is far less toxic than in many other shooters.
*Friendly fire is always on - so you have to make sure you wave that gun in the right direction before pulling the trigger.
*Check the continental map or use "instant action" on a regular basis to see where the fun is happening. The continental maps are huge and there is a lot of landmass without anything happening.
*Try to play a support role (engineer, medic) in the beginning. You can get xp points relatively easy this way

Max Payne. For any gamer who knows their salt, this name should be familiar. His publisher Take Two has released two games in 2001 and 2003 to great reviews and a decent amount of critical acclaim. Since then, though, the ex-cop has been left in the dust, barely being remembered other than that crappy movie that was released around then with Mark Wahlberg. It seemed for a while Max would just fade away, until back in 2012, when Rockstar Games, now owners of Take Two, released Max Payne 3. How was that? Well, we're taking a look at it now.
STORY: You're... Max Payne, of course. After the events of the last two games, Max is a drunken mess, he smokes regularly, he's addicted to painkillers, and he tries to find a reason to not blow his head off daily. Up until one day, when his old friend Passos comes across him and hires him to guard a wealthy family in Sao Paulo, Brazil named the Bronco's. Everything seems fine until the wife of the eldest Bronco is kidnapped, and Max and Passos go on a search to find her. That's all I can really say about it without spoilering it. It's a pretty well put together story. It can be pretty depressing at times when you see Max lose, but when he wins, which is kind of rare, it feels great. That's really all you can ask for. The story is a bit on the short side, took me 10 hours to beat it on Medium, but it's a good experience regardless.
GAMEPLAY: 3rd person shooter. You have 4 slots for guns. You have 2 slots one handed weapons, another for a two handed weapon, and the 4th one is dual wielding the two one handed weapons you have on you. All methods are satisfying enough, and gunplay is fantastic. The innovative Bullet Time from the last few games is here too, and that is great, and it has some new features. If you carry painkillers on you, and you lose all your health, you have a chance to shoot the guy who would have killed you and take him out, getting some health back and putting you back into the fight. Ammo can be a bit scarce, especially on the harder difficulties, but if you're efficient enough, you can do well. The game is freaking hard, btw, even when I played it on Medium, it was hard. The game is really satisfying when you beat the levels, and I ended up replaying it on Hardcore, which made me tear my hair out a bit but it was totally worth it. Gameplay is fantastic, maybe even best of 2012.
GRAPHICS AND PERFORMANCE: Game looks good. The favelas of Sao Paulo look grimy and dirty, the nicer penthouses are well designed. There are a lot of nice details in all the levels without a doubt. This isn't a grand open world game like GTA or Red Dead Redemption or LA Noire like Rockstar is known for making, but the smaller levels are fine. They all look great. Game runs pretty well as well, since it's a game from 2012, if you have any recent hardware you should be fine. Runs well enough on my PC, and if I can run it, you can run it.
CHARACTERS AND VOICE ACTING: Max Payne has his voice actor from the last games, James McCaffery, and goddamn, is he as good as ever. The other characters are voiced well enough too. The characters look good, Max goes through a bit of a redesign halfway through which some people didn't like, but I thought he looked fine. Overall it's fine.
MULTIPLAYER: Practically abandoned on PC, played a bit on my 360, kind of fun, but nothing spectacular, odds are unless you get a big community for it you wont get to play it anyway.
EXTRAS: In each level, there are clues that relate to the story, though you have to look for a few of them. There are also some parts for golden versions of each weapon, and if you get all the parts scattered around the levels, you get a better version of the gun every time you pick it up. Once you beat the game, you unlock Score Attack, which is basically a kill and get points mode. There's also the New York Minute mode, where you have to beat a level in a minute. Well, you get time for killing guys, but still. If you arent impressed by that, then you have New Youk Minute Hardcore mode, in which you have to beat the whole game in a minute with the same bonuses, with no deaths. Yeah... good luck with that.
FINAL VERDICT: Phenominal game. One of the best of 2012, strong competator with Far Cry 3 and Mass Effect 3 for that slot. 9/10, it's worth picking up around a sale, hell, even right now. It's also one of the few games that I keep going back to time and time again to play through it once more, so I have to give some credit to them for that. Grab this game, you won't regret it

It is no secret that the video game market of today has become increasingly catered to the mainstream, action-oriented and rather simple-minded community. With franchises such as Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto and Just Cause celebrating record-breaking releases, we are bearing witness to a market specialization unparalleled in its current form, thanks to the video game industry's global reach. Given the circumstances, it is an utter miracle that a game as marvelous and hauntingly beautiful as The Talos Principle ever even came into existence. In fact, this game was originally supposed to be a continuation of the "Serious Sam" series, Croteam's age-old shooter that is possibly as dumbed-down as it gets. However, in the midst of developing the "intermissions" between each of the sections filled with a senselessly large amount of lead, explosions and mildly entertaining puns, Croteam were experimenting with a few puzzle elements. Designed to let the players cool off inbetween pretending to be Rambo and Duke Nukem, they were supposed to be nothing more than a sidekick, but ended up as much more than that. Sure enough, said puzzling elements resulted in an overwhelmingly positive response amongst the playtesters, captivating their attention for hours on end and essentially causing them to disregard the rest of the game's content. Croteam quickly realized the potential they had on their hands, and started over from scratch with nothing but the goal of creating the best puzzling experience to date in mind. And oh boy, did they deliver.
This unpredictable chain of events was the birth of "The Talos Principle", arguably the single best first-person puzzler ever made, leaving classics like the Portal series in the dust and building on the successes of other puzzlers such as The Swapper and Q.U.B.E. in the process. Armed with tricky puzzle mechanics, a beautiful setting and the sheer brilliant writing of Tom Jubert and Jonas Kyratzes, this game presents the pinnacle of all thoughtful gaming.
But let's start small, shall we? In essence, The Talos Principle consists of two distinguished forms of content: On the one hand, we have the puzzling experience. The player is quickly made familiar with several puzzle mechanics, with another few being introduced as the game progresses, and solves increasingly complicated set-ups throughout the game. As with any puzzle game, these range from the unavoidable one-step-to-solve introductory puzzles that are almost a nuisance to deal with, to the intermediate puzzles that, while a little more complicated, are unable to withstand a proper approach for long, ending with the mind-melting brainbreakers toward the end, which are clearly meant for the more astute among us. But such is not to say that a logical genius is needed to complete the game; While the puzzles make up almost the entirety of the game's playable content, only some are a necessity to complete. The Talos Principle handles the abundance of isolated content nicely, maintaining a proper sense of progression despite the game's free-will approach to what the player does, and what he does not. As such, both newcomers to the puzzling genre as well as established fans will thoroughly enjoy the puzzling experience The Talos Principle offers.
But this puzzling does not come on its own. It is paired with what is possibly the best writing ever to appear in any game, of any genre, of all time. Posing the work of ingenious modern thinkers Tom Jubert and Jonas Kyratzes, Croteam made a decision that turned this game from a nice, but bland, puzzler into an engulfing and elusive experience without comparison in the triple A world, smashing all of the expectations their pre-release sneak peeks had set for myself. And the expectations were sky high, after they had announced the writers behind the indie mega-success "The Swapper" and the ubiquitous flash game "The Infinite Ocean" would be working on this project. Both games deal with a plethora of philosophical thoughts in the neighbourhood of physical reductionism and nihilism, and have successfully approached the average gamer with thought experiments and realizations descended from intellectual behemoths, inspiring shower thoughts and sleepless nights over the most fundamental of questions. And yet, not only does The Talos Principle creatively reinvent what has been chewed through for millennia, it also succeeds in turning abstract philosophical concepts into something all of us can relate to, here and now. The storyline, like so many others, begins with the player being dropped into a world without any knowledge of the why, where, when or how. As more and more fragments of answers emerge, the player slowly uncovers their purpose in the game and is faced with fundamental problems in human thinking, all the while building up to an ultimate choice in which what the player has realized will come to the test. But the game does not just passively offer food for thought, the player is metaphorically pummeled with deep-reaching questions about purpose, existence, morality, qualia, and an innumerable amount of contradictions that you will undoubtedly fall victim to. But once again, one doesn't need to major in philosophy to appreciate the incredible work that has gone into this part of the game. The writing is simultaneously both aimed at the average human as well as the passionate thinkers, and will, without fail, stump even the best of us at times.
All of this would already be a pleasure to play by itself, but Croteam did not let up and perfected every last aspect of the experience they wanted to create. The Talos Principle comes with a beautiful soundtrack composed by musical genius Damjan Mravunac, who appears to possess universal expertise in all corners of sound design and production and has been around in the video game industry for about as long as I have been alive. The tracks perfectly accentuate the setting of the game, adding to the experience in all the right ways without taking away the player's attention from the puzzles or the thinking. Completely lacking percussion, the soundscape of The Talos Principle is incredibly soothing, and manages to hold its own as a standalone product that I find myself listening to again and again.
In short, The Talos Principle provides dozens of hours filled with puzzle-solving, realizations, questions, answers and general intellectual fun accompanied by a hauntingly serene score. The sheer amount of unique puzzles and extras, combined with the multiple layers of thinking that can be found inside the game, warrant not only a second, but even a third or a fourth playthrough of this magnificent beast.
From me, The Talos Principle receives a perfect score. Croteam performed a herculean effort in introducing the puzzling genre to the triple A world, and succeeded marvelously in doing so. The game is an all-around coherent and polished experience that captures your attention from start to finish, and cleverly avoids the one-time-playability many puzzlers and thinking-games tend to suffer from. I recommend the game to anyone who appreciates putting their brain to good use every once in a while, as well as all of the DLC.

Ben, the quiet loner who mines and occasionally sculpts, had a mental break down and attempted to bludgen himself to death because his pet Husky Asphalt died in an angry turtle attack. This is Rimworld.
Sasquach, the pascifist nurse who can build a room like nobody's business, got heat stroke and went a little nuts, shedding her clothes in the living room and running for the hills in the middle of a heat wave. This is Rimworld.
Inga likes to beat people with a stick. This is Rimworld...
Rimworld is a strategy game masked as a top down colony sim with a unique aesthetic and an emergent, complex AI system. Yes, you have to build and manage a base like most sim, sandbox games. However in Rimworld there are complex factors that are super important to the success of your colony.
Stories are generated by "simulating psychology, ecology, gunplay, melee combat, climate, biomes, diplomacy, interpersonal relationships, art, medicine, trade, and more". Key word "and more". Your sims can go insane and it will completely ruin your entire colony when Bert decides to strip and run out into the tundra and pace around in an unresponsive daze! Factions can attack but when taken prisoner can potentially become part of your colony, but only if you have someone with social skills that can chat em up.
This is what makes Rimworld so fun and addictive. I have started over about 6 times, sometimes because of updates but also because I am super curious about how colonies will end up in tundras, or jungles, or if I choose 3 men or 3 women, or 5 tribal members or 1 rich loner. No two stories are ever alike! It's hard to tell that this is even an Early Access game. It could be balanced a bit more, especially in Cassandra Classic mode, however it is very enjoyable.
I would highly recommend this game if you love simulation, strategy, humor, survival aspects, and if you enjoy replayability. 10/10 I'm totally obsessed and can't stop playing. It's summer and I'm always inside playing this game, dammit! Look what you've done to me, Ludeon Studios!!

Ok this is without a doubt the best game I have ever played ever. It's hard to find a game that is great in all aspects, but Croteam really hit the nail on the head with this one. If the graphics weren't convincing enough, the puzzles are amazing and beautifully crafted so that there are many ways to solve them. There's even stars to collect which involve seeing how the puzzles interact with each other to provide a great result. The story and lore is insanely deep and thought provoking, so if you are one who does not enjoy reading, thinking, or even storyline games in general this is not for you. One of the things i loved was that the game kept you thinking even without the puzzles. The philosophical aspect is breathtaking, questioning existence in general and making you think whether or not you are actually alive, yet alone exist. The game draws heavily on the creation story in the Bible, but the way it is executed is outstanding. Even the audio logs had deep meaning and thoughts that were inspiring at times and made you appreciate the world and what  we have. Everything this game does is amazing, from the great puzzles, to the excellent story, even to the humorous and well-placed easter eggs. The only games this could be compared to are Portal and Portal 2, but Talos is lightyears ahead in terms of complexity. I feel the need to stress the quality of the graphics again. They are just beyond beautiful and completely breathtaking (Egypt is the most beautiful out of all the worlds IMO). The DLC is also excellent and takes the puzzles from the main game to the next level by upping both the size and scale. I highly suggest getting this game if you are somoene who likes to think and enjoys learning new things. This is not the game for people who like FPS's or any game that doesn't involve a storyline and/or deep thought. The ending to this game is also the best out of any game I've ever played (which is saying a lot because Portal 2's ending was excellent). All around this is a great game and it's hard to find cons with it! You will enter and leave this game a completely different person than you were before. This game sparks a deep connection with the player and inspires a new way of thinking within them.
I can't wait for the sequel!

Max Payne. For any gamer who knows their salt, this name should be familiar. His publisher Take Two has released two games in 2001 and 2003 to great reviews and a decent amount of critical acclaim. Since then, though, the ex-cop has been left in the dust, barely being remembered other than that crappy movie that was released around then with Mark Wahlberg. It seemed for a while Max would just fade away, until back in 2012, when Rockstar Games, now owners of Take Two, released Max Payne 3. How was that? Well, we're taking a look at it now.
STORY: You're... Max Payne, of course. After the events of the last two games, Max is a drunken mess, he smokes regularly, he's addicted to painkillers, and he tries to find a reason to not blow his head off daily. Up until one day, when his old friend Passos comes across him and hires him to guard a wealthy family in Sao Paulo, Brazil named the Bronco's. Everything seems fine until the wife of the eldest Bronco is kidnapped, and Max and Passos go on a search to find her. That's all I can really say about it without spoilering it. It's a pretty well put together story. It can be pretty depressing at times when you see Max lose, but when he wins, which is kind of rare, it feels great. That's really all you can ask for. The story is a bit on the short side, took me 10 hours to beat it on Medium, but it's a good experience regardless.
GAMEPLAY: 3rd person shooter. You have 4 slots for guns. You have 2 slots one handed weapons, another for a two handed weapon, and the 4th one is dual wielding the two one handed weapons you have on you. All methods are satisfying enough, and gunplay is fantastic. The innovative Bullet Time from the last few games is here too, and that is great, and it has some new features. If you carry painkillers on you, and you lose all your health, you have a chance to shoot the guy who would have killed you and take him out, getting some health back and putting you back into the fight. Ammo can be a bit scarce, especially on the harder difficulties, but if you're efficient enough, you can do well. The game is freaking hard, btw, even when I played it on Medium, it was hard. The game is really satisfying when you beat the levels, and I ended up replaying it on Hardcore, which made me tear my hair out a bit but it was totally worth it. Gameplay is fantastic, maybe even best of 2012.
GRAPHICS AND PERFORMANCE: Game looks good. The favelas of Sao Paulo look grimy and dirty, the nicer penthouses are well designed. There are a lot of nice details in all the levels without a doubt. This isn't a grand open world game like GTA or Red Dead Redemption or LA Noire like Rockstar is known for making, but the smaller levels are fine. They all look great. Game runs pretty well as well, since it's a game from 2012, if you have any recent hardware you should be fine. Runs well enough on my PC, and if I can run it, you can run it.
CHARACTERS AND VOICE ACTING: Max Payne has his voice actor from the last games, James McCaffery, and goddamn, is he as good as ever. The other characters are voiced well enough too. The characters look good, Max goes through a bit of a redesign halfway through which some people didn't like, but I thought he looked fine. Overall it's fine.
MULTIPLAYER: Practically abandoned on PC, played a bit on my 360, kind of fun, but nothing spectacular, odds are unless you get a big community for it you wont get to play it anyway.
EXTRAS: In each level, there are clues that relate to the story, though you have to look for a few of them. There are also some parts for golden versions of each weapon, and if you get all the parts scattered around the levels, you get a better version of the gun every time you pick it up. Once you beat the game, you unlock Score Attack, which is basically a kill and get points mode. There's also the New York Minute mode, where you have to beat a level in a minute. Well, you get time for killing guys, but still. If you arent impressed by that, then you have New Youk Minute Hardcore mode, in which you have to beat the whole game in a minute with the same bonuses, with no deaths. Yeah... good luck with that.
FINAL VERDICT: Phenominal game. One of the best of 2012, strong competator with Far Cry 3 and Mass Effect 3 for that slot. 9/10, it's worth picking up around a sale, hell, even right now. It's also one of the few games that I keep going back to time and time again to play through it once more, so I have to give some credit to them for that. Grab this game, you won't regret it

This is the story of Arkady.
Arkady had crash landed on different planet with his ex-wife Reika and a teen named Red.
Arkady was taught in his previous life to never helped the wounded, so he would not doctor anyone. I knew that this would eventually be the downfall of Arkady.
Life goes on for the colony.
They end up naming themselves the Hialeah colony.
Hialeah was not a very advanced colony. It was difficult to survive due to the lack of knowledge on how to create a sustainable food source, but they managed to do so and were happy.
Then the Dark Scythes attacked.
The Dark Scythes were a local tribe that were hell bent on looting the Hialeah colony.
Raid after raid went by, but Arkady led the charge in each battle to protect what he had created.
Arkady and Reika found that spark once again that they had when they were first married, they were now once again in a relationship.
A worker from another tribe joins called Lee.
Things are going well for the Hialeah colony.
Arkady felt that he was once again ready to spend his life with Reika, so he proposed.
She accepted and they were ready to get married.
The collapse started  when Cobra showed up.
Cobra was a former member of the Dark Scythes who was on the run. He asked to join the Hialeah colony for protection.
The colony decides to let him in.
The Dark Scythes did not take kindly to this and attacked with full force.
Lee was the first to fall. He had his nose and left ear shot off. Many other bullet wounds were found on his body, primarily in his left leg.
Reika fell second. She was shot many time in the chest, but she took many out before she fell.
Lee and Reika were rushed to their beds for treatment by Red.
Cobra and Arkady were able to chase the attackers away.
Arkady got a pulse rifle from one of the dead attackers.
Just when Cobra was about to help the wounded, the Dark Scythes started another attack.
This attack was different than the first. They had decided that they had lost enough men on frontal attacks, so they were planning on using mortars.
There were two people incapable of walking due to their wounds, so waiting them out was not an option.
Arkady went since he could not help the wounded in any other way, and Cobra went too since he was the reason this was happening.
The two men were heavily outnumbered, but not out gunned. Most of the 9 attakers only had pistols or single shot rifles, while Arkady had a charge rifle and Cobra had an SMG.
They were able to push back the attackers, but Cobra was badly wounded in his torso.
Arkady and Cobra returned home.
Cobra was near death, so he was forced to stay in bed until he could get better.
At this point in time there are three wounded people that all are getting infections.
Food was once again low, so the only thing Arkady could do to help was go hunting.
Just as he was about to leave for his hunt, the experiences he had in combat caught up to him and he had a mental breakdown infront of everybody.
Reika could not forgive Arkady for breaking down at the moment she needed him most, so she called off the wedding.
Overwhelmed by grief, Arkady had another breakdown.
At this point it looked like Lee would need an amputation of his left leg, Reaika would die due to her left lung being infected, and Cobra would die to multiple infections in his torso.
Arkady was an outcast to his own colony, but he was the only one who could save them from this.
Then an escape pod crash landed not far from the colony.
In the wreckage was Sloan, a woman who was badly injured.
Arkady was exhausted from his constant efforts to support the colony, but he went to save his only chance of a person that would respect him and treat him normally.
Red used the last of the medicine stockpile to save Sloan.
Once Sloan woke up, she decided to leave.
Arkady was not about to let that happen after they used the last of the medicine that could have been used on his fellow colonists on her.
Arkady confronts Sloan outside as she is trying to leave.
Sloan refuses to return, and Arkady has been pushed to his limit. He beats Sloan to death.
Time goes on after this.
All of the colonists have made a full recovery.
None of the colonists forgave Arkady for murdering Sloan.
A new tribe attacks with only clubs. They are easily warded off, but Arkady manages to capture one of them that has very high speech.
Red tries to treat the new prisoner, but the prisoner goes insane.
Arkady was forced to shoot the prisoner.
Even though he was forced to, none of the other colonists understood and claimed he killed her in cold blood. This was most likely due to what happened with Sloan.
They can not act on any of this though since the Dark Scythes attack once again.
Everyone takes cover behind the sand bags and prepares themselves.
This time the Dark Scythes brought grenades and molotovs.
Fire starts to spread. Cobra is the first to get engulfed in the flames.
Next is Lee. Both of them died without any hope of saving them.
Arkady and Reika are the only ones left that are able to fight.
Arkady dies next to Reika from a direct hit molotov.
That is the end of Arkady, but his colony could return to its former glory.
Red treats Reika's wounds.
Half of the buildings are burned to the ground.
Reika returns to full health.
Now it is time to rebuild.
It is winter so the first thing they need to do is set up a source of heat.
They are about to set up the power once again, but Reika goes berzerk and murders the her savior, Red.
Reika did what she hated Arkady for, killing someone in cold blood.
Reika dies due to the cold.
The Hialeah colony is now all dead, with barely anything still standing to show for it.
Reika broke the man that was Arkady. Hialeah was nothing without Arkady.
♥♥♥♥ you Reika.

I never suspected one game could go that far with only a floor and a street lamp. The designer really understands what minimalism is, and knows that it's more important to get the core mechanic right rather than filling the game with content. It's better to fill it with endless costless zombies and shoot them wave after wave because that's what gamers do.
Yet Another Zombie Defense doesn't try to wrap the player's experience with a storyline (avoiding the pitfall of Dead Effect) and focuses on the sandbox aspect of tower defense genre.
I really appreciated the tension created by this limited environment ; you can stay close to the lamp to see your friendly local zombies, or dive into the darkness to grab money, bandages or ammunition.
You can build quite a fortress but the game have a great risk/reward here : since the items drops where the zombies lay, you'll have to run into danger to grab them. So if you play it safe behind your walls, you'll never get enougth ressources to face the upcoming challenges. Simple but effective.
As a minus, the tower defense lacks depth : only 3 barriers and 2 turrets. While playing, I surprised myself wanting more elements to be placed like another street lamp to see farther, lures to manage the zombie flow, and maybe tar to slow them down. I hope they'll be implemented in the future ;)
Even if it's not game that will engage you for 15 hours straight, it grows on you and you always want to try another defense option, with sole goal of beating your own high score. That shouldn't have been easy for the developers to balance every item of the game to get that feeling right, but they succeeded.
Not only I recommend this game as a nice filler, but I also recommend it to game design students.

An early access game that WORKS? What is this contraption?
Well, Rimworld is the perfect example of early access, an extremely treacherous and shady service, done SO ♥♥♥♥ING RIGHT! You can almost not notice the "Alpha" stamp on the game. Exceptionally few bugs.
Now, story-wise, the game has nothing. These "Story tellers" are actually just difficulty parameters
. Furthermore, when ACTUALLY selecting the real difficulty, there's no "normal", the closest you can get is "some challenge" or "Rough".
Action-wise, the game is satisfying and what normal gamer would call "realistic" (the right word being "authentic"). Your settlers will often times miss, even ones with high shooting skills. Melee is definetly the way to go at CQC.
You can even capture injured attackers, patch them up, and SELL THEM TO PIRATES, WOOOO! Become a slave-tycoon! Or, through the stockholm syndrome, recruit your enemies to work for you! Or just leave them for dead, to bleed out from their missing limbs, explained below.
Characters can even lose bodyparts; Arms, legs, eyes, destroyed stomachs, lungs. These can be replaced with either organic replacements (only for intestence), simple prosthetics or even bionic bodyparts which are better than your pathetic orgnic♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or simply dismissed. I have had several one-legged, armed or eyed guys. Even some One-lunged or one-kidney(ed?) ones too.
The simplistic Prison Architect-ish art style fits perfectly into this amazing experience.
Did i mention that you can create your own scenarios? Customize your starting gear, exposition and characters! Even starting animals!
Final verdict: For being Early Access: 9/10, needs more story, things to do, goals. As a normal game: 8/10, same comment.

The Talos Principle seems like a direct entry into the narrated puzzle-adventure drama that Portal and certain precursors (sort of, like Uninvited perhaps) are in. The game starts with you waking up in a mysterious place and someone tells you he is God. You solve various puzzles just getting around as well as to further the plot.
The puzzles are well thought out, but the world itself can be broken with minor effort. Played straight, the voice acting and other assets (textures, lighting, overall design unity, levels, et c) are superb! It's a wonderful addition for the people that greatly enjoyed Portal, its sequel, and similar games.
One thing that is distinctly annoying is the habit of the game to frustrate the narrative by weaving it between text, visual cues, and the voice of God. People who do not take the time to explore the entirety of the game will likely miss out on much of the underlying plot, which is a shame as the deeper inspection of philosophy in this medium could provoke quite profound awareness in the audience - it is really the meat of the game's plot.
The puzzles, while grossly ordered by color in terms of difficulty and organized into sections for thematic convenience, can be very obtuse, requiring a lot of moving around and inspection. Additionally several of the bonus puzzles require lateral thinking to fully enjoy and some are a direct test of quick reflex with known game techniques you are taught.
Altogether a wonderful game, and well worth the time, money, and effort to explore.

This has to be one of the best games I have ever played, let me explain why.
Ok, first off, I am a HUGE fan or Portal 1 and 2. So I went into that thinking this might be similar. And in a way, this game is just like portal, but completely turned upside down. The basic layout is the same: You solve interesting puzzles chambers to proceed. The setting however is completely different. Where Portal is about british sarcasm and the interesting storyline between you and GLaDOS (in my opinion), The Talos Principle is a lot more about the existance of life, AI, beautiful scenery and at time exhausting philosophical questions. You can play the game at your own pace, which is something I personally like and you can constantly make your own decisions. And believe me when I say certain choices have a huge impact on the game.
The puzzles themselves are do-able, and occasionally very difficult. I solved them all without help from the internet, just 1 tip from a friend was all I needed to complete all the puzzles. But that doesn't mean they are easy. Some took me incredibly long to solve, but when you do find the solution, it just feels so good! The philosophical stuff they tell you in the game really interested me and gets you thinking. It's some serious stuff, really. After playing for a couple hours straight I was mentally tired of solving all the puzzles and thinking about all these deep issues. You could skip most of it if you really don't care about it, though I don't recommend it because that will remove maybe the biggest part of the game. The narritive (the story) in this game is not the best, but it is very solid and well made. The main focus  of this game are ethical, philosophical questions and the puzzles.
There are also tons of extra things to get, like in Mario, many secret items to find and collect. These can be REALLY hard to collect (I collected only 10% of them I think without help). But if you like more challenges, you can put a lot more time in this game if you want!
Oh one more thing: There are some brilliant (hard to find) Easer Eggs in this game. Try to find them!
All and all, I had the greatest experience playing this game. It was really fun, rewarding and challenging.
If you like challenging puzzles wrapped up in some narrative and a lot of complex philisophical issues, this game is THE perfect game for you! Definately worth it's money! Now I'm off to play the DLC!

This game. Oh my God, this game. I have never felt so engaged, so emotionally invested.
This game puts you in the deep and dirty. It held no punches, it did not deviate. It gave you the worst ideals of the Nazi regime, the grimiest experiments and most morally-devoid acts, amplified them and spread them about a world to explore. It hits hard. There were times where I felt enraged by the actions of the Nazi soldiers before me, and I wanted nothing but to stick a knife in their neck. At the same time however, each soldier that has dialogue was packed with character. You could see how they were still human, how they momentarily hesitated in their actions or mistakes, but the deep Nazi connections blanketed all that and they continued with their action. Amazing game, one of the most immersive and insightful games I have played since the STALKER series.
-Excellent plot-related writing.  You can predict the plot without too many problems, but there's still so much pleasure in taking part.
-Puzzles are a mix of critical thinking and a lack of overthinking.  You learn how to properly switch between large-scale planning, and smaller-scale instinct for resolving puzzles that can either be large and complex or a series of small tasks.
-Incredible philosophical discussion.  Note that I'm not saying "incredible philosophy".  The game likes to mess with your perspectives and make you question them regardless of what they may be.  The in-game conversations also provide insight into how to properly discuss a philosophical subject like consciousness (or show you that there might not be a proper way to have such dialogue).
-Lots of exploring, contrary to how it may seem at first.  You just have to look around the maps and you glean most of the story this way.  They do reward you for looking around, you can only make complete sense of the events by exploring, sort of like how Bioshock has the audiotapes around.
-Really great aesthetically, like beautiful.  Gameplay is incredibly smooth too.
The devs really went out of their ways to offer an incredible game with atmosphere that is UNIQUE to their own art style and writing.  The soundtrack is also pretty great too, doesn't overpower the game.  IMO this is one of the best games I've picked up in years.  $40 is actually worth it if you consider that it'll probably take you 30+ hours to beat, more likely 40+ if you do all the extra stuff in a very quick amount of time.  I left this review just because I felt the devs REALLY deserve as much praise as they could get for their work.  8/10.   Only thing that could be improved is that it could've been longer for the price they're offering, but at $10 it is a STEAL.

The legend of Gareth.
Gareth was a rich man, here to start his new life alongside his best friend Olive, a cat. He landed on a strange new planet and quickly established a base in an old ruin, building a farm and beds to ensure the best life for him and Olive.
One day whilst farming Gareth spotted a man in the distance, stumbling across the wasteland. This is how Gordon was introduced to Gareths simple but happy life. Gordon didn't have many skills, in fact, Gordon had no skills. He was a nudist and a pacifist, allowing Gordon to deal with any threats that may come to Garethville. He took a shine to the Potato patch and spent his days farming away, rarely getting involved in anything other than his crops.
Life went on in Garethville. Olive, Gareth and Gordon lived out many days happily, trading with the locals and establishing their small outpost into something they could love, a home. Things were going well, untill a shadow from Gareths past arrived, Tiffy. Tiffy was Gareth's ex lover from a his old life, determined to reunite with him. She landed badly, broken and unconcious. Gareth almost left her to bleed out in the rain, and she would have done if not for Gordon. Gordon decided potatoes were not enough for him, and with his sweaty naked body he carried Tiffy back to Garethville.
Tiffy spent many days recovering, while being tended to by Gordon. Gareth stayed out the way, not wanting to confront his past. He instead occupied his time with the incresed bandits in the area. After a raid, Gareth noticed movement in the corpses. A peg legged man with a mohawk, lay unconcious and bleeding from the multiple gunshot wounds Gareth had just inflicted upon him. Taking pity on the man, Gareth brought him home to Garethville, placing him in the medical ward alongside Tiffy.
Everything was gong well, Tiffy was recovering, and the man (whom Gareth had named Peggo) seemed to be getting better. In the end however, it would be Gordon, the nudist pacifist that undid everything Gareth had worked so hard to accomplish.
An illness came in the night and took Peggy, causing Gareths crazy ex to eat his corpse as Gordon was late with breakfast. This sent Tiffy even crazier and she started to knock down the door. Not wanting anything to do with violence or fixing the mess he had caused by bringing her here, Gordon went back to tending his crops.
As Gareth was deciding how to deal with the situation another bandit raid attacked. Four of them this time, more than Gareth had ever faced alone. Gareth decided to deal with Tiffy first, kicking down the door and attempting to knock her out with his bullets. Unfortunately she didnt survive the fight, what a shame. Gareth made his way past the crops and the ever useless Gordon to fight the bandits alone. The battle was long and Gareth held his own, killing 3 of them. The fourth got a lucky shot, curving round the side of his cover. Gareth fell, knocked out but alive, bleeding in the dirt he had worked so hard to defend.
Gordon didnt care, Gordon wouldnt fight. Gordon just wanted to look after the potatoes. He watched from a distance as Gareth was carried from his home over the shoulder of a raider, never to been seen again.
Moral of the story. Never trust nudists.

After 19 hours I can say this game is pretty awesome. I would ignore the EA tag as this game fells like anything but an EA title. There are 3 different scenarios to choose from: the standard of 3 people crashing on a planet and trying to survive, the rich explorer on his own looking for adventure, or 5 surviving tribe members trying to rebuild after a catastrophe. If none of those tickle your fancy they have added an editor and you can make up your own scenario (it is pretty epic what you can do).
Once you get everthing set up then you choose a map size and a location on a planet. Make sure to pay attention to the times you can grow crops, you don't want to be stuck somewhere you can only grow crops for a limited amount of time, and also pay attention to the average temps as some people like certain temperatures. After you selcect your planet is when you get to pick your crew of people. I suggest trying to find people without any injuries (scars included), and make sure to be diversified in the peoples abilites. It's funny some of the quirks these peopel have :)
Launch your game and immediately pause so you can scope it out, plan how you want to build and set your people to working. I recommend watching some videos before hand as there is a learning curve, but once you get the basics down it's a ton of fun.
I can see me investing a lot more time into this one for sure. Good luck and have fun!!

This was the best 75 cents of my entire life. For those who want a full review, read on. Otherwise, I give the game a 9/10 for a low price and fun gameplay.
I found this game randomly, saw it was 75 cents for a two pack (ON SALE), and instantly got it thinking it would be only decent, but it's actually really good! This is a very simple game, and as such it is not very difficult to learn the different mechanics. As the title may suggest, this game is about defending yourself from zombies, but it's in a third person perspective and it's done pretty well overall. This game offers two gamemodes, which are Defense and Endless Night (which can be unlocked by getting to night 7 of Defense). The 3 characters are Guy, Girl, and Swat, and they do not (as far as I've seen) have any difference between them. I think it would be cool to add some special characteristics to make the characters different; such as the Guy having more Defense, the Girl having more Speed, and the Swat having more Damage or Firing Speed. Every Night in Defense mode you can buy upgrades like fences or weapons, and so you evolve from night to night. But as expected, the zombies slowly get more challenging too. This game is a masterpiece for the asking price of as little as 50 cents for a copy, and is still fun. For those who have that little amount of money in their steam wallet, I highly recommend getting this game. It's lots of fun.

I have just completed my first playthrough of the game. I saved the one on the right, you'll get what that means when you get to that part, as it's a pretty big spoiler and major turning point. The good news is it's in the beginning part of the game.
This game. Oh my God, this game. I have never felt so engaged, so emotionally invested.
This game puts you in the deep and dirty. It held no punches, it did not deviate. It gave you the worst ideals of the Nazi regime, the grimiest experiments and most morally-devoid acts, amplified them and spread them about a world to explore. It hits hard. There were times where I felt enraged by the actions of the Nazi soldiers before me, and I wanted nothing but to stick a knife in their neck. At the same time however, each soldier that has dialogue was packed with character. You could see how they were still human, how they momentarily hesitated in their actions or mistakes, but the deep Nazi connections blanketed all that and they continued with their action. There were also Soldiers who were as merciless as their commanders, and killed indiscriminantly.
This was an experience like no other. The writing is perfect, the graphics are appealing, the music great, and the story is phenominal. The gunplay and the shooting felt amazing. Some parts it felt a little wonky, but you get used to it.
I am very much biased towards this game, but that's mostly because the ending had me in tears. I can't play this for less than four or so hours a playthrough. I highly recommend it, get it when you can.

I won't comment on the puzzles, due to the difficulty level being all over the place and not really a linear progression. I also won't comment on the graphical or audible elements, because they aren't the centrepoint of the game, but despite that they were often beautiful and emotive beyond other games by a significant margin.
What I've come to comment about is the philosophy, and the lingering thoughts this game leaves you with. It's unlike most games, where there's always a big baddy to defeat, even in a puzzle game with no weapons or offensive capabilities. This game, if you take the time to explore, and go for that larger completion rather than just blasting through as quick as possible, makes you realise a great many things. Yes, it has an underlying story that is utterly heartwrenching, and can bring tears to your eyes at times, but it brings to life a very real set of questions and moral considerations that are relevant today, tomorrow, for the next few years.
If you're thinking about buying this game to feel smart, don't. It will achieve that goal, but not in a satisfying way. However, if you want something a bit more original, and more intellectually involved, this is the game for you. It speaks to you as a player on a level that other games haven't really touched upon quite as deeply as this, and there are many moments when you will find yourself stopping in game to consider what you've just seen/heard/read/done.

This is the story of Arkady.
Arkady had crash landed on different planet with his ex-wife Reika and a teen named Red.
Arkady was taught in his previous life to never helped the wounded, so he would not doctor anyone. I knew that this would eventually be the downfall of Arkady.
Life goes on for the colony.
They end up naming themselves the Hialeah colony.
Hialeah was not a very advanced colony. It was difficult to survive due to the lack of knowledge on how to create a sustainable food source, but they managed to do so and were happy.
Then the Dark Scythes attacked.
The Dark Scythes were a local tribe that were hell bent on looting the Hialeah colony.
Raid after raid went by, but Arkady led the charge in each battle to protect what he had created.
Arkady and Reika found that spark once again that they had when they were first married, they were now once again in a relationship.
A worker from another tribe joins called Lee.
Things are going well for the Hialeah colony.
Arkady felt that he was once again ready to spend his life with Reika, so he proposed.
She accepted and they were ready to get married.
The collapse started  when Cobra showed up.
Cobra was a former member of the Dark Scythes who was on the run. He asked to join the Hialeah colony for protection.
The colony decides to let him in.
The Dark Scythes did not take kindly to this and attacked with full force.
Lee was the first to fall. He had his nose and left ear shot off. Many other bullet wounds were found on his body, primarily in his left leg.
Reika fell second. She was shot many time in the chest, but she took many out before she fell.
Lee and Reika were rushed to their beds for treatment by Red.
Cobra and Arkady were able to chase the attackers away.
Arkady got a pulse rifle from one of the dead attackers.
Just when Cobra was about to help the wounded, the Dark Scythes started another attack.
This attack was different than the first. They had decided that they had lost enough men on frontal attacks, so they were planning on using mortars.
There were two people incapable of walking due to their wounds, so waiting them out was not an option.
Arkady went since he could not help the wounded in any other way, and Cobra went too since he was the reason this was happening.
The two men were heavily outnumbered, but not out gunned. Most of the 9 attakers only had pistols or single shot rifles, while Arkady had a charge rifle and Cobra had an SMG.
They were able to push back the attackers, but Cobra was badly wounded in his torso.
Arkady and Cobra returned home.
Cobra was near death, so he was forced to stay in bed until he could get better.
At this point in time there are three wounded people that all are getting infections.
Food was once again low, so the only thing Arkady could do to help was go hunting.
Just as he was about to leave for his hunt, the experiences he had in combat caught up to him and he had a mental breakdown infront of everybody.
Reika could not forgive Arkady for breaking down at the moment she needed him most, so she called off the wedding.
Overwhelmed by grief, Arkady had another breakdown.
At this point it looked like Lee would need an amputation of his left leg, Reaika would die due to her left lung being infected, and Cobra would die to multiple infections in his torso.
Arkady was an outcast to his own colony, but he was the only one who could save them from this.
Then an escape pod crash landed not far from the colony.
In the wreckage was Sloan, a woman who was badly injured.
Arkady was exhausted from his constant efforts to support the colony, but he went to save his only chance of a person that would respect him and treat him normally.
Red used the last of the medicine stockpile to save Sloan.
Once Sloan woke up, she decided to leave.
Arkady was not about to let that happen after they used the last of the medicine that could have been used on his fellow colonists on her.
Arkady confronts Sloan outside as she is trying to leave.
Sloan refuses to return, and Arkady has been pushed to his limit. He beats Sloan to death.
Time goes on after this.
All of the colonists have made a full recovery.
None of the colonists forgave Arkady for murdering Sloan.
A new tribe attacks with only clubs. They are easily warded off, but Arkady manages to capture one of them that has very high speech.
Red tries to treat the new prisoner, but the prisoner goes insane.
Arkady was forced to shoot the prisoner.
Even though he was forced to, none of the other colonists understood and claimed he killed her in cold blood. This was most likely due to what happened with Sloan.
They can not act on any of this though since the Dark Scythes attack once again.
Everyone takes cover behind the sand bags and prepares themselves.
This time the Dark Scythes brought grenades and molotovs.
Fire starts to spread. Cobra is the first to get engulfed in the flames.
Next is Lee. Both of them died without any hope of saving them.
Arkady and Reika are the only ones left that are able to fight.
Arkady dies next to Reika from a direct hit molotov.
That is the end of Arkady, but his colony could return to its former glory.
Red treats Reika's wounds.
Half of the buildings are burned to the ground.
Reika returns to full health.

The simplistic Prison Architect-ish art style fits perfectly into this amazing experience.
Did i mention that you can create your own scenarios? Customize your starting gear, exposition and characters! Even starting animals!
Final verdict: For being Early Access: 9/10, needs more story, things to do, goals. As a normal game: 8/10, same comment.

Rockstar manages to take Max Payne where Remedy left off and, in my opinion, surpass the first two games in quality. Obviously, being nine years later, they had plenty of time and more resources to work out new mechanics and animation style, specifically the cover system which was absent in the first two.
The other notable aspect of Max Payne 3 is that the ending isn't as depressing as the first two. The first game already started off depressing due to his family being murdered and the second one involves his downfall as a police officer. Here, Max is a private security guard in Sao Paulos, Brazil, for a rich family. Similar to the first two games, however, a major conspiracy is set in store for Max as he traverses the various parts of Brazil, fighting criminals and paramilitary goons. Without spoiling anything, I will say that the game ends on a high note as you get to see Max, for once in his life, relaxing and content with things.
The strongest aspect of the Max Payne games were always the writing, and the Houser's do Sam Lake justice by writing a brilliant script. The character dialog is strong, the plot is complex but not contrived, and narrative is exhilerating. The major side characters, Raul Passos and Detective Wilson da Silva are interesting due to their own backgrounds. And the flashbacks to New Jersey was a nice throwback with Max's classic outfit and his involvement in destroying the local mafia.

TL;DR: I recommend this game wholeheartedly to fans of puzzle games, philosophy, ambience and intriguing narratives.
I first want to say that this is my first review. I feel compelled to write it in order to recommend this great game to others. Playing this game gave me the rare experience of being pulled in completely by the mystery and ambience and alluring narrative of a game to such a degree that I had a hard time breaking away from the game until I had completed it.
I think, the plot of the game should be spoiled as little as possible for newcomers, so my advice is: dive in, dive down the rabbit hole, and be amazed! In short, it is a puzzle game with a great story, a very well paced narrative, great music, beautiful scenery, great writing, great voice-acting, and realistic feeling reactivity to choices (yes). The game is long, but the puzzles and level design are creative enough for it not to get boring. And although the game is long, it is not too long. This game sets a standard for atmosphere and intelligent writing that I hope other games will try to meet.
Some things that could be held against the game: some puzzles were hard - some were very easy. But easy puzzles doesn't bother me in a game where every couple of solved puzzles advance the narrative. And some of the scenery can get a bit repetetive - although this kind of fits with the narrative, and anyway, the creative level design keeps it interesting throughout. And maybe it should be made clear that although the game is played in first person 3d, it is not a shooter or any kind of action game (although time constraints factor in at places), but a puzzle game. So if that is not your thing at all, and if you wouldn't consider playing a puzzle in spite of a great story and great writing, this probably won't be your thing. But I think it would be a thing for many.
As I said, my advice is to dive in. And only take to the internet and guides and walkthroughs for completionism and secrets after you have experienced most of the game first-hand.
To give you some insight into my perspective, I am a jaded former student of philosophy and an at times disillusioned gamer. This game kind of rekindled my interest in some philosophical subjects as well as my hope for narrative in games.

It is an OK game. Some changes brought to the Max Payne series could completely kill it, but luckily they are pulled well enough to work (even though in some cases just barely.)
Combat is almost as good as it used to be. It certainly looks  better. The game's budget is visible. It looks fantastic, runs fantastic and plays fantastic. Especially impressive are animations, making the bullet time a joy. The downside is lack of weapons. There are plenty weapons is the game but you are limited to only 3 weapons at any given time (2 handguns + large weapon.) That means you will have to use what game gives you and you don't have much choice in what you use. I found myself using primary automatic weapons and with a very headshot focus system they are simply better than anything else. Because of that the gameplay is quite repetitive and there aren't really moments which would stand out.
There are quite a few things I don't like, period. The game if full of cutscenes. We already got one bad Max Payne movie, we don't need another. I am not a big fan of a large ammount of uninteractive elements in an interactive medium. But that was their decision and they did pull it pretty well. Game switches from one to the other quite seemlessly and often recognizes what weapon you are carrying during gameplay segments. It did cause problems at times. At some points the game would trigger cutscene after every encouter and move me to the next room. This didnt give me a chance to loot ammo and eventually I found myself with none. While game is very cutscene heavy, they are not terribly interesting to watch.
The tone of the game is quite different than this of MP1&2. Instead of comic-pulp-noir we have a hollywood action in style of "Man on Fire" - with lots of swearing, violence but none of the emotional punch. While I don't terribly mind the change of the setting (levels are quite varied and nice to took at) I miss the humor and overall cleverness. Gone is the satire and gone are the dream sequences. Instead there is lots of yelling, alcohol/drug abuse, f***ing and one again yelling all wrapped up in annoying screen effects. The story is simply weaker as Max motivations are external rather than internal.
So for those who played MP1&2 it is good enough to give a shot. If you didn't play MP1&2 you should check out those instead.

Wolfenstein New Order is a monster of a game, weighing in at over 40 GB and it is one heck of a game, with excellent production values and a proper story that, while somewhat cliche-y, is actually more than just... "kill Nazis". With a large mix of weapons, alternate modes, dual wield, "commanders" and reinforcements, stealth kills (including knife-throwing) and a LOT of different fatalities, esp. if you accomplish takedowns. Add to that a scifi-y alternate history universe, tons of colelctibles (various gold artifacts, letters and codes, background info and bonus content) and you have one heck of a game that satisfies.
Wolfenstein New Order is set in an alternate WW2, where Nazis have discovered some sort of alternate technology that severely outclass the allies, and in a desperate bid for survival in 1946, with war all but lost, Allies launched a suicidal airborne assault on the military leader, known as General Deathshead, hoping to cut the snake off at the head, and at the tip of the spear is Captain B.J. Blaskowiecz. You start on the plane, you have to help defend the plane, from Luftwaffe, run around with damage control, make a mid-air leap, then when the plane finally ditched on the island, you have to swim to a turret, help break out the trapped comrades, fight your way into the island, take out the local commanders, get enough weapons to storm the castle, ascend a vertical face while shooting bad guys, make it into the compound, shoot more Nazis, and... well, for the rest you have to play the game yourself. Let's just say it did not end well with BJ ended up in a vegetative state for a dozen years at a mental institution, only to wake up when the Nazis are liquidating the entire building. He fought his way out, saved the nurse who took care of him. Only to find the truth... It is now 1960. Germany not only conquered Europe, but America too. New York was hit by an atom bomb and US surrendered. There is no more resistance, or is there?
The graphics are good, and the weapons are brutal but realistic, albeit in a scifi-y sort of way. There were tons of enemies to wade through, from grunts all the way to supersoldiers, and worse, such as robots and the "monitor" a huge robot several stories tall and armed with a ton of weapons.
The extra touches like posters, music, and more are very impressive as well. The story could have been a Hollywood screenplay, and there were two sex scenes (don't worry, no exposure) even. And as said before, a ton of death, mostly inflicted by you. The vehicles and so on are numerous and all look right. It is a lot of fun to play. There are five levels of difficulty with the highest obviously requiring some advanced tactics and some mad skills.
The game also has a performanced based perk system where the actions you perform gains you perks in that category. Want to carry more knives? Make thrown knife kills. Want better stealth kills? Do more stealth kills. Want bigger pistol magazine? Do more pistol headshots. And so on.
The addition of commanders adds an interesting tactical dimension to the game. Commanders have radio headsets that can call in reinforcements, and your headset will determine how close they are but not in what direction. It'd be ideal if you can kill them first, but it wasn't always possible.
The bosses have special weak spots that need to be exploited, but that's par for the course.
And the ending is a clear setup for a sequel, though it may or may not involve BJ Blaskowicz, as the ending is rather ambiguous.
My one complaint is the part of the game where there is a need for "dash slide", where you run, and you hit crouch mid run to slide under some obstacles. There are several spots in the game you need to do this, and if you fail, you die. That gets somewhat annoying as you can't do that with just one hand (run is SHIFT and crouch is CTRL). And I prefer playing FPS with mouse-keyboard.
I ran this game on an older hardware, 1st gen i7 and GeForce 445M (yes, laptop) at 1680x1050 with low settings and it ran quite well.
All in all, this game is a real tour de force, as killing Nazis (say it like in Inglorious ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s) doesn't get that old, esp. when there's a scifi edge to it, and the story, if a little bit on the cliche side, is loads better than the typical shooter fare. Add the little touches and you have one heck of a game. Yes, I know I said that many times.

The legend of Gareth.
Gareth was a rich man, here to start his new life alongside his best friend Olive, a cat. He landed on a strange new planet and quickly established a base in an old ruin, building a farm and beds to ensure the best life for him and Olive.
One day whilst farming Gareth spotted a man in the distance, stumbling across the wasteland. This is how Gordon was introduced to Gareths simple but happy life. Gordon didn't have many skills, in fact, Gordon had no skills. He was a nudist and a pacifist, allowing Gordon to deal with any threats that may come to Garethville. He took a shine to the Potato patch and spent his days farming away, rarely getting involved in anything other than his crops.
Life went on in Garethville. Olive, Gareth and Gordon lived out many days happily, trading with the locals and establishing their small outpost into something they could love, a home. Things were going well, untill a shadow from Gareths past arrived, Tiffy. Tiffy was Gareth's ex lover from a his old life, determined to reunite with him. She landed badly, broken and unconcious. Gareth almost left her to bleed out in the rain, and she would have done if not for Gordon. Gordon decided potatoes were not enough for him, and with his sweaty naked body he carried Tiffy back to Garethville.
Tiffy spent many days recovering, while being tended to by Gordon. Gareth stayed out the way, not wanting to confront his past. He instead occupied his time with the incresed bandits in the area. After a raid, Gareth noticed movement in the corpses. A peg legged man with a mohawk, lay unconcious and bleeding from the multiple gunshot wounds Gareth had just inflicted upon him. Taking pity on the man, Gareth brought him home to Garethville, placing him in the medical ward alongside Tiffy.
Everything was gong well, Tiffy was recovering, and the man (whom Gareth had named Peggo) seemed to be getting better. In the end however, it would be Gordon, the nudist pacifist that undid everything Gareth had worked so hard to accomplish.
An illness came in the night and took Peggy, causing Gareths crazy ex to eat his corpse as Gordon was late with breakfast. This sent Tiffy even crazier and she started to knock down the door. Not wanting anything to do with violence or fixing the mess he had caused by bringing her here, Gordon went back to tending his crops.
As Gareth was deciding how to deal with the situation another bandit raid attacked. Four of them this time, more than Gareth had ever faced alone. Gareth decided to deal with Tiffy first, kicking down the door and attempting to knock her out with his bullets. Unfortunately she didnt survive the fight, what a shame. Gareth made his way past the crops and the ever useless Gordon to fight the bandits alone. The battle was long and Gareth held his own, killing 3 of them. The fourth got a lucky shot, curving round the side of his cover. Gareth fell, knocked out but alive, bleeding in the dirt he had worked so hard to defend.
Gordon didnt care, Gordon wouldnt fight. Gordon just wanted to look after the potatoes. He watched from a distance as Gareth was carried from his home over the shoulder of a raider, never to been seen again.
Moral of the story. Never trust nudists.

Wolfenstein New Order is a monster of a game, weighing in at over 40 GB and it is one heck of a game, with excellent production values and a proper story that, while somewhat cliche-y, is actually more than just... "kill Nazis". With a large mix of weapons, alternate modes, dual wield, "commanders" and reinforcements, stealth kills (including knife-throwing) and a LOT of different fatalities, esp. if you accomplish takedowns. Add to that a scifi-y alternate history universe, tons of colelctibles (various gold artifacts, letters and codes, background info and bonus content) and you have one heck of a game that satisfies.
Wolfenstein New Order is set in an alternate WW2, where Nazis have discovered some sort of alternate technology that severely outclass the allies, and in a desperate bid for survival in 1946, with war all but lost, Allies launched a suicidal airborne assault on the military leader, known as General Deathshead, hoping to cut the snake off at the head, and at the tip of the spear is Captain B.J. Blaskowiecz. You start on the plane, you have to help defend the plane, from Luftwaffe, run around with damage control, make a mid-air leap, then when the plane finally ditched on the island, you have to swim to a turret, help break out the trapped comrades, fight your way into the island, take out the local commanders, get enough weapons to storm the castle, ascend a vertical face while shooting bad guys, make it into the compound, shoot more Nazis, and... well, for the rest you have to play the game yourself. Let's just say it did not end well with BJ ended up in a vegetative state for a dozen years at a mental institution, only to wake up when the Nazis are liquidating the entire building. He fought his way out, saved the nurse who took care of him. Only to find the truth... It is now 1960. Germany not only conquered Europe, but America too. New York was hit by an atom bomb and US surrendered. There is no more resistance, or is there?
The graphics are good, and the weapons are brutal but realistic, albeit in a scifi-y sort of way. There were tons of enemies to wade through, from grunts all the way to supersoldiers, and worse, such as robots and the "monitor" a huge robot several stories tall and armed with a ton of weapons.
The extra touches like posters, music, and more are very impressive as well. The story could have been a Hollywood screenplay, and there were two sex scenes (don't worry, no exposure) even. And as said before, a ton of death, mostly inflicted by you. The vehicles and so on are numerous and all look right. It is a lot of fun to play. There are five levels of difficulty with the highest obviously requiring some advanced tactics and some mad skills.
The game also has a performanced based perk system where the actions you perform gains you perks in that category. Want to carry more knives? Make thrown knife kills. Want better stealth kills? Do more stealth kills. Want bigger pistol magazine? Do more pistol headshots. And so on.
The addition of commanders adds an interesting tactical dimension to the game. Commanders have radio headsets that can call in reinforcements, and your headset will determine how close they are but not in what direction. It'd be ideal if you can kill them first, but it wasn't always possible.
The bosses have special weak spots that need to be exploited, but that's par for the course.
And the ending is a clear setup for a sequel, though it may or may not involve BJ Blaskowicz, as the ending is rather ambiguous.
My one complaint is the part of the game where there is a need for "dash slide", where you run, and you hit crouch mid run to slide under some obstacles. There are several spots in the game you need to do this, and if you fail, you die. That gets somewhat annoying as you can't do that with just one hand (run is SHIFT and crouch is CTRL). And I prefer playing FPS with mouse-keyboard.
I ran this game on an older hardware, 1st gen i7 and GeForce 445M (yes, laptop) at 1680x1050 with low settings and it ran quite well.
All in all, this game is a real tour de force, as killing Nazis (say it like in Inglorious ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s) doesn't get that old, esp. when there's a scifi edge to it, and the story, if a little bit on the cliche side, is loads better than the typical shooter fare. Add the little touches and you have one heck of a game. Yes, I know I said that many times.

At its most basic, RimWorld is a base/colony builder style of game where you are given control over the lives of a group of colonists and try to build functioning new home for them on a harsh rim world. It is your job to see that all of their needs are met ranging from ensuring that they have an adequate food source to ensuring that their moods are kept high to planning and preparing elaborate base defense systems to fight off the many hostiles that seek to bring your colony doom.
But beyond this initial aspect, RimWorld is also a story generator where you can create a wonderfully in-depth story just from what happens in game and a little creativity. You might have a wildly successful colony that has lasted years and years, having fought off countless raids and unfortunate events to build a thriving community in the unlikely of places. Or, your colony might have only survived a few days at the most, having struck down the wrong wall and opened up an ancient mechanoid nest whose inhabitants cruelly exterminated your colonists, ending their hopes and dreams.
RimWorld is a type of game that can bring out the best and worst in you based on your decisions. Will you choose to be a benevolent leader who chooses to aid anyone who comes seeking help or will you be a cruel and efficient tyrant who abuses his prisoners and harvests their organs for profit. It is a type of game that can out your emotions, from anger over the stupidity of one of your colonists to joy from having fought off that enormous raid with no losses to grief as you realized that during another raid, your star colonist had accidentally been shot by his own wife during the chaos and is now nothing more than a vegetable, never to move again and the first to be put on the menu if times get hard.
I won’t deny that RimWorld can be a tough game at first to get into, one that seems that no matter what you do, you always end up failing in the end. Don’t fret and just keep at it and eventually, you’ll find a breakthrough and finally win for once … only to fall 5 minutes later when another tragedy strikes. This is game where you measure your victories in how far that you’ve managed to come each and everytime, where you’ll discover that you can enjoy failing whent hat failure did not come until after you’ve broken a personal milestone, having survived however many days or done what you’ve set your eyes upon.
And if you’ve managed to beat the best that the vanilla game has set upon you, then there is always the deeper world of mods in RimWorld to add new challenges for you to face or new ways that you can play this game, adding in countless hours of replayability. It is just a fantastic game that you will spend hours and hours on. If you are still unsure, watch some Let’s Plays on YouTube or streams on Twitch of the game and decide for yourself if you really want to join the rest of us in RimWorld and never, ever escape it.

Started a colony with a guy named Frank. Had him for a long time and somehow went completely unscathed through countless battles. I thought to myself, "Wow! This guy is superman!". Next fight: loses both of his arms. Somehow he is still able to do research for me, so I decide to keep him around. After about a year in game I give him 2 bionic arms. A while later there is a massive raid that kills one of his best friends and his wife. Completely depressed, he continually goes berserk and keeps putting my other colonists in the hospital (those bionic arms helped him with that). I end up having to euthanize him. As one of my doctors kneels by his bed after his latest berserk rampage that needed to be stopped with a shotgun to his face, they have a farewell chat and then the doctor ends his life. I now have a shrine built to him in the center of my colony. He will always be remembered.
On a more technical note, the storytelling AI is a genius feature that I have never seen in another game. You really get the impression while playing this game that there is a story that the AI is taking you through. It controls the stream of events your colony experiences to create a certain experience for you. I don't know exactly what is happening behind the scenes, but it really does feel that it is doing much more then simply sending you random events depending on the size of your colony.
If you have any interest in colony/town simulation games, then this is a must buy.
