So where do I start with this review? I think the majority of us older gamers will remember Age of Empires from late 1999 or early 2000. I first played Age of Empires in the late 2002's and early 2003's (curtsy to my cousin who is old enough to be my father for introducing me to this game). I could play this game before I could even read or write, I watched my elder siblings play this game and learnt from them how to do everything.
So as you can tell, this game was one of the first games I ever played and it was the game that really got me into gaming in the first place. I still have my original copy, another copy I picked up for £7 in Morrison's one time in 2008 with the expansion packs.
Let's get properly into the jucy bit of this review. This game is fantastically done but to call it "HD edition" is misleading as it is hardly high definition, they just scaled up the textures and possibly changed the water textures. I can't thing of any other negatives though. I can loose my self in this game for hours and still not want to leave the screen for one second, the competitiveness of this game between empires is crazy (especially on hardest AI settings). The game also works similar to real life, you all have your resources, some have more of one than another, and you can sell or buy resources (like importing and exporting) and have your own supply. It's also interesting how the AI can launch an attack on you when you haven't even started to gather an army and can just wipe out your empire in less than 20mins into that specific game.
In my expierence if you play islands death match large (8players) the best way to go about an invasion is first of by building up a decent size navy and attack from the seas first and then transport your troops to low concentrated area and then have a battle on land between land based troops.
I wouldn't recomend this game to people who don't enjoy games that require a fair bit of patience though, that being said I think that this has to be the best RTS game I have ever played.
Step into the light child, and prepare yourself for an experience that calls into question everything you think you know about being human.

Developers love calling their latest AAA shooter a "modern shooter with an old-school heart" whenever they can, but usually all they mean is "you can carry more than one gun." They tried saying the same thing with the previous Wolfenstein remake, you know, the one with the god-awful open-world gimmick that made traveling from mission to mission feel like torture.
Surprisingly, The New Order delivers on the old-school feel; it's a very fast-paced game that works better as a run and gun than a cover-shooter. Guns feel unique, varied, and powerful, with interesting secondary firing mechanics that unlock as you play, so you never really find yourself getting bored with the guns you've been using since the opening sequence. Rechargeable health is non-existant, finding hidden caches throughout the map feels both necessary and fun. I've found that the idea that you should reward the players for exploring the nooks and crannies of your map to be a somewhat dated idea in the eyes of the modern developer, so it felt really refreshing to think "I'll bet there's a health upgrade somewhere at the end of that seemingly pointless hallway" and actually being right. Yes, there are a few modern-gaming gimmicks thrown in that feel pretty annoying (don't expect to be free from QTE's) but these moments are infrequent enough that it didn't ruin my experience or make me feel like Machine Games thought I was an idiot. Boss battles are challenging, fun, and unique, and usually involve giant mechs, it's great!
The game never takes itself more seriously than you do: it's cheesy, over the top, ridiculous, and self-aware. The cutscenes are over-dramatic in the best way and BJ gives an entertaining, brooding, almost Max Payne-esque narration of what's happening. I loved it. Think 80's Action B-movies. Dialogue aside, the story also presents itself through collectibles and through the environment itself in the form of recordings, newspaper clippings, etc. that fill you in on the details of how the Nazi's won World War II and successfully took over the world. If you're into alt-history, you'll really appreciate all the detail in the background and the expansive reading material written in order to make this retelling of history feel natural and semi-plausible.

Let me tell you a story. I call it The Adventures of Agent Cobra: Episode 69: Checkmate.
Our heroes, Agent Cobra and his furious monkey-boy sidekick Furious have just returned to their Byzantine castle hideout in the mountains. No sooner had they returned than a new document was faxed to their secret missions-only fax machine. Furious picked it up.
"Zimmering zwounds, Agent Cobra, it's a message from the leader of the Byzantines!" He said, flapping the page in the air.
"Well, Furious my boy, what does it say?" He was calm, nonchalant, which was odd, given the traumatic conclusion of their last adventure. Of course, being a car with an automatic assault rifle in the hood, his emotions were difficult to gauge.
"I'm not sure. The message reads: 'how do you turn this on roggan wololo wololo wololo roggan start the game already start the game already don't point that thing at me furious the monkey boy wood please wood please woodwoodwoodwoodwoodwoodwoodwood please <laughs>. Stop. Sincerely, The Byzantine Leader'. What does it mean, Agent Cobra?"
"Furious my boy, that's a cipher," he said, as he somehow lit a cigarette. Puffing a noxious cloud from his exhaust, he continued, "If I'm not mistaken, it can be decrypted to mean 'Dear Cobra Car and Furious the Monkey Boy: I am aware of the dangers of requesting your assistance so often, especially given the... emotional nature of your last mission,'" he shrugged, "'but I fear circumstances have left me with no choice. The reasons for your new mission are confidential, I fear, but your objective is simple: the enemy king must die. Do this and you shall be rewarded.'"
"You decrypted that in your head?"
"Many newer cars have onboard computers..."
"Well, yeah, but not for cryptog..."
"We ride, Furious my boy, to slay the enemy king."
"But which enemy did he mean, Agent Cobra? There are so many. The Aztecs, the Koreans, the Malians, the Franks; how will we know which one to assassinate?"
Cobra put his tire on the confused sidekick's shoulder. "The only way we know how, Furious my boy. The only way we know how."
And that, my son, is why there are so many ruined castles in Europe, and a few in Asia, Africa and Central America.

Pros:
+Strong story driven title
+Narrative gameplay and cutscenes
+Gory
+Great Graphics
+Music fits nicely
+Voice acting is done great and fits in perfectly for the mood he’s portraying
+Cover system and slow time function are great
+Combat is good
+Very dark in nature
+AI don’t mess around
The Middle:
+/-Linear gameplay (this is up to the player who’s playing the game) – I felt they did an excellent job with the concept. It kept the player sucked into the story and at times made me forget I was going from point A to point B, but to go achieve that goal that was needed during that chapter. Not once did I think to myself that this was linear.
+/- Can sound emotional and/or depressing at times, but then again, this is where knowing the knowledge about the last two titles are crucial (I thought it fit in perfectly, but attitude reflects everyone differently when playing a game)
Cons:
-Can be a slow start or even a confusing start if you haven’t played the original 2 games (or didn’t even read about their story via some online source)
-Controls can be wonky at times or at times don’t feel fluid as it should be
-Multiplayer is dead
Summary:
You are placed in Brazil to protect some VIPs and the action takes off immediately. The story at first can start off rather slowly, but it does pick up rather quickly after the first two or so chapters. Max Payne is always narrating the story (as if you were reading a comic book or something similar), whether it’s telling himself to go this direction or a witty comment on why he took the painkillers. Some of the cutscenes do elaborate some portion of his past, but they don’t explain everything on what happened in his past. The cutscenes are nicely done and also give a lot of information for the chapter and the buildup to the final plot that shows at the end of the game.
The graphics are done excellently. A lot of detail went into this game. There is gore (for those who are squeamish), but it’s done right to fit the nature for this game. The blood splatter seems consistent to the bullet wounds and/or explosions, but not overly used when compared to other shoot-them-up titles (i.e. 5 gallons of blood on the floor with only one dead body).
The music fits nicely with the game and it doesn’t sound overwhelming or try take the focus away when listening to the cutscenes and/or when Max Payne beings a narrative discussion. The sounds are done right and the explosions/gunfire is not overwhelming when firing them off. Voice acting was done very nicely. It wasn’t bland, but it was dark and emotional; all relating to his past experiences.
The combat system is done nicely with the game. You’re in 3rd person view unless you pick up selected weapons that have a scope on them. The cover system is done appropriately depending where and how you stay in cover. If someone that has a height advantage above you, they’ll more likely hit you while you’re in cover, but the same can be done to them. The aiming is flawless. I had no issues aiming at their heads whether it was normal pace or slow-motion, though at times the controls do feel wonky. I would have moments where I would want to slow-motion in a direction and the controls would hesitate or be unresponsive. This would also be the case when trying to go into cover, but it would hesitate, I’d click again and it would send me into cover and then right back out of cover.
The AI hit their marks a lot more than most shoot-them-up shooters. This is why the cover system and slow-motion function are key. This isn’t a Battlefield or Call of Duty similarity. This game relies heavily on those two functions or the outcome will be your undoing. I really enjoyed this title and I haven’t played the other two titles. I did some reading on the story prior of playing this title, so I had some clue on what to expect when it came to his emotions and the reason why he was doing the things he did.
The game is rich in story, yet dark in nature. I was never bored or felt the gameplay was linear in any way, shape, or form. I felt the game was more of a movie that you control the main protagonist. I thought they did an excellent job at this game. I didn't play multiplayer because I didn't find any matches, so I cannot give a review based on any multiplayer aspects. Other than that, I would definitely recommend this game.

The legend of Gareth.
Gareth was a rich man, here to start his new life alongside his best friend Olive, a cat. He landed on a strange new planet and quickly established a base in an old ruin, building a farm and beds to ensure the best life for him and Olive.
One day whilst farming Gareth spotted a man in the distance, stumbling across the wasteland. This is how Gordon was introduced to Gareths simple but happy life. Gordon didn't have many skills, in fact, Gordon had no skills. He was a nudist and a pacifist, allowing Gordon to deal with any threats that may come to Garethville. He took a shine to the Potato patch and spent his days farming away, rarely getting involved in anything other than his crops.
Life went on in Garethville. Olive, Gareth and Gordon lived out many days happily, trading with the locals and establishing their small outpost into something they could love, a home. Things were going well, untill a shadow from Gareths past arrived, Tiffy. Tiffy was Gareth's ex lover from a his old life, determined to reunite with him. She landed badly, broken and unconcious. Gareth almost left her to bleed out in the rain, and she would have done if not for Gordon. Gordon decided potatoes were not enough for him, and with his sweaty naked body he carried Tiffy back to Garethville.
Tiffy spent many days recovering, while being tended to by Gordon. Gareth stayed out the way, not wanting to confront his past. He instead occupied his time with the incresed bandits in the area. After a raid, Gareth noticed movement in the corpses. A peg legged man with a mohawk, lay unconcious and bleeding from the multiple gunshot wounds Gareth had just inflicted upon him. Taking pity on the man, Gareth brought him home to Garethville, placing him in the medical ward alongside Tiffy.
Everything was gong well, Tiffy was recovering, and the man (whom Gareth had named Peggo) seemed to be getting better. In the end however, it would be Gordon, the nudist pacifist that undid everything Gareth had worked so hard to accomplish.
An illness came in the night and took Peggy, causing Gareths crazy ex to eat his corpse as Gordon was late with breakfast. This sent Tiffy even crazier and she started to knock down the door. Not wanting anything to do with violence or fixing the mess he had caused by bringing her here, Gordon went back to tending his crops.
As Gareth was deciding how to deal with the situation another bandit raid attacked. Four of them this time, more than Gareth had ever faced alone. Gareth decided to deal with Tiffy first, kicking down the door and attempting to knock her out with his bullets. Unfortunately she didnt survive the fight, what a shame. Gareth made his way past the crops and the ever useless Gordon to fight the bandits alone. The battle was long and Gareth held his own, killing 3 of them. The fourth got a lucky shot, curving round the side of his cover. Gareth fell, knocked out but alive, bleeding in the dirt he had worked so hard to defend.
Gordon didnt care, Gordon wouldnt fight. Gordon just wanted to look after the potatoes. He watched from a distance as Gareth was carried from his home over the shoulder of a raider, never to been seen again.
Moral of the story. Never trust nudists.

Short review: An engrossing and wildly entertaining Nazi shooter that breaks from the brown corridor shooters of recent years. Hindered by engine capabilities and certain graphical glitches, suffers from optimization issues, but an enjoyable shooter nonetheless.
*Spoiler alert for the first 90 minutes of the game*
Long review: Wolfenstein: The New Order is a first person shooter that takes place in the '60s after the Nazis have won World War II, led by a mad scientist who revolutionized warfare by inventing robots to crush the opposing force. After being gravely injured by flying shrapnel, you awake in a mental hospital in Poland as B.J Blazkowicz, a US soldier rescued by fisherman. In a comatose state in the hospital, B.J sees the Nazis shutting down the hospital and massacring everyone in it, and taking Anya, the head nurse who cared for you for 14 years in your wheelchair.
Breaking free from his chains, B.J sets out on a brutal, blood-filled path of revenge against the Nazis, slaughtering all that stand in his way and taking Anya with him to join the Resistance fighters to bring down the Nazi regime across the world.
Wolfenstein's gameplay is simple in terms of first person shooters. Pick up various weapons and shoot Nazis with them, with the added bonus of laser weapons and dual-wielding assault rifles and shotguns. Blast your way through the levels with guns blazing, or pick off each enemy one by one using a simple but satisfying stealth system. With the addition of choices that lead to different timelines with different scenarios, the game's replay value is high and should keep you entertained long enough with it's supposedly 20-hour campaign.
The New Order's graphics are nothing special for next-gen consoles and for PC's in general, but it is very enjoyable to look at and very aesthetically pleasing. However, I feel that the graphics are Wolfenstein's biggest downfall. I have experienced multiple framerate issues and horrid texture pop-in from just looking away and looking back at something. There are supposed fixes, but the game's engine has it's limitations and has many problems RAGE did. Some textures are rather low-res, and I sometimes cannot even hit 60 with a GTX 970. Cutscenes also locked at 30.
Wolfenstein is oddly different from the Call of Duties and Battlefields we get every year. A debut game from MachineGames, it falls back on the fact that it's justified to rip Nazis to shreds with high-caliber weapons because - well, they're Nazis. Also uniquely, the game manages to be a mindless shooter while an engrossing, rich story with likeable characters is mixed in.

Bought this game several months ago.
So far my experience has been quite positive. The game is still in its Alpha stage (6.2 as of now) so there are still old and new bugs. They are luckily not that bad as the game is fully playable and fun.
I'll lay down some of the
things first:
the game runs quite smooth most of the time, usually at around 50-60 fps. The issues start when a big firefight erupts with lots of explosions, smoke and gunfire. The fps might drop by about 10 which is still manageable but the absolute worst is when there are many explosions which basically cause the whole game to freeze for a half a second. This used to be a big problem a couple months ago but the latest updates have improved on this. (When I bought this game, my frames were very low and the stutter/freezing kept happening more often)
the graphics aren't as good as I would like. But then again this is still an Alpha so the team is most likely ironing out bugs and adding other content in before concentrating on polishing it. Most textures look great, my biggest issue has to be with lots of jagged edges that I can't seem to get rid of. Also the foliage on some plants is not too pretty, same goes for grass.
Those were the biggest negative things I could think of. Now for the
bits:
Weapons look, sound and "feel" great.  I would not say that they're as realistic as in Arma 3 (the weapons are not real but they function as if they were) but they are pretty damn close. Weapons have nice feedback when firing, they feel as if they actually had some heft to them. Firing more than a single shot causes a great loss of accuracy and a loss of control in where you are firing. The sounds are great, weapons actually sound like weapons in this game. You can actually differentiate between your teams and the opponents weapons.
There are already several maps in the game and they offer various combat environments which lead to different types of gameplay. You can fight in a forest where you have to be wary of where your enemy is as its easy to hide in foliage, you can shoot across a sand filled hilly landscape with little cover, or you can fight in close quarters in a more urban environment where the enemy can be on the other side of a wall or on a rooftop. Maps tend to be quite large which lets you maneuver and use that as an advantage in a fight.
What makes this game set itself apart from most other games is that you most often will be playing with a squad of up to 9 people (as of now) in which most people have microphones. Cooperation usually functions perfectly between you and your squad though sometimes you do get a commander who does not know what they're doing.
From my perspective this game is really fun to play and a great buy if you like a more slow paced shooter with a sense of realism. The game is being updated quite regularly with new features being added and performance being optimised. At this current stage in development I would totally recommend this game.

EDIT: Wrote a review that is more detailed.
SQUAD, which has its roots in the quite popular mod for Battlefield 2: Project Reality
Aims for both the mod, and the now - standalone Squad, with much upgraded Graphical engine, is to simulate the realistic battlefield as much as this is possible. So, you will spend much time lying, crawling, and sneaking around. This is no Battlefield gameplay, where you shoot and run.
And, this mod does it pretty well. Well populated 50v50 matches, several game modes (Capture mode where you have to conquer enemy and hold your own flags, and Insurgent mode, where you either defend weapon caches, or destroy them).
Why is this different however? In this game you absolutely have to cooperate with your teammates on a "SQUAD" level. Team is divided into squads of people, 8(?) each. With a single team leader to coordinate squad movement and deployments, however, you can play without one too. Each squad must fill out different player roles in order to be an effective fighting force, medics, AR positions, AA, and AT. Munitions people, etc.
Each team has its own voice channels, no additional software required (local and squad. Squad leaders and commanders get their own too).
But, thats Infantry. Since its Early Access, is is not finished - Vehicles and Aircraft. Both transport and strike.
Development wise, the game have its performance and compatibility issues, but the DEV are working on it. Patches are coming in not as often as one would like - but the patches are big.
Overall, I like this kind of gameplay and execution is well, for EA and now. I would recommend to support this DEV.

It is hard to express how much I love this game. It is easily one of the best games I have ever played. With a unique method for delivering an incredibly compelling story, and puzzles that get harder as you go (and make Portal 2 look like a children's game), the gameplay is definitely good enough on its own, but what really gets you is the resounding effect of the dialog.
This isn't just some puzzle game. It forces you to think. What makes you a person? How can you prove it? Why do you even WANT to be a person? Given a definition of "being", when extrapolated to its extremes, what does that mean? Can a string of tin cans be defined as a 'person', given your definition?
Easily some of the most impactful dialog I've ever experienced in a game, and not just in the MLA sessions. As you explore more of the world, minutia you find along your journey, in the audio logs, or some of the files in the terminals, will reveal the truth behind your world, while simultaneously exposing you to the human side of a calamity. I wish I could say more, but I can't risk spoiling it for you. It is something you have to experience for yourself. This is a game to be perfected, too: pick everything up, find all three endings, and download the DLC (which I'm ~1/3 through).
If you want to think in a way that no game has yet made you think, get this. If you like good puzzle games, get this. If you enjoy games with great stories, get this.

After 19 hours I can say this game is pretty awesome. I would ignore the EA tag as this game fells like anything but an EA title. There are 3 different scenarios to choose from: the standard of 3 people crashing on a planet and trying to survive, the rich explorer on his own looking for adventure, or 5 surviving tribe members trying to rebuild after a catastrophe. If none of those tickle your fancy they have added an editor and you can make up your own scenario (it is pretty epic what you can do).
Once you get everthing set up then you choose a map size and a location on a planet. Make sure to pay attention to the times you can grow crops, you don't want to be stuck somewhere you can only grow crops for a limited amount of time, and also pay attention to the average temps as some people like certain temperatures. After you selcect your planet is when you get to pick your crew of people. I suggest trying to find people without any injuries (scars included), and make sure to be diversified in the peoples abilites. It's funny some of the quirks these peopel have :)
Launch your game and immediately pause so you can scope it out, plan how you want to build and set your people to working. I recommend watching some videos before hand as there is a learning curve, but once you get the basics down it's a ton of fun.
I can see me investing a lot more time into this one for sure. Good luck and have fun!!

When I first played this game, I was about 6 years old. Since I was born outside an English-spoken country, I didn't know much when it comes to scripts and texts written in English.
It occured to me that even though I was six and I didn't know English, the game is easy to learn and hard to master. Down to heart the game never bores me as there is so many strategies you can do. This adds to the complexity of the game, but at the same maintaining a newby-friendly environment.
The first time I got a hold off this game was back in 2004 (when I was literally 3 or something) when our family got our first computer (Windows 95). My father played a series of games back when he did his bachelor's degree. One of them being Age of Empires 2. If I remembered correctly it was the classic game "Age of Empires 2: The Age of Kings" plus the expansion pack "The Conquerors." No matter how nooby I was, I had a lot of fun compared to the other games that he gave me (including Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos and SimCity 2000).
Comparing to the original game plus "the Conquerors" expansion, not much has changed in terms of gameplay. Although obvious to the title "Age of Empires II HD" the graphics were remastered to better suit today's computers and to stay compatible. This of course brings back the nostalgia and good vibes before I got a hold of the remastered edition.
Although the addition of the Steam Workshop and the max population to 500 is nice, it's the same old game with the same campaigns, and the same gameplay/style. The expansion packs/DLCs; "The Forgotten" and "The African Kingdoms" are a nice addition to the game, bringing in new civilisations from other parts of the world.
I rate this game 10/10 in terms of gameplay and strategicness but it might just be bias. Although I have played other RTS games, Age of Empires II will always be the most suiting once you grow into it. And who knows? Maybe in another 8 years the community will still be strong and the game will continue to be remembered as a step to a change in PC gaming for that time.

Squad is in the process of evolving into the pinnacle of milsim FPS'. Even as an alpha, the gameplay and strategic processes involved in a coordinated battle between 72 individuals is as rigorous as any military themed CQC games. As new elements are introduced, such as the recent addition of new maps/and the famed Mod Deuce .50, the tactics previously used in past versions evolve to accomodate these new assets, so every month seems to bring about a new wave of ideas and strategies. New players are met with a new-player friendly game where roles are taken seriously and each individuals main purpose is to support the squad/fire team element to the maximum of their capacity. Whilst other modes highlighting talents of clan vs clan and precision on the battlefield, public games with random individuals who coordinate with each other effectively to win the game leads to a higher satisfaction of teamwork, leading to friends who will challenge you to become better and more effective on comms/gameplay/situational awareness. The graphics are amazing, and albeit the gore of wounds could leave a bit to be desired, the sounds of AK fire snapping overhead is enough for anyone to hit the dirt midsprint. I'd encourage any milsim/FPS aficionado to try Squad, spend a few hours playing each role and getting used to the dynamic of the game before stepping up the plate as a Squad Leader. For more information, find the "JoinSquad" subreddit for up to date news, information, FAQ, and dev responses for a feel of the amazing community behind Squad.

I am one of those guys who run Linux, and try to do everything using it. Yet this game is still a reason for me to dual boot Windows.
Hundreds of players, waging war on four giant open continents. Whether you want to play a sniper, an infantrymen rushing points, or want to jump into one of many different vehicles or planes, this game has got you covered. Planetside makes you feel small, just one soldier in a huge battle. You are not "Hero X" or "The tank of the team". You are just another guy with a gun, no super powers others do not have.
There are a few things to keep in mind though:
1) Most important for new players: This game has a very long and steep learning curve. In your first hours, days, maybe even weeks in the game a lot of people will kill you, easily. This is not because the game is pay to win, as many reviews of people with less than 100 hours in suggest. This is because those players know where to take cover, how to approach and how to aim exactly the way to get all their bullets in your head, instead of spreading half their clip over the wall behind you.
- or if you are more the solitary type, watch videos by people like
that cover the basics of playing this game. You might not need it in other shooters, you will need it here.
2) I said this shortly before already, but I'll say it again: This game is not pay to win. At all. Everything except for some purely cosmetic items can be unlocked through
, which you earn by doing useful stuff (repairing, kills, spotting, basically everything). All weapons can be unlocked through these points. And these points are easy, really easy to get. A focused new engineer can make 1000 cert points in the first 1-3 days of playing. That gets you any gun or upgrade you want.
You want to be engineer or medic for this, usually.
3) Got some certs? Don't just drop them all on a new gun at first, because: Almost all weapons are sidegrades, either all purpose or excelling in a specific situation. New players should upgrade their armor first, and maybe cert into a vehicle after that. Vehicles are fun.
I have currently almost 500 hours in, but am by no measure a pro yet. I'll leave further recommendations to others. My advice is give it a try, watch some tutorials, and maybe I'll run you over on my
someday. Just keep in mind that everything you see a 'pro' do, is something you can do as well. No pay to win, no barriers. Just raw experience.

Developers love calling their latest AAA shooter a "modern shooter with an old-school heart" whenever they can, but usually all they mean is "you can carry more than one gun." They tried saying the same thing with the previous Wolfenstein remake, you know, the one with the god-awful open-world gimmick that made traveling from mission to mission feel like torture.
Surprisingly, The New Order delivers on the old-school feel; it's a very fast-paced game that works better as a run and gun than a cover-shooter. Guns feel unique, varied, and powerful, with interesting secondary firing mechanics that unlock as you play, so you never really find yourself getting bored with the guns you've been using since the opening sequence. Rechargeable health is non-existant, finding hidden caches throughout the map feels both necessary and fun. I've found that the idea that you should reward the players for exploring the nooks and crannies of your map to be a somewhat dated idea in the eyes of the modern developer, so it felt really refreshing to think "I'll bet there's a health upgrade somewhere at the end of that seemingly pointless hallway" and actually being right. Yes, there are a few modern-gaming gimmicks thrown in that feel pretty annoying (don't expect to be free from QTE's) but these moments are infrequent enough that it didn't ruin my experience or make me feel like Machine Games thought I was an idiot. Boss battles are challenging, fun, and unique, and usually involve giant mechs, it's great!
The game never takes itself more seriously than you do: it's cheesy, over the top, ridiculous, and self-aware. The cutscenes are over-dramatic in the best way and BJ gives an entertaining, brooding, almost Max Payne-esque narration of what's happening. I loved it. Think 80's Action B-movies. Dialogue aside, the story also presents itself through collectibles and through the environment itself in the form of recordings, newspaper clippings, etc. that fill you in on the details of how the Nazi's won World War II and successfully took over the world. If you're into alt-history, you'll really appreciate all the detail in the background and the expansive reading material written in order to make this retelling of history feel natural and semi-plausible.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is the latest game in the Wolfenstein series, where you go around and kill high tech Nazi's. Since I wasn't even alive when the first game came out and I got a console that could play any of these games back in 2012, and even if they were around then, I was just too busy replaying GTA5 or the Mass Effect trilogy to pick them up. But I heard the games were fun so I decided to pick up the latest game around the Xmas sale. So what did I think of it? Well, that's the purpose of this review, ain't it? Let's take a look.
STORY: You play as B.J. Blaskowitz, who is not a gay porn star despite what that first name might imply, but is instead a Nazi killing soldier who leads a charge against General Deathshead. However, one of BJ's best men is killed (happens in the first couple minutes so spoiler warning is not needed) and BJ is put in a coma after a head injury. When he wakes up, he finds that the year is 1960, and that Nazi Germany has taken over all of Europe, America, and most, if not all of the world. B.J., after meeting up with a rebel group who plans to overthrow the Reich, goes all across Europe to build up the resistance and overthrow the Nazis and take out Deathshead once and for all. Decent story, has some pretty badass moments, more effort put into it than any Battlefield singleplayer ever, except maybe the Bad Company games.
GAMEPLAY: Usual FPS gameplay. You can carry multiple weapons, and can even dual wield most of the weapons. You get usual pistols and assault rifles, grenades and sniper rifles, stuff like that. You also get a cool laser cutter that you can use to cut chains and later metal plates. Gunplay is pretty fun, enemies can be kind of hard later on, like really hard, but ah well, it's still fun no matter what. It's a linear shoot em up like CoD, but it's better and has more energy to it.
GRAPHICS AND PERFORMANCE: The game looks pretty good. The game has a bunch of cool places, from the London Science Museum that's been Nazified, a work camp in Croatia, and yes, the Nazi moon base, all of those and the other levels look cool. Performance is pretty good, too. Decent enough framerate through out the game, no drops, so I don't think I can complain too much.
CHARACTERS AND VOICE ACTING: B.J is fine, he's really mopey when he does monologues, which is kind of lame, but ah well. There's a Polish nurse that becomes your love interest, she's fine too.  Deathshead is your usual cliche Nazi German bad guy, but that's fine. Kind of disappointed I can't kill Hitler, but ah well. The two guys you choose between save, an Irish guy who's name escapes me and I'm too lazy to look up and an American rookie, are fine, I went with the Irish guy myself. There are a few more decent characters that I'm not gonna get into, but they're for the most part fine. Voice acting is good across the board, cannot complain.
EXTRAS: There really isn't much to do side activity wise. There are some collectables here and there, which are the standard now. There's also an easter egg where you can play the old Wolfenstein game, that's pretty cool. Other than that, not many extras.
FINAL VERDICT: One of my favorites out of 2014. Good fun, not the most impressive or innovative, but it's pretty damn fun. 9/10, pick it up sometime.

Gather around children, Dracathio has a story to tell.
Once upon a time a crazy ginger went on the road with his crazy father, while on the road he came across a demo game on his dad's laptop, titled Age of Empires Demo.  The crazy bored out of his mind ginger figured "hm lets try this" about a week or so later over killed three very unqiue seniors and was so badly wanting to try the other features that were grayed out on the menu screen.  He finally gets home from being on the road and gets the game in gold edition, he beats the senerios and plays them again, and beats them again, he than gets the sequal and does the same dang thing.   He decides to spend hours upon hours messing around with random maps destroying empires that try to build up decently and laughs when the enemy doesn't know how to tower defense because bad programming.  He realizes though he keeps on scratching up the disc's from constant play.
He than gives up on trying to get another copy and moves on with his gaming, over 10 years later he sees a steam summer sale and buys this version and feels the biggest wave of nastalga ever, and that grin from long ago comes across his face once more.
------------------------------------------------
My love for strategy games started with that single demo on my father's laptop, from age of empires i spread across to playing games like Evony, Evony2, Castlelot, Three Kingdoms Online, Age of Kings, Backyard Monsters, Clash of Clans, Civilization 5, and many others I just can't remember.

Max Payne 3 is a fresh look at an older and deflated alchoholic who still finds himself standing over the corpses of innocent women caught in the middle of scandal, greed, and corruption.
Whilst this may not be the comic book stylized flim noir that the earlier two games were this still has all the angst and grit of Max Payne; Now finely ground into a powder that glistens the screen with every motion of the drunken and pill popping tragic hero.
Whats great: Max Payne is Maxed out. You can play the game in four difficulties and still have fun each time. The more challenging difficulties force you to do unorthodox bullet dodging and land headshots almost every time (especially near the end). Easier difficulties allow the joy of lighting up a room full of baddies. Either way the AI stays solid and the bullet prrof vests still work against you. The voice acting by James McCaffrey and his co-stars (specifically Julian Dean) are not only extraordinary but hold the organic feel that rockstar is so well known for. The story whilst very different from the first two games is set ablaze with Tony Scott references the world over based on the flim Man on Fire starring Denzel Washington. The Locations and sequences in every level leave a grand feeling of surviving the worst that Max has ever been through yet. The pacing of the story is slower than most games and demands that you soak in the whole thing. Still if you're not into story mode there is an arcade mode that is unlockable after the stories completion, which is very satisfying.
Whats Annoying: Whilst this game kept the Payne-full essence it does have some new changes that make it feel slightly inconcsistant. First off you may not notice that your bullets fly at light speed in bullet time, hitting your targets without so much as a heat trail whilst in the earlier games your bullets were as projectile based as the enemies you faced. Every once in a while there will be a sequence whether in easy or hard difficulty that isn't done just right and so forces you to redo a small portion of the game many times over. I've had more than a few moments in which I duel weild weapons whilst in corner cover only to have Payne fire one gun around the corner and the other pointing straight up into the air next to his air firing at nothing. It's a very odd thing for a master marksman to do and throws me out of the game every time. I also wish you didn't have to sit through ever cutscene. As awesome as the quality of the game is I shouldnt have to be forced to play through every cutscene to get to my game.
Whats it Worth?: I bought this game full price because I love rockstar and I love the dark and brooding character that is Max Payne. I love that he coinstantly goes through his past and even frinds a way to reinvent the reasons for not eating a bullet. I love the voice acting, the story, and the unique situations that you have to get through. The setting is believable and the gameplay is to die for. I wish there were more cover based 3rd person shooters like this even with it's flaws. It's not hard to appreciate the game and I've played it many times through on steam and PS3.

People used to tell me this was the Battlefield of the poor or cheapskates.
Well, I played Battlefield after this and was so bored that I went right back to Planetside.
It might not look as polished or cool as the new BF titles, but at least it feels like a real war with dozens of players fighting each other in epic three way fights with combined arms (infantry, tanks, aircrafts)
I have spent countless hours in this game fighting over the same bases over and over and it NEVER got boring because every fight is different (unless it is zerged by the enemy, which, admittedly, happens from time to time)
It is a great game with a fair F2P mechanic that only locks cosmetics behind a pay wall. Everything else can be earned with free ingame currency called certs. And while some of the prices may seem way too high, they can all be achieved by setting goals for oneself and work for them. It's also what kept me motivated all the time. To unlock new stuff followed by setting my aims for the next unlock I wanted to achieve.
Truth be told, the game could be better. Updates are sparse, sadly, whether it is regarding new content or mere bug fixes, but at least the game isn't abandoned by the dev team, and the player count isn't declining too rapidly despite the game being quite old by now.
Planetside is a unique MMOFPS shooter that has no competition on the market. Sure, there might be other FPS games around, but none of them truly give you the same mass scale battle feeling like this game does. Until another MMOFPS game emerges on the market, this is the only game there is for it. If you are interested in huge combined arms battles, this is the game for you. Just don't give up right at the start, as the game has quite the learning curve.

Do you dislike CS, COD, BF, etc, because you feel restricted by the maps in them? Do you dislike the arena feel FPS games give you? You need to know the exact best routes, every spot where you can throw a grenade to catch opponents anywhere unaware, all those couple of lanes where the enemy can come from? D you feel boxed in and restricted?
PlanetSide 2 to the rescue! Open world FPS game with (almost) no limitations! Massive battles, as in a couple of hundred foot sloggers wresting for control of just one base! Add in tanks shelling the base or busting each other. Add in support vehicles - sunderer as a battle wagon or a troop carrier, harasser as an agile "jeep" of a kind and ATV! Add in air - fighters, gunships, troop transports! Add in player constructed structures (turrets, walls, bunkers, pillboxes, etc...)! The scale and diversity is mind humbling!
Sure, in the bases (there are dozes of bases on a continent, and there are four continents), there are routes which are most used, but don't get too used to that. Death can come from ANYWHERE. You can be flanked in so many ways. You can be outsmarted in so many ways. You can be killed in so many ways.
You can be sniped from hundreds of meters away. You can be "bombed" or shot by an air vehicle. You can be shelled by a tank - near or far away. You can be jumped on from behind or above by a jet pack using light assault. You can be just stomped on by a max unit - an armed exo-armor for single infantry unit. You can be crept on by a cloaked (light bending cameleoline cloak, making him very hard to see) infiltrator and stabbed! You can be just shot in the face by a shield using heavy assault using his wide arsenal of weapons! You can be blown to bits by C4, frag grenades, sticky grenades, anti vehicle grenades, tank mines, anti infantry mines and god knows what!
You can participate in huge vehicle fights, using main battle tanks or lighter tanks, sunderers, harassers or even ATVs. And you can even use the cortium farming (needed for player constructions) ANT to fight with its array of weapons and special abilities. Or you can just be the lone wolf sniping tanks stealthily! Or use a sunderer to set up spawn points for your empire. Or change the loadout and you have a full blown battle bus, durable and able to deal lots of damage. Andd in another sunderer for repair support and a third for ammo and a couple of more and you'll have sunderer train the enemy fears to face!
You can fight in the air with the fighters - dog fights, squads ruling skies and denying enemy air, doing air to ground runs killing infantry and vehicles alike! Or you can use an agile troop transport, Valkyrie, to set up spawn points for you team mates. Valkyrie is also armed, you can use it for combat and have your team with you, shooting from the rumble seats! Or do a precision drop on an enemy hard point! Or become the whale pilot - run a Galaxy, offering larger transport capacity and having a larger arsenal than the Valkyrie. Transport your squad accross the continent offering mobile spawn point and fire support!
There is just so much to do!
5 infantry classes plus the MAX suit each make gameplay different. Infiltrator, his main perk being the cloak. Light assault using jet pack. Heavy assault has shields and most diverse arsenal of weapons, including tank busting rocket launcher available. Medics specialize in healing and reviving, but also have available to them the most accurate weapon class, the assault rifles. Engineers repair, suply ans support. They also have the turrets they can deploy. Maxes have a much larger health pool than normal infantry and deadlier weapons - they just cost you resources (which regen over time). They are mean fighting machines that can take out full squads when played by skilled players. They can also be killed easily, if they play stupid - a C4 (that a light assault, heavy assault and medic and engineer have access to) will kill them. As will a tank mine. And two anti infantry mines. And grenades, rocket launchers and the engineers special sniper rifle, 'Archer' which is solely designed to kill maxes.
Three empires to choose from, all with different "culture". The New Conglomerate are marked by their slower firing but hard hitting weapons. The Terran Republic philosophy is to put as much lead as possible down the range - fast firing, lighter damage per hit. Vanu Sovereignty uses plasma technology, which has no bullet drop for most weapons. Firing rate and damage is average compared to the NC and TR.
What are you waiting for?
Yeah, right, forgot. You are probably overwhelmed. The learning curve is hard. I mean really hard. There is just so much to learn. Positioning yourself and having awareness of your surroundings is perhaps the most important thing, and that you can learn only by playing. Gunplay is also important, but different than in most of your FPSs. Time To Kill is longer, except of course for some of the one hit kills, like a headshot from a sniper.
Be prepared, you will die a lot. You are the king of CS? Sure, ok. You will still die a lot. There are so many things that can kill you and the attack can come from so many directions that YOU. WILL. DIE. A. LOT.
The game is not Pay to Win, only Pay to Speed Up The Grind. You get exp in the game for many many thing. For each 250 exp you get a Cert, which is the in game currency that is used to unlock weapons, equipment, attachments to weapons, vehicle weapons, everything. You can also buy the unlocks with cash, bypassing the grind. Things that you can get only for cash are only cosmetics. Like camos for your soldier/vehicles, cosmetics for you soldier/vehicles or reskins of base weapons, like golden or black variants of the base weapon that you can buy with certs.
And finally, a starter advice. Stick to the weapons you get for free for some time. They are widely considered the best or most versatile in their classes. Unlock other equipment and attachments to those weapons and only later start looking at other weapons. The other weapons are mostly just sidegrades, offering slightly different profiles and are meant for different situations. Most notable exception are the rocket launchers. Get a A2A lockon launcher. Your default launcher is a dumb fire. And join an Active outfit that also offers training to their members.

Early 2015: I have a low spec desktop and can't play many 3D intensive games. After a long and torrid affair with Prison Architect, a friend tells me RimWorld is sort of like PA in space. It's not. It's better than that.
Unless you've fallen in love with games like PA, you may look at RimWorld and think 'Huh'. 2D top down view, simplistic looking, very basic. True, but that's the beauty of it. It looks simple on the surface, it's a lot more complex underneath. This is, as described, a colony story simulator. You're telling the story, and it will grip you, almost whether you like it or not. Part management sim, part - er - 'sim sim', part base builder and part RTS, RimWorld is the space-born sibling of Dwarf Fortress and Prison Architect. It's given me hundreds and hundreds of hours of fun pre-Steam release, and it has paid for itself many, many times over in fun.
Highly recommended.

When I first played this game, I was about 6 years old. Since I was born outside an English-spoken country, I didn't know much when it comes to scripts and texts written in English.
It occured to me that even though I was six and I didn't know English, the game is easy to learn and hard to master. Down to heart the game never bores me as there is so many strategies you can do. This adds to the complexity of the game, but at the same maintaining a newby-friendly environment.
The first time I got a hold off this game was back in 2004 (when I was literally 3 or something) when our family got our first computer (Windows 95). My father played a series of games back when he did his bachelor's degree. One of them being Age of Empires 2. If I remembered correctly it was the classic game "Age of Empires 2: The Age of Kings" plus the expansion pack "The Conquerors." No matter how nooby I was, I had a lot of fun compared to the other games that he gave me (including Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos and SimCity 2000).
Comparing to the original game plus "the Conquerors" expansion, not much has changed in terms of gameplay. Although obvious to the title "Age of Empires II HD" the graphics were remastered to better suit today's computers and to stay compatible. This of course brings back the nostalgia and good vibes before I got a hold of the remastered edition.
Although the addition of the Steam Workshop and the max population to 500 is nice, it's the same old game with the same campaigns, and the same gameplay/style. The expansion packs/DLCs; "The Forgotten" and "The African Kingdoms" are a nice addition to the game, bringing in new civilisations from other parts of the world.
I rate this game 10/10 in terms of gameplay and strategicness but it might just be bias. Although I have played other RTS games, Age of Empires II will always be the most suiting once you grow into it. And who knows? Maybe in another 8 years the community will still be strong and the game will continue to be remembered as a step to a change in PC gaming for that time.

Rockstar's DRM rates as the worst I've seen in recent years.  If there is a method to play this game's single player modes offline, I haven't been able to find it.  The Rockstar "Social Club" client will sieze the whole game if it has trouble connecting to the internet.  I travel a lot; so I rely on games like these, that have a good single player story, to pass the time.  Oh well.
Finally, the cutscene integration is the real killer of this game.  If your running around with a long gun (like I like to do), everytime there's a short cutscene, the game moves the long gun to your off hand, and puts whatever pistol/machine pistol in your shooting hand.  To makes matters worse, if you already have two handguns, when you try to select the long gun, you DROP it, and then have to face whereever it landed to pick it up, and THEN you can finally start shooting (provided you didn't just give up and start blasting away with whatever lil' peashooter was already in your hand).  Oh, and there's a short cutscene to transition you through just about every stinkin' room/area, so if you spent the time to stockpile your long gun's ammo, nobody cares - you have to do it Rockstar's way.
Go take a long walk off a short cliff, Rockstar.

First off this game is no Call of Duty. So jumping into a game and playing with that mentality will get you killed, ALOT. This game, in my opinion, takes some of the best elements form the Battlefield and ARMA games and blends them beautifully. Working with your squad, and your squad working with other squads on your team is the key to winning.
A minimalistic HUD and no icons really make this game feel more like combat and less like a shoot em up game. And simple to learn controls keep you in the action without having to look up a key map. Even the squad roles are handled nicely, with roles getting handed out in a limited supply per squad. This means that not everyone can get RPG’s or grenade launchers. But that is not a hindrance.
Once you’ve ran around a bit in the firing range it’s time to take on some combat. In a game joining a squad is easy, and after some running a bit the bullets start to fly. At any moment a firefight might break out, and there is no way of knowing how long it will last or what the outcome will be. You’ll find yourself in the heat of the action as bullets wiz by, teammates call out enemy contacts, and downed friends call for medics.
Even the sound design is amazingly done. To the point where you can identify gun shots, where they came from, and what gun fired them. Or my favorite is when you can hear an enemy sneaking up on you, their footsteps getting louder as they get closer. Guns and even voice communications sound different in rooms or hall ways.
The visuals are impressive too. Dust kicks up from bullet hits. Smoke fills areas as grenades go off, and once the dust settles the fight continues. Even watching the movements and animations of soldiers is spot on. A superb ragdoll system means that even watching a soldier go down is strangely satisfying.
10/10 Would recommend.

If you're thinking about playing this game, do it. The game as it is, is beyond your imagination. Although not as well-known nor as pretty as, say, battlefield or arma, but the community and the scale of Planetside 2 will make those AAA game make a run for their money. All in all, to anyone downloading the game, welcome to planetside.
-Battles can go up to (in my experience) several factions with at least 20 vehicles(both air and land) and 100+ players shooting the living daylight out of each other.
-The starter guns are as good as the one in the shop. The different stats make the guns in the shop more suitable for a specific role (CQC, long range engagements,etc)
-The community are supportive and encouraging to new players. There are outfits (essentailly clan) that host ops where noobs and verteran can join. The ops can range from casual plays and party music playing in the comms to Arma style tactics and stragies.
-Although not as fun, you can solo in this game and still have a fun experience. You can either follow other players in tanks, fighters, transporters (both air and land) or as infantry. It's also possible to just snipe people from hundreds of meters away.
-Skills>Money. You can pawn high level players regardless of your level. It's all abot knowing the map layout, game mechanics, and good internet.
-Large map + Traveling = ROAD TRIPS!!! The maps(call continents) are made up of about 25-35 hexes, each as big as a small battlefield map. It's possible to spawn-hop from base to base using the in-game spawn options.
-Battles can be so big that they lag (unless you have a beast computer.)
-It's a game that uses client- side hit detection. So you can have cases where you seemly get insta-gibbed or someone stand there while you shoot half a magazine worth of bullets into them. This rarely happens(usually in large battles) and when it does, only a few millisecond delay.
-Although guns are considered sidegrades, you can use in-game credits to upgrade your class's resistance to bullets (by one bullet per level, max 5) and things like that. The upgrades are minor and only play a large role in engagements between extremely skilled players.
-It's possible to get overpowered by one side. As there are no regulation as to how players can attack a base, brute forcing their way in is allowed. (As someone that have been on both sides, it can be both fun and bring/horrible to be one either side.)
-The TTK(time to kill) is low, at most about .5 of a second. It can be unforgiving for new players as they can die without knowing how.
-Guns and high level class upgrades (most are not needed as much as the previous levels) can cost alot.(It's possible to earn the credits in a few hours of great fights)
The youtube videos can be useful in your decision to play the game. The different outfits and factions(teams that you play as, that have slightly different weapon mechanics) you join can affect your experience.
The community hub on steam can have more information on the game also.

If I remembered correctly it was the classic game "Age of Empires 2: The Age of Kings" plus the expansion pack "The Conquerors." Comparing to the original game plus "the Conquerors" expansion, not much has changed in terms of gameplay. Although obvious to the title "Age of Empires II HD" the graphics were remastered to better suit today's computers and to stay compatible. I rate this game 10/10 in terms of gameplay and strategicness but it might just be bias. Maybe in another 8 years the community will still be strong and the game will continue to be remembered as a step to a change in PC gaming for that time.

At its most basic, RimWorld is a base/colony builder style of game where you are given control over the lives of a group of colonists and try to build functioning new home for them on a harsh rim world. It is your job to see that all of their needs are met ranging from ensuring that they have an adequate food source to ensuring that their moods are kept high to planning and preparing elaborate base defense systems to fight off the many hostiles that seek to bring your colony doom.
But beyond this initial aspect, RimWorld is also a story generator where you can create a wonderfully in-depth story just from what happens in game and a little creativity. You might have a wildly successful colony that has lasted years and years, having fought off countless raids and unfortunate events to build a thriving community in the unlikely of places. Or, your colony might have only survived a few days at the most, having struck down the wrong wall and opened up an ancient mechanoid nest whose inhabitants cruelly exterminated your colonists, ending their hopes and dreams.
RimWorld is a type of game that can bring out the best and worst in you based on your decisions. Will you choose to be a benevolent leader who chooses to aid anyone who comes seeking help or will you be a cruel and efficient tyrant who abuses his prisoners and harvests their organs for profit. It is a type of game that can out your emotions, from anger over the stupidity of one of your colonists to joy from having fought off that enormous raid with no losses to grief as you realized that during another raid, your star colonist had accidentally been shot by his own wife during the chaos and is now nothing more than a vegetable, never to move again and the first to be put on the menu if times get hard.
I won’t deny that RimWorld can be a tough game at first to get into, one that seems that no matter what you do, you always end up failing in the end. Don’t fret and just keep at it and eventually, you’ll find a breakthrough and finally win for once … only to fall 5 minutes later when another tragedy strikes. This is game where you measure your victories in how far that you’ve managed to come each and everytime, where you’ll discover that you can enjoy failing whent hat failure did not come until after you’ve broken a personal milestone, having survived however many days or done what you’ve set your eyes upon.
And if you’ve managed to beat the best that the vanilla game has set upon you, then there is always the deeper world of mods in RimWorld to add new challenges for you to face or new ways that you can play this game, adding in countless hours of replayability. It is just a fantastic game that you will spend hours and hours on. If you are still unsure, watch some Let’s Plays on YouTube or streams on Twitch of the game and decide for yourself if you really want to join the rest of us in RimWorld and never, ever escape it.

In dirty bomb you dont pick your guns or perks they are premade cards that you get. and to get them you can either get them by buying them (ill get to that later.) getting a case at the end of a game that you can open to get a random card. Or by crafting them. To craft cards you have to have shards, and you get these by recycling cards you dont want. The rarer the card the more it requires. So your thinking at this point "Okay that makes so whats wrong with it." well to craft a card you have to two things: shards and the ingame currency. I forgot to mention this but the card rarity starts at default, iron, lead, bronze, silver, gold, and cobalt. (And a few special edition ones from companies and diffrent events in game.) Not only that but the only diffrence between the lowest card that is good to get at the start is bronze to cobalt is the color of there clothes and gun. What's to say about this game..... Alot.
You'll need a decent PC to run this game. (I know it says I played this game very little, but I have over 1000 hours under my belt.)
With all the cheap feeling ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t from each of the three factions when on the receiving end, I feel the need to warn you that you will die. ALOT.
But the BS is fun. It's easily countered, and usually requires some amount of skill to play. (So you buying said weapon is a bad idea off the bat.)
Play in either medium fights, or large ones. Small fights only with backup, or else you'll die to the Elite PS2 players, who can take bases by themselves.
All guns are sidegrades. Test the in VR Training, and start on Koltyr at first. Trial your preferred weapons so you get a feel, then buy them when you thin,k you got the hang of it. Remember, some of the better weapons are default. Most other weapons specialize or fill a niche.
Love your classes! Each one specializes in a certain thing, and each has a weakness. Upgrade their abilities so you stand a fighting chance against the enemy! And don't forget C4, medkits, Proximity mines, or the wonderful selection of grenades!
This goes for vehicles and their weapons too! You can get a cloaked ATV for some roadkills, or one with a shotgun and turbo for closing that gap between you and the enemy! Maybe a tank with flak cannons, or High-explosive rounds with extra protection from C4! Perhaps a Fighter plane, with lock on Air to Air missiles to be the troll of the skies, or with Anti-Personnel guns and Stealth Modules, for assasinating large groups of enemies!
Customization? Sure! Would you like Giraffe Camo, or Hot Pink, maybe Soccer Balls? Jason Vorhee's mask, or Stormtrooper?
Turn your Light Tank into a Abrams! Turn your Jeep into a Warthog! Decorate your Gunship for that dread-bringing look!
Pay to Win? NAH! Membership grants a XP boost, a small amount of ingame cash each month, and access to daily membership offers! All of this you still get with out paying a nickel!
Battles never end, they just move. 4 main continents; Snow-filled Esamir, the jungles of Hossin, the Desert know as Indar, and the grasslands of Amerish. Get 20 Victory Points(VP) and you lock a continent down. Do so, and you get a sweet bonus.
Each continent has dozens of bases, with 3 major facilites: Tech plants for spawning Heavy Tanks, Amp Stations for Cooldown redction on turrets, and Biolabs, for Passive Health Regeneration. These are hard to take, so bring your A-game!
Wanna talk with other people? Join an Outfit! Most will have dedicated Leaders to organize into Squads and Platoons, which hold 12 and 48 respectively. Play with your friends, and get more XP, too!
An Acheivement Hunter? Directives will love you! There's one for pretty much everything, from kills as a certain class, or doing specific things, like seasonal events! Challenging and Long, these will make you cry as you realize you're not good enough to out-snipe snipers from 70+ meters! HAHAAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAH
Anyway.
There are rewards for each kind of player, for the assassin to the run-and-gun types. Each massive acconmplishment of finishing a Directive nets you a unique weapon, camo, or customization option! Each Directive Weapon is unique, with a playstyle to suit the majority of players!
Still here? Good! IT means you're interested!
Here's the last few things.:
Three factions.
New Conglomerate. Heavy hitting. Slow. Shotguns. Juggernauts. Shotguns on Juggernauts. Shot guns on Planes. Freedom. SHOTGUNS ON EVERYTHING!
Terran Republic. Fast. Lots of Bullets. Miniguns. Order. Facist. Communist. Double Barrel Tank. USSR. Terminator with dual Miniguns.
Vanu Soveriegnty. Bill Nye. Lasers. Plasma. Little Bullet Drop. Accurate. Latex. Hover Tank. Butts. Robo Cop with lasers.

I really don't know what to say about this game that hasn't been said by the other negative reviews before me. What started off as an incredibly interesting, and entertaining experience turned sour about half-way through, when the puzzles suddenly stopped being fun and innovative, and started being the same-old same-old force-fed to you in a slightly rearranged fashion.
The computer terminal started out interesting, and I always looked forward to talking with it, but as the conversations went on, it twisted my words more and more, to the point where the end results were unrecognisable as a proper conversation. I don't know if that was the original intention or not, but speaking with it became more of a chore than anything, knowing that you were only going to be interrogated at length about something you'd never even said.
The only thing I still enjoyed by the end of the game was the fact that I could still stop and say "wow" at the stunning visuals, when I was presented a new location. Everything else had long overstayed its welcome.
Like many others, I was drawn by the hype, and the promise that this game was the next Portal, that it was going to blow my mind with the story, and the amazing puzzle elements. Quite frankly, I was underwhelmed, and part of that may have been the excess of hype, building my expectations to an unrealistic degree, but I feel like I would still have left this experience more frustrated than satisfied, especially if I'd paid the full $40 asking price.

is hard.
It's absolutely amazing as a puzzle game, though. It uses a fairly small amount of mechanics which are easy to understand, but they're combined into a series of varied puzzles that will challenge you greatly. You'll constantly keep learning new tricks and you'll frequently get stuck as the game keeps bringing new puzzle elements or sometimes red herrings designed to mislead you in solving the puzzles, and mechanics that you once thought are an obstacle become a part of the solution.
But if there's one thing that
really excels at, it's the environment design. Puzzles are seamlessly spread among ancient ruins, pyramids, castles and forests, and several individual puzzles are always a part of one map that requires you to combine elements from multiple sections of the map for bonus objectives. It isn't just a great puzzle game, it also looks gorgeous.
The game has a rather philosophical storyline, which you might choose to ignore and simply focus on the puzzles, or you might revel in it by reading all the emails, excerpts of literary works and other messages which you can access in the numerous computer terminals throughout the game. In the end, this is entirely up to you.
If you liked the base game, the
DLC is a perfect expansion of the game, featuring even more fiendish puzzles, more striking landscapes and an arguably more interesting storyline.

I like this game, but think the developer has spent too long creating the theory, but not actually playing his game. In 60 in-game days I've had 3 solar eclipses, +7 raids, a volcanic winter (no crops, winter conditions), +4 electrical shorts (broken equipment, fire) and various other problems arise -- all on the "easy" setting. Feels like I had set the game to a "hurt me plenty" playmode, but in reality the percentages are correct according to their wikipedia -- 9% chance for an enemy raid, 5% mad animal, 3% for cold snap or heat wave, 1.2% short circuit/fire (so I had 3 in 60days, wtf?). I don't know if the RNG is busted or if these event-checks are being triggered hourly in game but you're never given a chance to "play" before something bursts into flames or your crops die.
I'm absolutely for hard gameplay, but without a proper tutorial or basic ramping of difficulty this game is pretty unplayable in its current state without some editing through mods or later versions.
And not necessarily a negative, but I would not be surprised if this game is a rip from Prison Architect.  Simple enough style, extremely similar sprites ... and a disturbing feeling that it's just a mod of PA.

Planetside 2 is a remarkable game for its time, having been out for a number of years now, and the developers are still updating it and coming out with new stuff all the time. Planetside 2 is a large scale warfare game where thousands of players choose between three factions, NC (New Conglemerate) VS (Vanu Soveriegnty) TR (Terran Republic) and fight on four continents, plus a small continent for new players, so techinically five. Its got great graphics, especially because of the sheer size of the game, the continents, and numer of players, its rediculous how they managed it, but its amazing.
Unlike many typicall popular FPS's of today, instead of being a run and gun game, its a tactical warfare game about capturing territory and securing victory points to conquer the continents in the name of your faction. It may include shooting as many people as you want, but at the same time, you capture points to capture bases, and then defend and attack, all over the continents, every gameplay session is new and exciting because of the masive amounts of change that can occur while you're offline. Its not for everybody, but once you get a firm idea of what to do, its extremely fun, even if you dont know what to do, getting crazy and doing stupid things can still be fun.
One of my favorite parts is definitely joining an outfit, and fighting in a functioning squad and platoon. The community is extremely friendly, with everyone looking to have fun. No salty people screaming at you over the mics. There is nothing like participating in a battle with 200 other players in a small area of the map with your sqaud leader giving directions and leading your squad or platoon to success. If you like close teamwork and territorial conquest as well as shooting as many people as you want in a never ending supply, or eeven doing whatever you want on your own without someone telling you what to do, this game is for you. Good Luck and Have Fun.

After completing Wolfenstein : The New Order and unlocking every single achievement in a little over 20 hours, I can only honestly conclude:  It’s a kickass game !

A rather long, never dull and very enjoyable single player campaign with great variety (12 to 15 solid hours long, much more if you enjoy reading and looking around for collectibles or crank up the difficulty to ‘Uber’, plus the game really encourages a second play through); a surreal, albeit surprisingly good story, filled with smart flowing dialogue and intelligently written characters; incredibly violent, borderline neurotic and ultimately stellar gunplay; a seamless and simple stealth mechanic that does not seem forced and manages to make failure fun (You’re busted ? No problem ! Time to dual-wield those shotguns!); exceptionally tight controls, that perfectly merge everything that was right with the brutality and speed of old school shooters with the accessibility and smoothness of a modern day one; overall great sound design (the actors deliver their lines believably and naturally, the music is just brilliant and cannot be overstated and the loudness of explosions and bullets tearing through Nazis is pitch perfect); graphically sound, both artistically and technically, and the game just keeps on getting more beautiful throughout your progress (The Id Tech 5 engine has its issues, notably texture pop-up and rendering glitches, but it still manages to produce quite an amazing looking game).. to make things short, it's quite the list of qualities.
Furthermore and similarly to Bioshock, the game is completely devoid of multiplayer modes and is a single player only trip, going against today's standards of tacked on, low quality and utterly unnecessary multiplayer modes that often feel like an afterthought to try and sell map packs DLCs, rather than a meaningful way to add to the experience.  Which is a very big plus in my book.
So from where I stand, Wolfenstein: The New Order is the epitome, the very essence of what an FPS should be, a heartfelt tribute to a whole generation of old school and incredibly fun shooters like Doom, Quake and Half-Life and brings us back to a time where the single player experience was important and satisfying.

Max payne III fails mostly visually and mechanically.
Narratively it suceeds in the similar hard boiled vein of its precusor (and the voice acting by the veteran protagonist is brilliant as always), but the visuals and mechanics break immersion so completely that it just feels like an arcady shooter. I utterly disliked what they did to it.
Visuals:

After completing Wolfenstein : The New Order and unlocking every single achievement in a little over 20 hours, I can only honestly conclude:  It’s a kickass game !

A rather long, never dull and very enjoyable single player campaign with great variety (12 to 15 solid hours long, much more if you enjoy reading and looking around for collectibles or crank up the difficulty to ‘Uber’, plus the game really encourages a second play through); a surreal, albeit surprisingly good story, filled with smart flowing dialogue and intelligently written characters; incredibly violent, borderline neurotic and ultimately stellar gunplay; a seamless and simple stealth mechanic that does not seem forced and manages to make failure fun (You’re busted ? No problem ! Time to dual-wield those shotguns!); exceptionally tight controls, that perfectly merge everything that was right with the brutality and speed of old school shooters with the accessibility and smoothness of a modern day one; overall great sound design (the actors deliver their lines believably and naturally, the music is just brilliant and cannot be overstated and the loudness of explosions and bullets tearing through Nazis is pitch perfect); graphically sound, both artistically and technically, and the game just keeps on getting more beautiful throughout your progress (The Id Tech 5 engine has its issues, notably texture pop-up and rendering glitches, but it still manages to produce quite an amazing looking game).. to make things short, it's quite the list of qualities.
Furthermore and similarly to Bioshock, the game is completely devoid of multiplayer modes and is a single player only trip, going against today's standards of tacked on, low quality and utterly unnecessary multiplayer modes that often feel like an afterthought to try and sell map packs DLCs, rather than a meaningful way to add to the experience.  Which is a very big plus in my book.
So from where I stand, Wolfenstein: The New Order is the epitome, the very essence of what an FPS should be, a heartfelt tribute to a whole generation of old school and incredibly fun shooters like Doom, Quake and Half-Life and brings us back to a time where the single player experience was important and satisfying.

Dirty bomb, a F2P brilliant FPS.
Mixture between Team Fortress 2 and CSGO, yet unique in its own way. Dirty bomb is one of the best free to play shooters on steam, with dev support and constant updates. However, devs may be good, they do a really poor job advertising the game. The game has so much potential but no not too many players. Theres enough people to play with but community still feels shallow. There is a lot of content and many mercs to be unlocked. Some people might say "yOu hAvE to GRiNd tOO mUCH", but no. You can learn one merc while collecting credits for the next one! Now you can boost your progress buy buying the mercs with real currency, although this gives you no advantage over free to play users, you can be OP in this game without spending a dime! This game has its problems, but it's definitively not over the content or the balance. Its the optimization. A low end pc can run this game 1920x1080 with 60 FPS, but with some real quality degradations using FPS configs.. Also main menu lag, its horrible, menu ( in some pc hardware configurations ) is so laggy it hurts my brains. Devs blame this on older graphics being unoptimised, but they are working to fix it. Here's a list of pros and cons:
Pros
+ Much content
+ Well optimized networking with no lag
+ A perfect F2P scheme, with no pay to win.
+ Constant updates and the Devs listen to the community.
+ Tradeable skins soon to be added?!
+ You can get a new merc every 5-7 days of playing the game ( atleast 2h a day ).
+ Mercs are funny and have excellent models and voice lines.
Cons
- Poor optimization in both menu and in-game ( Only for low-end PC's, high-end run the game easily! )
- Not enough players, poor advertising.
Conclusion, give this game a shot. It will stun you how amazing and superb it is. With many mercs and fun to have, you will never be bored. And tell your friend about Dirty Bomb too!
