Over all i loved the gameplay, you can choose to play using stealth cover based or guns plazing wich is nicely complimented with skill trees that level up by compleeting tasks like get 10 stealth kills for example.
Some of them however force you to play in a way you would absolutely not do on your own for the sake of leveling up a skill to allow you to play like you want.
Also most of them is dependant on what weapons you have and the situation you are presented with.
For example if you want to lvl up stelth you may need a certain amount of throwing knife kills while in stealth and if you are at a part of the game where alarms that is imposible and the game sometimes decides what weapons you are going to have and you might not have acces to the specific weapon that you need to upgrade that skill tree.
Also there are moments where you are forced to play either stealthy of gun and run and if you spent all the time leaveling the oposite skills the difficulty at those times will be a lot harder.
But guns feel good enemies are stupid and there is plenty enough weapons to keep you entertained with them through out the game.
On the hardest difficulty it was actually verry difficult at times wich i love becasue i like a challange but it also has lower difficulties wich should be easy enough even for begginers i think.
Also how many excuses can they come up with for all your weapons to be removed!
Graphics however is a hit and miss.
It is realy obviously a console port with a lot of limmited settings.
It manages to look good enough to not be bothering to me and with a miner install of flawless widescreen it even ran smoothly on my tripple monitor setup.
However the most annoying thing with the game was the deapth of field.
Normaly dof in games are just a bit annoying but i can see how it makes those games look better when you can not turn up the aa but in this game it is rediculus i mean most of the fights are done in close quarters but the dof is so strong you can not see anything while you are standing in one room looking into the next room through a door.
Fortunately you can turn dof of by opeaning the command console and typing a code.
Press the ctrl key and the tild key at the same time to bring up the console then write: cvradd r_postprocessdofmode -3
then pross enter and it should fix it but you will have to do that every time you start the game if you don´t want to change a bunch of stuff in the ini file and stuff.
Also some stuff in the game is just a flat texture wich is fine because it will keep the game from being to demanding wich is good but they just chose some bad stuff to make like that.
Some stuff like cigarettes and junk on a table that you have to go up to and pick something up from for the story which makes the character bend forward and take a close look at the table.
The story is ok but the things bj says when he is reflecting on the situation is just bad.

It pains me (no pun intended) to say this, especially as a long time fan of the Max Payne series, but this game dropped the ball in a very big way. Gone is the introspective noir-tinged story of an undercover cop fighting the mob to redeem his past. Welcome a drunken, slovenly, constantly whining, fat, bald reprobate who isn't interested in redemption so much as money so he can support his various habits. Max isn't interesting as a man whose completely abandoned hope, and throughout the story supposedly he claws his way back up to seeing some kind of light, but the game doesn't give him any opportunities to do this with spontaniety. He just awkwardly slouches from suicidal to begrudgingly hopeful.
Apart from the story the game play is terrible. Max Payne 1 and 2 had the notion of a bullet ballet with Max executing daring leaps through space, bullet dodging by inches, and blasting away in beautiful style at his many foes as they rushed him. Now all the enemies snipe him from a distance making bullet time nearly useless. Gone is the style as you end up spastically flailing in bursts and starts just to stay alive long enough to get in a random headshot so that the encounter can end and you can focus on downing painkillers. Instead of molotov cocktails and rocket launchers like previous games Max is limited to a 'realistic' but boring collection of interchangable firearms and grenades that seem to fly wherever they feel like. Throughout this depressing, stressful, galling experience is felt like someone slapped the name of one of my favorite franchises onto a third person Call of Duty like game (endless waves of faceless bad guys, 'realism' draining out all sense of fun, cluttered slums serving as linear battle ground arenas...etc) and tried to awkwardly shoehorn in bullet time as well. Don't expect any meaningful tie-backs to previous Max Payne games either. If anything the game seems to go out of it's way to retcon the previous games and stains their legacy by making Max's complex issues one dimensional and making his world seem smaller and less dramatic.
Avoid this game if you're a fan of if you're not. The heart and soul is gone even if the voice actor remains.

What is there to say?
It's a software that does its job, and it does it well.
You can either create your own animated wallpaper, use one of the preset ones, or browse Steam workshop for downloading  any wallpaper. Creating one can be just as easy as recording a part of a video/game, saving it, and then using it as a wallpaper through this engine.
Don't worry about the performance drops, I'm using this on a low-tier laptop and I've never noticed any performance drop at  all, no matter what I was doing. It must be so minor if I follow the logic that there should be some performance drop because those still are animated wallpapers, but really so minor that one won't notice at all.
You can also change the wallpaper motion speed and add music to the wallpapers.

I cannot recomend this game highly enough. I have spent most of my time playing the offline version (before it came to steam) and I cannot even begin to think how many hours I have played in total and will play in the new steam version.
Even back multiple versions ago the game was still worth the price. With alpha 14, and more updates definitly planned, I could not be more excited to see what other both simaltaneously hilarious and also depressing moments will be crafted out of this masterpeice of a game. Don't be fooled by the "Early Access" label because even if this game was released tomorrow in its current state I would still hapily buy it and get every penny's worth of play time.
I know people often compare it to Dwarf Fortress, and many say the former is a better game, but it cannot be entirely compared. DF focusses on a much larger scale with less micro-management after a certain point and the game almost runs itself. With RW however, you cannot ever be
prepared for every situation the game throws at you. The storyteller AI, random generation of events, and even small little detail changesto your colonists can drestically change the approach needed to combat an evernt. Control is also much more fine tuned, meaning keeping an eye on all of your colonists (only between 1 and 15 at a push for the most you could reliably control and support) is critical to adapting to the world around you. As people change, the world chnanges and events change you will contstantly be adapting both your colonists roles and the styke you approach obsticles. A simple "Do this instead of this" is far from what is required.
Although a full and extensive tututial is lacking, as more hints are given as you play and discover features and mechanics, there is some beauty in the trial and error of colonies that result in some hilarous failure situations that provide huge learning experiences.
Again, I could not recomend this game highly enough and I am stoked to see what is next in store for it.

This game is a good fps shooter.
The negative review is mostly because it's overhyped.
This review is not gonna take in consideration the horrible port.
This is what happens when you lower the fps standards so much when a decent/good fps comes out it's 9/10 and game of the year, let's be honest and imagine this game coming out in the 00's, nobody would remember it.
Let me start with the good parts: the shooting is top notch, the feeling and sounds of the weapons is spot on, the dual wielding is good but i would have preferred more variety of weapons instead of that. The story and the settings are really original and the level design is also good.
But this game has also many problems: the stealth mechanics are flat out wrong, they don't fit with the difficulty of the game and they are badly implemented ( why are throwing knives there when the silenced pistol is more efficient in everything ? ), the sneakings are whay too easy expecially if right after that the game challenges you with hard shooting sections. The game has secrets and unlockables you have to find around the map like the old style fps's, but guess what ? they are all listed on the map, you just open the map and see where all these "secrets" are located, makes it really difficult to find them right ? ...  Lastly this game has an upgrade system based on achievements, it means it unlocks skills based on stuff like "kill 5 enemies while sliding on the ground" and "stealth kill 3 enemies while you have more hp than the max", this forces you to play in ways you wouldn't want to, it's a perfect example that wanting to be original and inovate doesn't always work ( and this comes from a person that absolutely dislike rpg-like upgrade systems in pure fps's ).
This game has its pros and cons, do the pros outweight the cons ? yes, but barely.

Solid team based F2P FPS, tight gameplay. There has been worry about the game being pay to win and I don't think that's true. Rarer loadouts for characters are cosmetic only and can yield the same perks as a bronze or silver loadout.
PROS
- Characters: I am fond of the characters not only because each has unique abilities, but also because I feel like their personalities shine through. The character profiles give a quick summary of the character's abilities and persoanlity, and the one-liners and such during play I think add to it. Plus, there's a nice amount of characters to pick from as well provided you buy them with in game currency or real cash.
- Gameplay. Tight FPS mechanics. It doesn't feel floaty or sluggish, and hit boxes make sense. Each character is limited to certain weapons though so that's something to keep in mind. You can't just equip any weapon to any character.
CONS
- It's F2P. That's not inherently bad though. You can buy any character with in game currency and you can also buy standard unlock cases with in game currency. My issue is that it seems like earning in game currency gets more and more time consuming as you gain more. For example as I apporach 50,000 in game currency that rate that I earn the gold from matches seems to dramatically slow down. I understand why they're doing it, it's just annoying to me. on your road to 20,000 gold you could earn some decent gold at the end for doing really well, but at about 40,000 or so gold you earn less in matches for doing just as good. Just seems a bit inconsistent in order for them to benefit from you maybe getting impatient.
- Recycling loadouts: It feels like they've changed the method of recycling your more common loadouts in order to get higher rarity ones often. I would imagine it could be due to it being a bit less of a hassle (but still kind of a hassle) to get higher rarity cards by trading in your more common ones. It seems like they have changed it every now and then in order to make it a bit more tedious and time consuming to get a higher rarity loadout and maybe entice people to buy with real money. Again, just something I've noticed.
- Maps: There are just not as many maps as I'd like to see. Most are fun to play on whether your attacking or defending an objective, but I'd just like to see more.

As you can see, I never write reviews, but... Rimworld.
Started out: aw this is easy, let me just build whatever the he-- get raided by 2 lame dudes, we survive then one colonist dies from infection. Okay... lets try that again.
Second try: we die of heatstroke.
Third try: doing pretty good, get raided... doctor dies by crossfire, infection kills last two.
I am on my fourth try and despite losing a colonist, I'm up to five colonists, over a dozen raiders killed, building up supplies right now, but a forest fire got out of control, on our way back I thought it would be a good idea to do some hunting, cross fired into a warg, the warg downed two guys, killed the warg, hauled them back and now we're trying to get them to recover from massive blood loss, one has an eye missing, no finger, the other is missing his nose.
Does this seem bad? Yes, they might die and we might have to bury them and periodically visit their little graves and weep, but it's so ♥♥♥♥ing fun. It's probably one of the most challenging, simple, but yet complicated games I've ever played in my entire life, I have no idea how I'll survive if someone comes with a rocket launcher. I will say, I'm usually an FPS player and I cannot stop playing this game. It's so creative and enjoyable, heat stroke and all. I wish the maps were a little bigger cause I'm running out of supplies and I've been unlucky with no Researcher, but everything is spontaneous, proceduraly generated and perfect. I'll probably lose this colony I've legit spent days to build and I'll be sad because of a spoiler I will not name that ♥♥♥♥ed me up once already, but that's what makes it fun: to see how long you can survive.
I hope they keep adding things to the game, such as furniture and random things.

This game took me about 17 hours to beat.
If you don't dislike puzzle games (or you know you like puzzle games), this game is a must have. For example, if you liked the core gameplay of Portal or Portal 2, you'll probably really like this game. I actually enjoyed this game a great deal more than the Portal games.
The key things I liked about this game were the consistency and fun of the actual puzzles and the writing and the story as revealed by the consoles and other various elements.
It feels like they put lots of effort into making sure the puzzles were more than just - here's some crap strewn about, now solve it. They do clever tricks to help lead you in the right direction and help you keep track of the state of a puzzle. Many puzzles have multiple solutions.
As far as the writing, it feels intelligent in a way that, disapointingly, not many other games achieve. I'm usually disappointed by games in which I discover a plot hole or I notice that the human characters (in a realistic setting) are behaving in a way that people don't actually behave or when they hand-wave to create contrived scenes, etc...basically, when it feels like the writer is not smarter or more knowledgeable than me about something and therefore doesn't have anything interesting to offer. This game manages to avoid those sorts of things (just what you'd expect from the person who wrote The Swapper), and I always felt like I was actually getting something out of the story as I made my way through. Just don't make the mistake of thinking that the Library Assistant is the mouthpiece of the writer - you might get frustrated with how they argue with you while simultaneously not giving you sufficient dialog options to respond.
Also, this is a huge point - they have options SPECIFICALLY for countering motion sickness. I consider a game pretty much ruined if, regardless of how fun the gameplay is, it makes me feel sick. It's just not possible for me to enjoy an experience like that (I'm looking at you, Antechamber and Ether One).
As far as criticisms:
It's not immediately obvious that you can reload your save after getting one of the endings so you can try to get other endings or mess around. You might mistakenly believe that you have to re-play the entire game. And, worst of all, because of how the "restore backup" feature works, you might end up playing a bit after getting one of the endings only to find you can no longer reload your pre-ending save because it gets overwritten after awhile. Don't make somebody lose all of their progress without warning them.
I didn't spend much time going after them, but SOME of the stars are, in my opinion, more tedious than fun. I don't like puzzles that involve searching through a big map for things and having to carry junk all over. Grabbing something and moving it to a new location is fine when there's a small area, but for some of the stars you have to do this over a very large area. Also, I certainly like the visuals of the world, but I don't appreciate being asked to scour every inch of the large map to find the location of a star. At that point I'd rather play a more stimulating game. It's the sort of thing that might be enjoyable if this was one of your only games, but in the context of having a large game collection and also some small semblance of a life, it's a hard sell to ask me to spend my time doing that.
I really like the idea of the recorder tool, but, in practice, it's unpleasant to work with when compared to other tools. My main issue with it is having to sit there and wait while making a recording, and having to re-record completely once playback is finished. I wished there was a way to "pause" the recording so I wouldn't have to make a guess as I was recording about how long I should wait in a given spot. The puzzles that involve using the recorder are really fun and novel to think about and rewarding to solve, I just wish that I had more control over it. It's easy to simply throw down a jammer and throw down a connector and see where you should go from there, but it's not so easy or fun to just hit the record button and then sit there for 30 seconds, hoping you're leaving enough time for your solution.
It's also harder to "figure out as you go" when working with the recorder. All the other tools are really easy to interact with so you can experiment and play around until an idea for a solution strikes you, but with the recorder it's annoying to "experiment" because you have to keep re-recording.
Anyway, overall, it's my new favorite puzzle game and I highly recommend it to anyone that doesn't dislike puzzle games.

Step back into the world of Max Payne in this third installment of the slow motion, first person shooter based on the legendary Max Payne as he takes down gangs and kills rogue policemen faster than cholesterol, and as always, between sessions of blackout drunkenness and doses of regret and shame on his past failures.
Now, to the brass tacks:
1. Graphics: All round well optimized. Bullet physics, destructible environment, excellent decals, visuals and character animations stand out extremely well. The game engine used is also light on resources, and any moden mid-range PC should be able to handle this title on High to Ultra settings. Make sure you have at least a Quad Core CPU and a recent mid-range NVIDIA/AMD GPU to enjoy this title.
2. Story: This third installment will take you through Max Payne's intriguing past through flashbacks as a medium, betrayal and strife are at an all time high and Payne's dissent towards the rich and his indifference to these he considers irrelevant to his character enhances one's perception of the characters and how they're built up in the story. His witty, often sarcastic comments on situations lightens up the terse, nondescript nature of some characters in a manner that draws your attention to them. Big win, Rockstar. The acting is also Gold here.
3. Gameplay: The slew of stealth, gunplay, physics, a destructible environment clad in an almost linear, open and vast world shows this game's capacity to deliver an underrated title beyond expectations. This is one aspect most reviewers here overlook. Sure, most mechanics (such as bullet time) have been reused, and to the same tune, vastly improved compared to the predesessors. Quick Time Events (QTEs) are few  and in-between, and have been used excellently, only where needed, unlike some titles that overuse and abuse QTEs. Highly appreciated.
4. Game stability: Thanks to Rockstar's infuriating and nauseating DRM built into the Rockstar client (that anally insists on logging on to your profile even when you're offline), this game's stability is severely compomised on newer platforms such as Windows 8.1 and Windows 10. Once again, courtesy of the infamous Rockstar DRM service that's econd to Uplay in it's anal stability and nagging behavior. Overlook that and you've got yourself a solid contender to the best Max Payne game out there.
Overall rating: Excellent, 9.0/10.
Notes: Buy this in a steam sale.
An old game that's still worth burning hours on.

The Talos Principle has opened my third eye to levels of enlightenment which I might have never experienced had I not played it. I feel like my brain has literally leveled up, xp which I will retain through life instead of forgotten in a save file in my graveyard of games I'll probably never play again. I'm bored of mindlessly killing things, grinding, sinking hundreds of hours into the same old gaming mechanics. I don't care how elaborate a skill tree can get, "First Person Killers" have saturated the gaming market, and not enough of them have story lines that mesh in an unpredictable way with the base objective of the game: Kill stuff, level up, talk to an NPC, kill more stuff, major storyline cutscene, repeat x30, you win. And I'm not just a gamer who plays things on easy, I always start with maximum difficulty so I can experience every game in the most real-world way possible.
I think this is one of those games that will steer many more people, and hopefully smart developers in turn, into types of games that make you think critically, problem solve, and maybe take a 5 minute break to delve into immersive text-based mediums. I have never seen text blended so beautifully into a storyline, where it isn't just supplimental lore, where it figuratively blew my mind. The text was about a third of the game in my opinion, I'm a moderate book reader but have never been in this much anticipation to read every line of text I came across in the game world.

First off, the history of Robocraft is a pretty rough one, with certain patches completely changing the game and its main selling point. Many negative reviews you read are from veterans who feel the game is no longer what they used to love, which is absolutely okay, but don't let it sway your opinion on this game; you should try it for yourself and see whether you like this game or not.
With that aside, I have to disclaim that I am not a veteran, as such I joined the game after the major patches, and I tell you confidently, Robocraft is one of the few games that immediately attract me to its beauty and is worth playing over and over again. That being said, the beauty in the game lies in being able to create your own robot and test it in combat.
If you're not into building robots, fret not, as there is a Community Robot Factory (CRF) where you can buy user-uploaded robots using either items you have in your inventory, or using virtual currency called "Robits" which can be earned by recycling parts you get at the end of every match, getting people to buy your robot on the CRF, or at the end of every month if you're part of an active clan. However, the thrill of blowing robots up does wear off after time, which puts you into the next phase of building robots for the most part instead of fighting with it. However, don't feel put off by this as personally at 125 hours I'm still thoroughly enjoying blowing robots up due to the diversity of Robocraft's Robots. Like flying? Buy or create a plane, helicopter or drone. Like driving? Buy or create a cruiser. Like towering mechs? Buy or create a mech or sprinter. Like being a futuristic robot? Buy or create a hover. These examples are just the tip of the iceberg of what you can potentially create in Robocraft; hybrids are a viable option too.
The combat aspect is also one area where Robocraft shines in, you can pick from SMGs, Plasma launchers, Railguns, Nano-healers, Anti-Aircraft flak, missile launchers, gatling guns, shotguns and tesla blades. You can also choose modules which grant you powers such as teleportation, invisibility, shields and EMP, albeit at a heavy cost. Being in combat is also extremely rewarding when you land a critical shot that tears your opponent in half, literally.
You may be skeptical of my review due to the sheer number of negative reviews, but trust me, give this game an hour or two, you never know what you can get out of this game :)
Tl;dr - If you like building bots and destroying other bots with it, get Robocraft.

TL;DR Highest recommendation!
A more in-depth review below.
So, what makes this game so good, and why are so many people praising it?
It's everything, really.
I don't play puzzle games, so I can't compare Talos with, say, Portal, but I can say that the puzzles are very good.  They range from easy to really complicated, though I must admit I was a bit disappointed with the pacing - even in  late game some of the puzzles were just a little bit too easy. The puzzles overall weren't that hard for the most part, and I would have prefered to have more of those really difficult and complicated ones.
But what I really enjoyed about the puzzles, is the design. They are well thought out (although, perhaps, it's more obvious if you solve the star puzzles - the more difficult and complicated ones). I also very much enjoyed how there were quite a few different tools and how one could use them in various ways, even interconnect them - the game gave me a chance to experiment.
I love the game's esthetic. The music is other worldly and fits the game perfectly; the atmosphere is wonderful; the locations are varied, unique, usually rather extensive, yet still beautiful and detailed. Few games have made me as eager to explore the beautifully crafted locations and stare into the splendid beaches, mountains, architecture, the skyboxes as The Talos Principle.
This game has quite a bit of plot, but it bestowes little of it on a plate. There are no cutscenes (except the intro and the game - ending ones), instead there are these 'computer terminals' that hold the archives, and the QR codes. The plot is rather separated from the game and is completely optional, but that's only for the best, as not only do the players have a choice if they want to commit to the plot or not, the game also expects the player to be intelligent and to learn as much as they can - or want, this also works alongside the themes of the game - intelligence, A.I., to name a few. I found the philosophy to be enjoyable, it brought some very sophisticated thoughts and ideas to my attention, made me contemplate things I had never considered before; the endings were satisfying and revealed answers to the remaining questions, also making me pondering the messages of the game and revealing some new hidden insights. Brilliant writting.
It made me feel human, and even made a big impact on my life.
Lastly, I loved how the game doesn't serve everything on a plate and doesn't hold the player's hand : there are hidden puzzles, hidden locations, and easter eggs, hidden stuff in general, and little to no guidance (ironically enough). Too often game developers try to shove down experiences down players' throats, yet it's so much more rewarding and special, when there are things - important things, not only jokes - waiting to be discovered, hidden dots being connected, and 68 65 78 61 64 65 63 69 6d 61 6c 20 6e 75 6d 62 65 72 73 to 62 65 20 64 65 63 69 70 68 65 72 65 64 2e. So a game that is intelligent and treats its players as such? Yes, please.
All in all, this was a special game, a true masterpiece, and one of my favourites now.

Solid team based F2P FPS, tight gameplay. There has been worry about the game being pay to win and I don't think that's true. Rarer loadouts for characters are cosmetic only and can yield the same perks as a bronze or silver loadout.
PROS
- Characters: I am fond of the characters not only because each has unique abilities, but also because I feel like their personalities shine through. The character profiles give a quick summary of the character's abilities and persoanlity, and the one-liners and such during play I think add to it. Plus, there's a nice amount of characters to pick from as well provided you buy them with in game currency or real cash.
- Gameplay. Tight FPS mechanics. It doesn't feel floaty or sluggish, and hit boxes make sense. Each character is limited to certain weapons though so that's something to keep in mind. You can't just equip any weapon to any character.
CONS
- It's F2P. That's not inherently bad though. You can buy any character with in game currency and you can also buy standard unlock cases with in game currency. My issue is that it seems like earning in game currency gets more and more time consuming as you gain more. For example as I apporach 50,000 in game currency that rate that I earn the gold from matches seems to dramatically slow down. I understand why they're doing it, it's just annoying to me. on your road to 20,000 gold you could earn some decent gold at the end for doing really well, but at about 40,000 or so gold you earn less in matches for doing just as good. Just seems a bit inconsistent in order for them to benefit from you maybe getting impatient.
- Recycling loadouts: It feels like they've changed the method of recycling your more common loadouts in order to get higher rarity ones often. I would imagine it could be due to it being a bit less of a hassle (but still kind of a hassle) to get higher rarity cards by trading in your more common ones. It seems like they have changed it every now and then in order to make it a bit more tedious and time consuming to get a higher rarity loadout and maybe entice people to buy with real money. Again, just something I've noticed.
- Maps: There are just not as many maps as I'd like to see. Most are fun to play on whether your attacking or defending an objective, but I'd just like to see more.

This game is one of those rare games where you actually really care about your colonists. I've been playing with one colony for about 12 hours now and we've been through a lot. I started my colony with one 19 year old man crash landing onto a planet with his pet dog Scarlet. Now initially, I had no idea how to play, but I did figure it out after a bit. The man named "Bossman" almost died to raiders within 3 days of landing. He got stabbed in the torso and lost his left lung. I initially thought that this would be it, but he recovered from his wounds, he still lost his lung though. Now a couple of colonists named Dally and Lambertus joined and we became good friends. The colony was starting to grow and then we got raided. 3 raiders came in but we took care of them by killing 2 and wounding 1. We captured the Captain named Goki. We convinced him to join our colony and we helped him recover from his wounds, he made a full recovery. Now there was 4. A pod crash landed in our area and 70 year old man named Michael "Chicken" Carlson was wounded from the crash. Initially I didn't want to bother saving him as that was another mouth to feed and he wasn't useful considering he refused to do labour. But I saw that he had a high art skill so I bandaged him up and he joined our colony. Now there were 5. The colony was doing good and a lot of food got harvested, until a woman named Gitta was asking for help. She was being chased by raiders and needed our assistance, so we answered her call. We dealt with the raiders chasing her and she joined our colony. Now there's 6. Dally and Gitta became boyfriend and girlfriend and Dally proposed marraige to Gitta, which she accepted. Bossman is now the doctor, Dally is the cook and constructor, Lambertus is a miner and hauler, Chicken is a sculpter, Gitta is a grower, animal handler and warden and itini is a soldier and hunter. Bossman got surgery from Dally to add a new lung that I bought earlier. Things were looking great until Lambertus, Dally, and Chicken got the flu. That's basically where I am right now, half of my colonists are bed ridden and Bossman is tending to them all and trying to make them feel better. We are having issues with food now and it's almost winter. I'm really hoping we can make it one more year, I have faith for these little people.

The Talos Principle has opened my third eye to levels of enlightenment which I might have never experienced had I not played it. I feel like my brain has literally leveled up, xp which I will retain through life instead of forgotten in a save file in my graveyard of games I'll probably never play again. I'm bored of mindlessly killing things, grinding, sinking hundreds of hours into the same old gaming mechanics. I don't care how elaborate a skill tree can get, "First Person Killers" have saturated the gaming market, and not enough of them have story lines that mesh in an unpredictable way with the base objective of the game: Kill stuff, level up, talk to an NPC, kill more stuff, major storyline cutscene, repeat x30, you win. And I'm not just a gamer who plays things on easy, I always start with maximum difficulty so I can experience every game in the most real-world way possible.
I think this is one of those games that will steer many more people, and hopefully smart developers in turn, into types of games that make you think critically, problem solve, and maybe take a 5 minute break to delve into immersive text-based mediums. I have never seen text blended so beautifully into a storyline, where it isn't just supplimental lore, where it figuratively blew my mind. The text was about a third of the game in my opinion, I'm a moderate book reader but have never been in this much anticipation to read every line of text I came across in the game world.

TL;DR Highest recommendation!
A more in-depth review below.
So, what makes this game so good, and why are so many people praising it?
It's everything, really.
I don't play puzzle games, so I can't compare Talos with, say, Portal, but I can say that the puzzles are very good.  They range from easy to really complicated, though I must admit I was a bit disappointed with the pacing - even in  late game some of the puzzles were just a little bit too easy. The puzzles overall weren't that hard for the most part, and I would have prefered to have more of those really difficult and complicated ones.
But what I really enjoyed about the puzzles, is the design. They are well thought out (although, perhaps, it's more obvious if you solve the star puzzles - the more difficult and complicated ones). I also very much enjoyed how there were quite a few different tools and how one could use them in various ways, even interconnect them - the game gave me a chance to experiment.
I love the game's esthetic. The music is other worldly and fits the game perfectly; the atmosphere is wonderful; the locations are varied, unique, usually rather extensive, yet still beautiful and detailed. Few games have made me as eager to explore the beautifully crafted locations and stare into the splendid beaches, mountains, architecture, the skyboxes as The Talos Principle.
This game has quite a bit of plot, but it bestowes little of it on a plate. There are no cutscenes (except the intro and the game - ending ones), instead there are these 'computer terminals' that hold the archives, and the QR codes. The plot is rather separated from the game and is completely optional, but that's only for the best, as not only do the players have a choice if they want to commit to the plot or not, the game also expects the player to be intelligent and to learn as much as they can - or want, this also works alongside the themes of the game - intelligence, A.I., to name a few. I found the philosophy to be enjoyable, it brought some very sophisticated thoughts and ideas to my attention, made me contemplate things I had never considered before; the endings were satisfying and revealed answers to the remaining questions, also making me pondering the messages of the game and revealing some new hidden insights. Brilliant writting.
It made me feel human, and even made a big impact on my life.
Lastly, I loved how the game doesn't serve everything on a plate and doesn't hold the player's hand : there are hidden puzzles, hidden locations, and easter eggs, hidden stuff in general, and little to no guidance (ironically enough). Too often game developers try to shove down experiences down players' throats, yet it's so much more rewarding and special, when there are things - important things, not only jokes - waiting to be discovered, hidden dots being connected, and 68 65 78 61 64 65 63 69 6d 61 6c 20 6e 75 6d 62 65 72 73 to 62 65 20 64 65 63 69 70 68 65 72 65 64 2e. So a game that is intelligent and treats its players as such? Yes, please.
All in all, this was a special game, a true masterpiece, and one of my favourites now.

Currently I have played 152 hours of Robocraft, I think I've played enough to make a review...
Robocraft (as the name suggests...) is a game that allows you to build robots to fight other robots.  While the concept is simple, I have found many different (and cruel...) ways to customize your robot to your will.  There are wheels, tank tracks, wings and rudders, mech legs, thrusters, skis, etc.  Along with that, you can share your robots with others in the factory and earn the in-game currency, robits.  These robits can be used to forge the materials you need to make robots.  The robits can also be used to buy robots in the factory.
Building robots are the core of the gameplay in Robocraft.  With your materials (which are extremely limited at first...) sorted in the catagories of chassis, movement, hardware, special, and cosmetic, you can build anything that you imagine (until you fill the max cpu of 2,000...).  If you don't like building and/or are looking for a robot that might suit your playstyle, you could go to paragraph 1 and read (trust me, I talked about that already...)!
As for game modes, there are Brawl, Pit, Battle Arena, League Arena, AI Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, Test, and Tutorial.  However, when it comes to the amount of loot and experience points earned in the many options, some are favored more than others.  For example, players who go to Battle Arena and League Arena earn more experience points and loot from loot crates, and for players who have a busy scedule and have an open slot of 10 to 20 minutes would be slow at leveling up especially at the later levels.
Overall, I recommend this game due to the fact that I love Legos and engineering.  This game isn't suited for everyone as the loot crate system seems rigged, earning robits is nearly impossible without premium, and the matchmaking system seems flawed.  In my case, the pros overweighed the cons and I reccomend that you play Robocraft WITHOUT PLAYING MONEY AT FIRST (can't stress that enough...).  Wait unitl you feel as you'll enjoy the game and then decide if you want to pay for more crates or premium.  Thanks you reading my review!  :D

I usually write a review for a game when I play it 10 hours... although as bad as it may sound that I've only played an hour and I'm reviewing, it's actually not that bad in some respects.
The gun selection is pretty big, I have to say. It's bigger than some $60 games out there, there is a good variety of guns.
Graphics are so/so but the fact that there's one lightpost and then a bunch of open land, there could at least be a little more scenery in my opinion.
Trading cards are easy, just the way I like it.
No voices in the characters, no running but the zombies increase in difficulty which is a good challenge.
Two game modes are actually enough for this game, it keeps you satisfied.
Online play works fantastic, probably the game's best feature. Online play makes the game easier and more enjoyable with randoms and friends.
For $1.99 and was on sale for 49 cents at one point, It's something you should consider buying.
Items like barriers and turrets don't help as much as you would hope, but creating a base around the lightpost (hint, hint) and trapping yourself inside with a turret on each side is a EXTREMELY good idea surprisingly.
Achievements, fun to try to accomplish. I have yet to get more but they do increase in difficult, so I like them.

Wasn't expecting much from this game when I downloaded it seeing as it was on the third page of the "Free To Play" section of Steam.
4 months later, I can't stop playing. Planetside 2 offers several things:
- A real F2P model. You can buy things with real money, but you need to earn the money in-game for several things. Upgrades to character suit and utility slots must be done wit the in-game currency for example.
- Continent - scale battles. At prime time on the server I play on, you can reach over 1000 people playing on one server, duking it out for control over a continent.
- It's just as fun to play with friends in a squad as it is to play solo. Both come with different tactics to try and take on bases, but you'll find yourself playing in a squad most of the time.
- A challenge. There is no match-making in this game. You will often find yourself getting instagibbed by pro players. I view this as a positive because playing this game has a serious effect on the way you play FPSes.
Don't expect to charge into a room full of guys with an LMG and tear them all down. This is the sort of game were you have to think.

While it doesn't do anything new, the game does play its hand really well, so for that I'll recommend it.

Wolfenstein: The New Order is undoubtedly an excellent game that injects a feeling of old-school shooter into a modern FPS package. This game has everything you can expect from a modern shooter and this is one of the few I found worth playing thoroughly since Bioshock. This game has a very immersive universe and an excellent story/script that makes it more than a shooter.
The designers payed attention to every details and did an excellent job at the dystopian exercise of imagining that the Nazis won the war. For instance, I really enjoyed the newspapers (or scrap of it) that relates the story of what happened since WWII. The game is full of those details, and also has a lot of hidden references. The cut-scenes are excellent and the voice acting is up to par.
For people – like me – who like to play a game thoroughly, there are plenty of secrets and challenges that extends the lifetime of the game (enigma codes, Nazi gold). There is also a branching in the story that allows you to replay the game with different characters.
I only found 2 minor downsides in this game:
- You can play in stealth mode, but the AI has been so dumbed down that it just doesn’t feels right. You can kill a guard in front of another one and he won’t notice that his buddy is dead.
- The levels are a bit too linear: there are some side paths to explore, but there is not a lot of branching nor depth in it.
That shouldn’t stop you from buying this game which is excellent.

Another mode is the endless night mode. which you gain after 10 waves of survival. In endless night mode there are no palisades. Weapons spawn by random of killed zombies. Here you must survive 5 min max.

This game is truly one of a kind, and I recomnend it to all. Planetside 2 is the only place where you will find battles between hundreds of players on one giant map, not a small confined one, a full contient to traverse. Planetside 2 is the only place where you will find such weapon and playstyle vareity, from driving a tank to piloting a jet, you can do it all. There are weapons cleary designed for different engagments, from CQC to long range. Whatever your playstyle is, you will find it in Planetside 2. The lore is also very intriguing, but not very present in the game.
Here's a short version: An expidition from Earth travelled through a wormhole and became trapped on the other side. Enventually they found a planet they named Auraxis, and began settling there. But tensions were high, with the discovery of ancient alien artifacts from a long dead race known as the Vanu, the Terran Republic, or TR, banned researching the new artifacts, and began oppressing the scientists who researched the artifacts. Along with oppressing new technology, the TR began oppressing everything else, such as corporations. This didn't sit well with corporate leaders, and they formed the New Conglomerate, or NC, and succeded from the TR for opressing them. At the same time, the scientists that had previously been reseaching the Vanu artifacts, seized the technology, reversed engineered it, and declared themselves the Vanu Sovreignty, or VS.
Each faction has "good" and "bad" sides, so choose carefully.
The Terran Republic wants to reunite the factions, but they are a dictatorship and rule with oppression and fear.
The New Conglomerate wants freedom from the TR, but it is made up of mostly mercenaries that only fight for the next paycheck from their corprate leaders.
The Vanu Sovreignty believes the only way for humanity to evolve is through technology, and they kill anyone who disagrees with their views.
Each faction also has different weapon characterisics. The TR have high rate of fire weapons and somewhat large recoil.
The NC have low rate of fire weapons, but they do more damage, and also have higher recoil. The VS have mid rate of fire, great accuracy, and decent recoil, along with no bullet drop for all weapons except for bolt action sniper rifles.

Though there have been many "modern reboots" of Wolfenstein over the years, The New Order does the best job of any I've played.  A key point is that this is a reboot of the original Wolfenstein, not Doom or Quake.  So even though we tend to think of retro FPSs as circle-strafing and bunny-hopping, this is not that type of game.  It's very much in the vein of "shoot them before they shoot you" style of the original (you will not be dodging bullets here).
To add depth to this style of shooting, The New Order introduces are very competent stealth system which allows you to take down enemies with silent weapons to improve your odds.  Once the♥♥♥♥♥♥finally hits the fan, a cover system allows you to make strategic shots instead of just standing out in the open trading damage.
I want to particularly highlight the way they handled the difficulty.  I did my first play-through on "Uber" and found that the game was surprisingly well balanced.  Rather than turning the enemies into bullet sponges, it mostly just made the enemies more deadly.  This actually encouraged me to rely on the stealth and cover systems more to succeed.  In other words, the increased difficulty actually meshed well with the mechanics of the game rather than just adding 2x the number of enemies or giving them 2x the health.
The only negatives I found were a few bugs near the end where certain vital items (such as health and armor packs) failed to spawn properly.  Consider this happens at the end of the game where all the big battles are, I was finding it quite frustrating that there were no healing items.  It was only after restarting the game that I found out the items were missing.
While it doesn't revolutionize anything about the genre, The New Order is a competently done reboot that pays homage to the original while improving on the mechanics for the modern age.  Definitely recommended.

I've been a fan of the Max Payne game series for years, and played through the first 2 games countless times Unfortunately, Max Payne 3 ended up being a major disappointment. It wasn't a bad game, but it just wasn't Max Payne at all. The character looks completely different, the setting is entirely different, and the premise just didn't scream Max Payne at all. Gone are the signature cutscene comic book panels. Gone is the New York setting. Instead we get shiny action-packed cutscenes and the sunny slums of Brazil. It was just a complete departure from the series and entirely undeserving of the name "Max Payne". Worst still, I hardly used bullet time throughout the entire campaign, most of the time forgetting it existed in Max Payne 3, despite bullet time easily being the series' biggest signature aspect. I don't know if it was developed by the same team who developed the first two games, but it feels like an entirely new team blasting the series apart to rebuild it in an entirely new image. How I'd sum Max Payne 3 up is this: a complete failure of a sequel that tried too hard to be distinctly different, and in doing so completely lost what the series is about.
I'd give Max Payne 3, 3/10.

Castle Crashers is one of the best games I have ever played hands down. The developers really did a good job of making this an enjoyable experience for players.
Pros:
+ Unique cast of characters. When I say this, I dont mean in personality, but in abilities. The base 4 characters (Plus the two DLC characters) are very interesting and have their own skillset and ways to play them
+ Interesting level design. None of the levels in this game seemed like filler to me. Everything was well designed and put there for a reason.
+ Graphics. The character/enemy/level designs are done very well. I really like the way everything looks in this game.
+ Bosses. Each boss in this game was unique and fun to fight. There weren't any generic "Shoot its weak spot while it's invulnerable" bosses (Excluding the catfish, which was interesting in its own ways.)
+ Controls. The controls are very smooth and easy to get the hang of.
+ Multi/Singleplayer. It is heavily suggested that you should play with 3 friends however the game is a lot of fun in singleplayer as well. The game is designed to be easy and fun for someone playing by themselves as well.
+ Gameplay. The combat and movement are very smooth and easy to get used to.
NEUTRAL
+ Insane mode. After beating the game, you are given the choice to replay it in insane mode. You keep your weapons and skill points but it starts you at the beginning. The experience makes it seem like youre playing it for the first time again because even though you have good items and abilities, the enemies are a lot stronger. Insane mode can get very difficult very fast, though.
CONS:
- Control presentation. The controls are explained as gamepad buttons. When doing tutorials, you are instructed to "Press X to attack" even if you do not have a gamepad plugged in. The keyboard controls are very easy to figure out though.
- Filler characters. This game has an insane amount of playable characters and a lot of them share the same ability that isnt that good. Quite a few characters use magic that sends arrows down from the sky and it does a very small amount of damage. Luckily, these are not characters you need to play as.
Final Review: I would recommend that you buy this game. It's given me hours of fun, and like I said: It's one of my favourite games.

While Portal 1 is much more about fast gameplay while still featuring some story at a small but still very suitable pace, Portal 2 focuses alot more on story. While some may say this is a good thing, I do not support big changes in most things, so that was a bad thing in my opinion. The only good thing I would say this change brought was how well played out the scene where you walk into GLaDoS' place and see her on the ground in different pieces while the lighting and music almost makes you feel bad for "killing" her in the last game.
That aside, the game did have some great features. Upgraded graphics, co-op levels and story, FREAKING GEL, and community made levels. The community made levels are a great option if you just want to take a break from all the story telling of the normal Portal 2 single player experience.
I would say overall this was a good game, even though I'm not too much of a fan of change. It is still another experience for die-hard fans of Portal, like me, and it sure is a mostly positive one.

This is the best game that Bethesda has ever published, in my opinion. Although some Steamworks features are absent in The New Order - such as Steam cloud support (which might be reason enough to not pick this up for some) - I'd still say that it's worth the cost of entry. Though from what I've heard, The Old Blood might be an even better pick if you're looking for a game in the classic FPS style. I can't verify that, though; so let's move on.
Bethesda not putting out any DLC for this game partially renewed my respect for the company. By doing that, they essentially allowed Machine Games/MachineGames to immediately start working on The Old Blood; a project that I find much more interesting than any horse armor nonsense they could've put out instead. It not having a multiplayer component is also a plus in my eyes - but I know it definitely isn't to others. I feel that not wasting their time on developing a tacked-on multiplayer mode allowed them to craft a more fleshed out and memorable campaign, packed with charm and character.
So, in short: buy it if you want to have a grand time shooting, slicing, and smashing Nazis. I'd also recommend picking it up if you want to support better business practices in the games industry. After all - the only way we'll get to see more DLC-less AAA titles is by buying the ones that come out.

There's about a million reasons why this game, which hasn't changed one iota since release, has kind of decayed over time. I'm not going to list them all, just remind you all that if you are considering picking this game up, remember that you have a big big download ahead of you, a lot of promises which still haven't come to fruition, and an extremely dedicated core fanbase which has probably all played this game since the first, or simply is dedicated to it now. Think EVE Online.
Now, basically, time = power. The higher level you are, the more stuff you have, and the more stuff you have, the better off you are. The longer you play, the more XP you will have, and because doing ANYTHING in this game will reward XP, even the worst player will beat the best player if, say, both players were playing heavy and met in a small room. Obviously if they fired at one another, the one with the more points invested in armor is going to win the gunfight.
And it's not even that I don't think players should be rewarded for their playtime, but, honestly, I've seen maps completely covered in red, blue and purple, and not once has it really ever meant anything. If I were playing with everything unlocked, I don't even really know why I would care about this game at all, since the only things you're really going to unlock by winning, is the ability to win harder with more vehicles and resource points and stuff like that. But nothing, in the end, really matters... it's not like any of the factions actually win anything, there's no rewards or anything like that, there's nothing.
In the end, I guess you can look at this as some kind of F2P Bad Company 2. It's not bad, I guess, but there's a lot of questionable balance issues, and honestly, I just don't find it very fun anymore. I like a good FPS, but there's just nothing to enjoy with this game anymore. Once you've taken every hill, every facility, every biolab... well, that's pretty much it. Likely you've seen everything, you know every circumstance, and you'll still wonder how despite the fact that your two factions are both staring down a corridor firing potshots, somehow you're still finding enemies standing right beside you, nobody moving to shoot and kill them...
But, bottom line, I guess I do have to recommend this game. Just for the simple fact that, if you have never played this game before, you do need to give it a try. Maybe the experience has been tarnished, but when this game actually kicks♥♥♥♥♥ it really kicks♥♥♥♥♥ Riding or driving in a big♥♥♥♥♥convoy of sunderers, prowlers and lightnings is pretty ♥♥♥♥ing exciting.
The most fun I ever had in this game was at first storming bases with a massive wave of allies, shouting Russian all the way. Then it was as a sniper. It manages that most wondrous of gaming achievements: the sense of discovery. I was immersed from the first second to the last glorious moments, and there's so many things to find. The writing and soundtrack are on point, and the puzzles themselves almost perfectly balanced and the pacing spot on.
This is a game of layers, and the length of the game is up to you. There are three endings, two of which tie into the main puzzles, while the third is tied to the bonus and more difficult ones. You'll likely find, as I did, that you want to finish ALL the puzzles, requirement or no, because they're just that good. There's only a couple of them I disliked, one of which required external tools to solve, another which seemed to break the rules the world had established, but other than that they're excellent.
If you've played Portal and wondered what's next, well this game is. It's such a natural spiritual sequel to that franchise, one which I would go so far as to say as surpassed its inspiration. Certainly it handles training you in a smoother and less obvious way.

I typically avoid doing reviews, not just for games but in general.
Often it's because I can't help but see reviews as opinion pieces instead of an actual product review.
I realize that I may contradict myself in reviewing The New Order, so bare with me. I'll try to keep it short.
I'll start simple;
GRAPHICS
---------------
its a beautifully (and demanding) game. I'm rocking a gtx 970 maxed settings/1080p and after a few hours i can see some rendering issues and drastic fps drop. I've never been one to choose graphical fidelity over fluidity and when i couldn't achieve 60fps by lowering settings, I knew I needed to let my pc rest.
AUDIO
---------------
mmk, this one I'm 50/50 on. Maybe its my setup, my gaming headphones, or something else but certain scenes in this game suffer from seriously unbalanced audio. If it weren't for the subtitles (which I initially tried to play without entirely) I would'nt have been able to keep track of what people were telling BJ in the middle of the missions.
However, the music is phenominal. The phrases "it's not what you say but how you say it" and "originallity isn't doing something entirely unheard of but doing the same thing in a different way."
Not once was I unhappy with the music. Action scenes are actiony/ambient enough to immerse you without completely distracting you. I understand that this may be confusing, but I prefer in game music to not be to distracting from whats going on. Think of when an actor hams it up but with music.
GAMEPLAY
---------------
The stealth isn't anything to boast about, but it does provide an interesting layer/dynamic that you typically don't see in many AAA fps. The stealth functions similarly to how Far Cry 3/4 function. Except you're not getting xp rewards.
If you're a run and gunner, you'll be more than accomodated for.
I am a cover shooter. Lots of Mass Effect, Gears of War, Deus Ex: Human Revolution, and even Assassin's Creed: Unity under my belt. Wolfn:TNO, arguably has the best fps cover system I've ever played.
PLOT
---------------
This is perhaps the biggest thing I personally care about in games. Is The New Order something to write home about? Not really, in my opinion. Without giving any spoilers I can only say its better than nearly any COD or Battlefield plot you'll see. I will say that its worth noting that Wolfn does 1 thing well. The alternate timeline concept was not only well done, but convincing. I guess you'll just have to play for yourself.
I hate point systems so I'll just say I recommend this game. Will I leave it installed? Probably not, but I definitely believe its worth whatever price you pay for it including the nonsale price.

Yes I am late to the party on this one, but I will still recommend it. Especially to any Max Payne fans.
I personally liked the first game in the series the most. Had the best/most intriguing atmosphere/story not to mention really impressive gunplay. (especially for its time) That being said I will say that I think Max Payne 3 is number two on that list. With Max Payne 2 coming in last. Though I enjoyed them all.
The second Max Payne tends to lose you right around the last 1/3 of the game. The first, and third games in the series do not suffer from that, and have great pacing all around.
Now to focus more on this game. It has great graphics, gameplay, gunplay, and the difficulty spikes can be a pain, but are not too bad. I personally like the melee on this game the best out of the 3 games. weapon selection is always pretty good in these games, but grenades are so scare I don't even think I got to use one. I remember in MP1, and MP2, you could get grenades, and definitely get molotov cocktails. They are not so present in this game from the players perspective.
Its not a short game, but its also not as long as people claim it is, I beat it on hard in about 12 hours, not counting setup and AFKs.
It is very movie like, the way it transitions back and forth is pretty well done. Especially for a game that came out 3 years ago.
I did like the reflections back in this game, and the snow levels (which is why I loved New York in the first game) That being said they used the atmosphere of this game to create a completely different feeling Max Payne, and they did a pretty good job of it. The music really accented what was happening in the game at the time, as well as, stands out as pretty good tracks overall. The music has always been pretty good in Max Payne, but the third one has the best music of the series.
The story/plot of this one didn't have as much impact on me as the first game, and a lot of it was cliche', but it turned out to be pretty decent.  The voice acting was good, and most of the sound effects were ok, but could have been better. The performance of hte game is pretty straight forward especially if you don't go crazy with MSAA. I do like that the gameplay reflects his age, and how worn he is. He is not near as fast as in the first 2 games. He takes at least twice as long to recover from a dive in this game. Much more of a cinematic experience than the first two games, but they molded the new with the old fairly well.
The multiplayer has been shut down by now, but the game is still worth purchasing. It also is one of the many games on steam that always sees a decent %off on ever Steam sale.

Castle Crashers is exactly what a 2D Beat Em Up should be. It's got good combat gameplay, excellent visuals, a fantastic variety of multiplayer modes, allows up to four players to play the game, great humor, plenty of levels, and a number of playable characters.
The game is cartoonish-styled, so expect a lot of over the top humor. Some of it is some mild black comedy, and there is some degree of blood and violence, comparable to TF2, but is slightly more mild.
The game has you in a (mostly) medieval setting, with the initial playable characters being four royal knights. There isn't much of a story outside of an evil wizard uniting several other kingdoms to attack yours for some kind of Magic Crystal (that the wizard directly steals) and claim the four princesses for varying reasons (only one is actually known to be held for forced marriage). Honestly though, in a silly beat em up that's as colorful and full of life as this one, it doesn't exactly need a big driving story. It just needs an atmosphere and charm to put on top of it's fun gameplay. And that's exactly what it has.
The gameplay is action-packed, wave of enemies after enemies show up constantly as you move forwardi n each level. You learn more attacks and abilities as you level up, and you can also combo enemies through various means, but the main means behind doing that is to jump and knock them into the air, where you can stay airborn for a while by striking your trapped enemies in the air repeatedly. You can use this kind of tactic to trap multiple enemise at once.
Of course, not everyone is going to enjoy the genre, so for those that do, the only real downside to this game is that it's gameplay can get repetitive. Sure you learn more moves after a while, and enemies and levels definitely change up, but the core gameplay stays the same, and when the action is so constant, it might get tiring for some pretty quickly. All the more reason to take breaks from the game though, right?
Also, there are a HUGE amount of characters to unlock. It can be tedious (some methods are particularly complicated, requiring that you beat story mode all over again with one new character just to unlock another one) so that's one thing about this game I kinda dislike. Not personally, but I can definitely see why other people wouldn't find value in it. If you enjoy the game enough though, you might just see it as replay value instead, especially if you're planning to bring some friends along. And while playing through the main story in singleplayer is definitely enjoyable, this game is most definitely more fun when you're playing with friends.

(especially for its time) That being said I will say that I think Max Payne 3 is number two on that list. With Max Payne 2 coming in last. Though I enjoyed them all.
The second Max Payne tends to lose you right around the last 1/3 of the game. The first, and third games in the series do not suffer from that, and have great pacing all around.
Now to focus more on this game. It has great graphics, gameplay, gunplay, and the difficulty spikes can be a pain, but are not too bad. Much more of a cinematic experience than the first two games, but they molded the new with the old fairly well.
The multiplayer has been shut down by now, but the game is still worth purchasing. It also is one of the many games on steam that always sees a decent %off on ever Steam sale.

Where to even begin.. Wolfenstein: The New Order is phenomenal. I kept delaying purchase of this game despite all the praise it received. I had no desire to spend 50 dollars on a genre that I don’t even enjoy that much, but at 14.99 I feel like I outright robbed the devs.
Graphically Wolfenstein is stellar; I didn’t encounter a single muddled texture or janky pop-in. Animations are natural and varied. The gun effects are meaty and unbelievably deadly feeling. Sound design reflects this quality with heavy, forceful gunshots and chaotic combat chatter as you mow down nazi foes. Everything about the presentation is just perfect.
But every modern FPS is shiny, the problem is that they are all bland, stale, predictable, and just plain boring to play. Not Wolfenstein, dear god not this game. You are unnaturally quick, agile and can leap and slide about the stage whilst dual wielding assault rifles.When the game gives you guns, it wants you to go ape with them. On top of that, Wolfenstein goes back to the good ol’ days of magical bottomless pockets, allowing you to carry about a full arsenal of chaos to use as you see fit. Gunning down one room only to slide into the next stealthily tossing knives into the backs of any nazi whose back is foolishly turned is pure joy.
As if making a good feeling shooter in this day and age isn’t reason enough to celebrate, the storyline and character development is mind blowing. Sure the emotions won’t be running as high as your first time playing The Walking Dead, but I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t swept away into the struggles of the protagonist and his rag-tag group of freedom fighters. With some seriously dark and difficult topics hit on with such taste and creativity, when the cutscenes are rolling it’s hard to believe this is an old school nazi killing arcade. That is, until the tone switches to absurd 80’s action movie mode and you gather around the round table to hatch a crazy plot to mow down more nazis. When you can go from entering a concentration camp-witnessing all the horrors associated with a locale of that nature- to melting nazis on the moon with laser assault rifles and never breaking the flow of the narrative or gameplay then you have accomplished something magical.
I could harp all day on how each part of Wolfenstein is expertly crafted, but the pinnacle of achievement here is the inconceivably masterful balance between so many conflicting styles, themes and narratives. Wolfenstein: The New Order is by far one of the best games I’ve played in 2015.

I've been playing this game since the original public release, and my has it come a ways.
So this game originally is about three survivors (that you make) of a destroyed ship above a planet amongst the outter rim of the galaxy, aply named the "Rim Worlds". It is your goal to survive of the planet and make a self sustaining colony. Or, if you're a weirdo, play for the end game and make a raggidy and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ship to escape the planet with the colonists you have.
The endgame stays the same throughout the 2 new starting scenarios, which is having a singular rich colonist the play around with, or having a small band of natives to the planet with little to no technology aside from being able to make bows.
Simple enough story, right?
Well here's the game.
Starting off is always simple. You can prioritize your colonists actions and give them specific jobs to perform, allowing you  to streamline your colonies work. You can make large fields to grow crops, make housing and furniture, regulate the temperature of rooms, and make entertaining things so your colonists don't get bored and start
roam around for like half an hour in a 'dazed' state.
This is where the game gets a bit challenging. And where I myself have the most trouble, and the most fun.
Balancing all of these things can be a bit of a challenge to undertake, especially if you're like me and decide to do it alllll at once. The way it's balanced is so unique and well polished over the 2 or so years (forget exact date of public release) I've been playing. This game is definetly my my number 1 time waster, and trust me you'll be sinking alot of time into it to get stuff done.
Simply put, if you're into the colony survival gametype, or like colony builder sims, this is definetly the first buy that should cross your mind.

I don't review games but hell, more people should play this. You should play this. It's a great first-person puzzler with a surprisingly enthralling narrative. Play it if you have any interest at all in the genre. Play it. Yes, you.
I picked it up in a sale since I liked Portal and Antichamber, and ended up getting something like a combination thereof with a side of Asimov-lite. The Portal (2) influences are particularly strong in both the mechanics and the aesthetic, but it brings a lot of other things to the table. Great puzzle gameplay with a great sci-fi setting and story, and against all odds an exploratory feel.
The basic puzzle mechanics in this game are far from original (the over-industrialized cubes and lasers should be very familiar), but they are deftly combined into a wide array of puzzles that stay fresh until the end. There are a few puzzles that are frustrating because they are more about execution than thinking, but for the most part this is very well avoided. One example is jumping, which can be done as in a typical first-person game but also via an unintrusive helper mechanic to assist with jumping on to moving platforms. Upon seeing this for the first time I was skeptical, but in practice it feels very smooth and doesn't break immersion in the way similar things (e.g. cover mechanics in some FPS) often do.
I found the pacing of the puzzles to be excellent, and the way in which they are unlocked smooths out any bump in the road - while there is an overall linear progression that introduces new mechanics and increases complexity, you can always leave a puzzle and try another. (The progression is
flexible if you want to be - I think you can unlock something like 70% of the game's puzzles by solving about 20% of them.) This is a slightly more artificial implementation of the way Antichamber plays out, and initially makes the game's environments seem rather sterile and segmented - each puzzle is fenced in and items cannot be brought in or out of their entrances.  But when you try to break these chains the world really gets interesting - not only are there loads of easter eggs to be found, but in fact there are a lot of bonus puzzles that rely on rule-bending. Thus the game world feels open and exciting to explore, despite its very artificially delineated nature.
The narrative is what really caught me by surprise. While the majority of it is delivered via text and audio logs, this isn't just a crutch or cost-cutting. It's all superbly well written, and fits together just well enough to gradually build up a cohesive understanding of the game world without spoon-feeding you. The gameplay and the story are almost completely disjointed, which normally would be something to criticize; but the unusual nature of
' setting makes it feel perfect here. (That unusual setting also allows the game to be very self-aware without ever breaking the fourth wall, which is super cute.) Even the QR codes that are initially just flavour end up tying in with the story.
The writing always does exactly what it intends to - it all feels very genuine. It's hilarious, thought-provoking and heartfelt at different points, each exactly when it means to be.  Reading some coverage of the game after playing, it seems much is made of the philosophical aspect. If you've done much thinking about metaphysics and ethics then it's unlikely there will be any new ideas for you here, but the game never feels like it's trying too hard - the philosophical diversions have an in-universe reason to exist and are
engagingly presented. Despite never having my "mind blown", I always looked forward to the next little debate.
My only real complaint would be that the story ran out too fast - I felt like I got 80% of the narrative in my first 10 hours playing, and the other 20 hours were dominated by puzzling. Perhaps I should be grateful that the bonus puzzles provided even the tidbits of story that they did; but the alternate ending for 100% completion is really quite underwhelming. There's one big narrative payoff for finishing the core of the gameplay, after which you're left with some of the best puzzles but almost nothing else. That said, the payoff was amazing (despite not being a surprise) and the puzzles alone (and a few secrets I stumbled upon along the way) were enough to keep me engrossed right through to 100%.
The game is technically very pretty for something that came from a moderately small developer, and the assets are all high quality if a bit repetitive. Once again the setting prevents this from breaking immersion, but aside from the few moments when you first discover visually different areas, it's repetitive nonetheless. This never really bothered me - I was too busy solving puzzles, and some of those moments I mentioned made up for it. There are a few vistas that are truly awe-inspiring when first revealed, especially thanks to the amazing accompaniment of the soundtrack, which is consistently on point - it fits the tone and aesthetic of the game extremely well, and adapts smoothly to fit the mood. For the most part it's slow paced and contemplative, almost ambient - the almost complete lack of percussion means it never distracts from puzzle-solving. It's only at key moments of exploration and progress that it comes to the fore, and it does so with gusto. (Good soundtrack for listening to while working!)
I don't think there's much else to say. Play it.
