My partner bought this game and I decided to give it a shot and was immediatley hooked.
I have just around 6 hours and I have decided to tab out of my game to write this review on why i believe you should buy this gmae. The following harrowing tale has just taken place in the space of about 15 minutes irl time and nothing i am about to recount has been made up. It has all just unfolded in front of my eyes and i just had to share the experience before i forget all the minor details.
It is the 6th of summer. After being banished from their previous tribe this band of plucky cavemen and women set out to start a new.
After a month of toil and food all but run out. Today is the day of the big harvest, at least, it was supposed to be.
It is a chilly morning. 3 degrees c but the sun has risen and its warming up niceley. Everyone is ready to take in the harvest when V3trox spies some raiders to the north. Fortunatley we have prepared for this. The tribe is all skilled in the use of bows and our recent addition "toad" has been working hard to equip everyone with a bow.
V3trox calls the whole tribe to arms but leaves toad behind as she is an outsider and has no place fighting for the tribe and is left to perform the cleaning duties.
3 radiers come into sight. One armed with a shotgun, another with an smg and the last with a pistol. 3 against 5. We may have more men, but they have gunpowder. V3trox takes the head of the group. Velaniel, Mantis, Berro and Hawk stand behind him. The bows out range the guns, but not by much, enough to to get a wave of arrows in befor the enemy come in range.
The first withering hail of arrows is released in a catastrophic failure, All 5 arrows completley miss, the tone of the battle is set. The first raider, armed with an smg opens up with a burst of shots. The group of tribesmen is peppered but mostly superficial wounds. A leg is shot here, an arm there but the tribesmen hold their ground and let loose another round of arrows. A couple hit but the damage is superficial. All 3 raiders are in range.
The tribesmen are quickly mowed down in a merciless shower of leaded death. V3trox is the first to fall. A shotgun sweeps across him. His torso shredded, a hole in his stomach, damage to his left leg, his left foot is nowhere to be seen and in its place just a bloodied stump.
Mantis is decimated. Smg rounds in every part of his body including his spine.
Berro takes two full shotgun blasts. Blood pooling beneath her
Hawk takes the worst. Every raider scores a good hit on poor Hawk with both kidneys sporting nasty bullet holes.
At this point all the tribesmen are still alive, albiet downed in pools of blood and vicera. Some concious and unable to walk. Others plain unconcious
Velaniel retreats to the safety of the camp and to seek aid from Toad but all is not lost. One of the raiders is downed under the pouring stream of arrows. The  remaining 2 raiders, satisfied with the damage they have caused proceed to try and take a prisoner each and proceed to pick up Hawk and V3trox but a stray arrow landing on the floor forces one raider to drop v3trox on the ground. The raider turns around to see Toad screeming at the top of her lungs brandishing a spear. He gets hit, somewhere in the torso. The raider lashes out. A flurry of punches knocks Toad to the ground giving the raider time to flee. Toad is down and out. The final raider, a blonde female, runs with v3trox over her shoulder. Who knows what these raiders want but she was desperate to get v3trox back to her camp.
Velaniel is trying to chase but struggles to breath. A stray bullet from the initial engagment has punctured her lung. Thats not going to stop her though. She continues the chase, launching arrows at the final raider. Each one lands a hit, each arrow slowing the raider to a bloodied stop.

Some of the most fun I've had playing an FPS in years.  I always appeciate a game in this genre that decide to focus just on singleplayer instead of multiplayer.  The story, while not treading any new ground, is servicable and the characters are likable and believable.  It's an alternate 1960 in which Nazi Germany won and now has crazy future tech to keep the population under their boot.  The game takes you to many fun locations all over the world that look beautify ranging from Nazi Berlin, to under the sea in a U-Boat to a Nazi moon base!  There is also a large perk system that both rewards you for your play style while incentivizing you to change up the way you play to explore all the ways you can approach situations.
Luckily, the game play is even better.  The classic play with few modern additions are greatly apperciated by myself.  Health only partial regenerates up to the closest multiple of 20 up to 100 HP and you can pick up armor points to supplement.  Being able to carry all the weapons you find without having to give up a weapon is also classic.  Each weapon has a secondary fire AND can be dual wielded.  You can control the secondary mode of each dual-wielded weapon seperately which allows for easy use of both modes at the same time.  You do lost the ability to aim down the sights, but they remain manageable as long as you don't fire in full auto except at close range.  The hell you can unleash when nessarary is a blast.
Another surprise is the relatively fun stealth system.  The AI isn't exactly the smartest about reacting to all the dead Nazis you leave in your wake, but it still is fun to sneak around stabbing unsuspecting Nazis.  You can throw extra knives from a distance to silent kill from a distance.  Remain in stealth when a commander is present keeps extra enemies reinforcements from coming.  Going in hot will cause a constant stream of angry Nazis to show up until you manage to kill all present commanders.
If you are anything like me, wishing you could play another FPS that takes insperation from the games of 15 years ago instead of being another CoD shooter, you'll love this game.  Totally worth couple playthroughs.

Where do I start. This game is amazing. If you like realism, tactics, ptsd, and cowering in cover as bullets zip by your head this is the game for you.
This game is only in Pre-Alpha and is already as polished as other finished products. Don't think you're going to run guns blazing and do well because you will get wrecked. This game takes patience and communication to make you successful.
The communication in this game is amazing. If you are in a squad you will be working with your teammates and listening to squad leader directives. There is squad chat, vacinity chat, and the ability for the squad leaders to directly communicate to other squad leaders to set up the battle plan.
The controls will take a while to get used to if you are a Cod or BF player. The sound in this game is amazing. The cracks of gunfire sound impressive and most importantly are a good indicator of where your enemy is.
There is a minimum HUD which only exacerbates the feel of a real gunfight. There is a compass at the bottom of the screen with numbers which correspond to different areas around you. "Contact NE 255!" for example is a way in which players indicate where hostiles are.
You will require patience and planning to execute plans.
For me the most impressive part of this game is the community. Players LISTEN to directives and follow through with orders from their squad leader. I have never been a Squad Leader and not felt in full control of my team. The teamwork in this game is amazing.
If you like tactical gunplay don't hesitate. At first you will probably be overwhelmed and then everything will just click.
Levels are huge, sprawling and realistic. Foliage and cover plays a realistic and immersive place for hiding or setting up ambushes. It will be hard to see enemies unless you are paying attention and concentrating on abnormalities in the terrain. Some people complain about spotting enemies .. but it works.
Squad leaders can set up rally points which act as spawn points for their team. Each member also has a shovel in which the squad leader can set up FOB's (forward operating bases). Then players can use them to craft and setup bases which can be spawned in. You can set up sand bags and basically outfit a base of operation on almost any area of the map.
Again. If you are on the fence just jump to the other side.
The developers are 100% in on development. There will be vehicles and such in later updates which will change the dynamic of this game.

Wallpaper Engine provides what it promises, animated wallpapers with audio including 3D and 2D animations, websites, videos and even certain applications. Choose an existing wallpaper or create your own and share it on Steam Workshop
Pro's
- It brings life to the boring wallpapers most users are used to with animation or sound or intereaction
- Support many files types and support 4k@60fps
- Allows users to change fps playback rates to make the wallpapers less demanding.
- Wallpapers will pause while playing games.
- Wallpaper interface and search and filters are well made.
- One of the few softwares on steam i'd recommend and for such a low price its hard not to.
- Easy to upload new content to workshop and isn't crazy and forcing you to jump through hoops
- The Dev's care about their software at this time and have tried to help me personally resolve bugs and reply a lot to post on the steam forums.
- Text is reable on a 2560x1440 monitor and resizes great to higher than 1920x1080 monitors.
Con's
- No Global Volume sliders to lower all wallpapers default volume levels (50% is default)
- It always is telling me "No Connection to steam, loading wallpapers from cache" when I am connected to steam and their isn't any issues with steam or it's API
- Video playback while uploading to steam workshop so the video and sound will be playing as you upload. (Requested and might be fixed in future)
- Very small 1440p and higher wallpaper selection but as more people purchase and make more this won't be as much of an issue. I'd recommend looking at the selection before purchasing it.
- Mute sounds should be added to a global volume sliders and slide it to 0% volume but instead it is hidden under Advanced Options and called Video audio output which is silly.

I should probably preface this buy saying that is this my first 8th gen game so I won't be talking graphics. So, what can you expect from this game?
Awesome mechanics
Fantastic artistic direction
Great characters
Loads of polish and small details adding to this well realised world (alternate 1960s Beatles are amazing, and the enigma code breaking was wonderful tangential learning)
Is there anything for me to criticize: Yes:
I was shocked that a game with the scale and budget of a hollywood blockbuster would have such a poorly handled story. Locations in which you play take place all across the globe, and most of them are in sections of areas, meaning there isn't much world building/exploration which results in the main problem: cohesion. The plot explains where you're going and drops you off so quickly you don't get the feeling of traversing the face of the earth, leaving a schizophrenic feeling in the level design and colour pallet. A conversation will start in the rebel base and end in:
- London at night
- A Nazi concentration camp in the Fall
- A REKT bridge in the middle of the sea
- The moon… THE MOON! WHAT?
The constant jump cut story telling almost killed any investment in the plot and completely ruined the ending for me, leaving a very bitter taste in my mouth: after the climax, you have a cinematic that probably lasts a minute before the credits roll. THAT IS NOT HOW YOU CONCLUDE A 14 HOUR STORY, AND THE PRECEEDING CLIMAX WAS AMAZING BY COMPARISON!
I only point out this problem because everything else by comparison was beyond fantastic. What they fail at with the over arching plot, they make up for with the small details. Asside from a few level locations, I refuse to spoil anything else, but be aware, this game's storytelling really don't flow well at all. I guess the acid test is: “Would I ever replay this game from beginning to end?” and my answer is: probably not. I may comeback for some of the moments that made my jaw drop, but I'd be using the chapter select feature.

Some of the most fun I've had playing an FPS in years.  I always appeciate a game in this genre that decide to focus just on singleplayer instead of multiplayer.  The story, while not treading any new ground, is servicable and the characters are likable and believable.  It's an alternate 1960 in which Nazi Germany won and now has crazy future tech to keep the population under their boot.  The game takes you to many fun locations all over the world that look beautify ranging from Nazi Berlin, to under the sea in a U-Boat to a Nazi moon base!  There is also a large perk system that both rewards you for your play style while incentivizing you to change up the way you play to explore all the ways you can approach situations.
Luckily, the game play is even better.  The classic play with few modern additions are greatly apperciated by myself.  Health only partial regenerates up to the closest multiple of 20 up to 100 HP and you can pick up armor points to supplement.  Being able to carry all the weapons you find without having to give up a weapon is also classic.  Each weapon has a secondary fire AND can be dual wielded.  You can control the secondary mode of each dual-wielded weapon seperately which allows for easy use of both modes at the same time.  You do lost the ability to aim down the sights, but they remain manageable as long as you don't fire in full auto except at close range.  The hell you can unleash when nessarary is a blast.
Another surprise is the relatively fun stealth system.  The AI isn't exactly the smartest about reacting to all the dead Nazis you leave in your wake, but it still is fun to sneak around stabbing unsuspecting Nazis.  You can throw extra knives from a distance to silent kill from a distance.  Remain in stealth when a commander is present keeps extra enemies reinforcements from coming.  Going in hot will cause a constant stream of angry Nazis to show up until you manage to kill all present commanders.
If you are anything like me, wishing you could play another FPS that takes insperation from the games of 15 years ago instead of being another CoD shooter, you'll love this game.  Totally worth couple playthroughs.

This game is solid in every way. The action is good, but, against all stereotypes, this shooter is carried by its film noire storyline and its soundtrack. Yes, I said soundtrack. In an industry where the motto goes "a good soundtrack is the one you don't notice", Rockstar has pushed the soundtrack to the front and they know what they are doing.  This isn't the first game with an emotional story, but I bet you've never had such events driven home by the soundtrack quite like you will experience here.
Only downside in this game is how unpolished (yet very important) those last-chance kills are. When you die, you get a couple of seconds to turn your fate around by shooting your killer. The game makes full use of this by putting you in positions where you WILL die (and come back). Well, 60% of time it doesn't work, either because the enemy shot you through a wall or because Max doesn't want to turn and aim at him. So you just stand there, watching the game urge to do something that can't be done. It's practically mocking you and you will be very annoyed. Other than that, it's a solid game.

Puzzle games on PC have a bad reputation. Most puzzles in PC games tend to be pixel hunts, or require the use of an esoteric form of logic in combining items to solve them. The Talos Principle from the developer known for the Serious Sam series Croteam, bucks this mind boggling trend. Instead they give you a game that requires you to use not only visual logic to solve the puzzles, but an understanding of time as well. This leads to a game that is not only fun to play, but addicting as well.
The Talos Principle is very similar to the game Portal. Complete each puzzle world and move onto the next. During your puzzle solving escapades, you learn about the game world and try to piece what happened to it to together. Whereas in the Portal series the story was told by graffiti, PA announcements, and by the main antagonist, The Talos Principle does this through the use of computer terminals where you can read e-mails, hidden audio logs, and hidden Q-Codes. These Q-Codes are not only readable in game, but also readable by a code reader on the players phone. Cool fact - The player is also allowed to periodically paint their own Q-Codes in the game world. These codes then become apart of the game world and are available to be read by the player in later play-throughs.
The puzzle solving in The Talos Principle can be very fun and sometimes frustrating. Each overworld is divided into multiple arenas. Each arena is subdivided into individual puzzle areas. At the start of each puzzle, you are told what items are needed to solve it, and these items are available in the puzzle area. It is then up to the player to combine these elements together to solve the puzzle and get a Tetris style piece. Sometimes the combinations required to solve the puzzle are not obvious and can lead to back-tracking and the need to reset the puzzle. In some of the puzzles, not only do you have to combine the tools together, but also avoid items that will kill you. If you die, the player is reset to the start of their current puzzle. For some of the harder puzzles, this can be quite frustrating. The player uses these Tetris pieces to complete additional puzzles to unlock new abilities and overworlds.
Where the puzzle solving in this game shines is in its bonus puzzles. Each puzzle arena has at least one star hidden in it. To get these stars, the player is required to think "outside of the box." This can mean that the player will have to combine elements from different puzzle areas to unlock the star. This creates a puzzle that gives the player a sense of accomplishment when they solve them. I had more than one "a-ha" moment while trying to solve them. Collect enough of these stars and you can unlock new puzzle arenas that contain advanced puzzles. After the puzzle solving required to collect the stars, these advance puzzles are easy to complete.
While The Talos Principle's puzzles are awesome, the game is let down by the use of a check-point save system. While there are multiple checkpoints scattered through out the game world, there are none in the puzzles themselves. As stated earlier, if you die while working on a puzzle, no matter if you are right next to the goal, the puzzle resets to its starting state. Since death is instant, this can be quite frustrating for some of the longer puzzles. I could understand the logic behind check points during the early days of gaming when memory was in short supply, but today the use of this mechanic is, in my opinion, lamentable and is only used to extend game play time. The graphics, on the other hand, are amazing. They are so highly detailed that the player is immersed into the game world. I often found myself just exploring to look at the splendor that Croteam created.
Despite its use of a check point save system, The Talos Principle is a highly addictive and fun game. From its beautifully rendered world to its finely crafted puzzles, the player is left with a sense of wonder upon completion of the game. I highly recommend this game to anyone who loves puzzle games or is looking to try the genre out for the first time.

The storyline turns the secret history of World War II that was present in the earlier games in the series and turns it into an alternate series where the Nazis have won the war and completely taken over. After a last gasp attempt to take out a Nazi General goes completely wrong, our hero William "BJ" Blascowickz gets some shrapnel lodged in his brain and goes comatose for 14 years, during which the Nazis conquer the rest of the world. He eventually wakes up from his coma to find that the world he knew is completely gone, and ventures out with his sexy Polish nurse to find what cells of resistance that remain and find a way to defeat the Nazis.
It's a good premise, and the "What If?" scenario gets a lot of mileage, through dialogue and records and news articles, demonstrating that, indeed, Nazis were as awful as we always thought they were. The characters all feel real, doing what they can to fight the Nazis and keep their spirits up, but slowly starting to break down due to the crushing weight of it all. Even the most unlikeable of the support characters are still relateable and human, and the villains, while cartoonishly evil, are very competent, rational, and, above all ruthless. Story is indeed one of the stronger points of The New Order. There are some flaws; it should be paced a bit better, settings get changed out for new ones seemingly instantly; You go from train station to submarine to secret moon base to museum with scarcely a cutscene connecting all the locations. It really feels like the story for the locations was figured out after the locations themselves. The two alternate timelines change absolutely nothing, save for some dialogue and cutscenes; some alternate missions and a different ending could've been done as well to make it feel more like the choice really mattered.
Overall, it's a good story with some minor flaws, plot holes, and sticking points. Definitely the strongest out of all the Wolfenstein games up to this point.
The gameplay is a hybrid of modern shooters and the older level-by-level FPS' from which Wolfenstein derives its namesake. Your health regenerates (up to a point), Iron Sights are a thing, Enemies take cover and you're encouraged to as well. The game is also murky as all hell, too, which I blame purely on the post-processing effects, which make it incredibly hard to see what you're shooting at. However, the levels are also open-ended, with exploreable side paths and secret areas, Collectibles, ammunition, health and armor all need to be monitored and can be found lying around the level rather than just being given to you like some other shooters I could Call of Duty, I mean mention.
It all works rather well and makes the game actually fun to play, even if it gets frustratingly difficult at times. It's possible for the checkpoint save system to go off when you don't have any health or ammo, and then trap you in a hard boss fight or throw an army of Nazis at you while you have nothing but a butter knife to make do with, but there weren't any levels or locations that I found insurmountably difficult. The game doesn't have Evil Within problems, at least, where it was never clear whether or not enemies were even taking damage; juicy bullet squibs pop out of squishy Nazis, Bright orange fluid leaks out of their giant robots, and the ting of gunfire hitting armor can be heard even at long distances. Enemies require a variety of weapons and tactics to defeat, although I discovered very few enemies that were any match for my trusty lazer rifle.
It's definitely one of the better shooting experiences I've had in a while: It's fun, intense, and difficult, and is the highlight of the Wolfenstein experience.
Nothing really worth mentioning on the technical or performance front. VT Compression and a decent amount of V-Ram are neccessary for good performance. 64-Bit system is a must or the game won't even run. Overall, it's a decent port and runs generally smoothly. Those post-processing effects though.... Ugh. Gross. Disable those if you can. None of the graphics options seem to actually do much of anything, and the low and medium presets actually make the game run WORSE because they disable VT Compression and set the VT Cache to low.
BUUUUGGGGGGGYYYYY and their matchmaking is broken.

What can I say about Age of Empires 2- Really, it is very hard to find a place to begin that adequately gives this game credit. Age of Empires 2 is one of the best old school rts games ever made and the HD Edition just makes that so much more clear (literally).
Between the new content via expansion packs, additional compatibility with newer OSes, Steamworks and workshop support there is just so much here on offer. Some may say that the graphics are not improved enough, that the game still looks old and to them I say- yes. So? This is a HD remaster rather than a HD remake and with a game like this which has aged very well that is all we really needed.
Age of Empires 2 boasts a massive array of empires to use, each with their own tile sets and unique special units. It has a full map editor which allows for certain scripted events, a series of full campaign maps and a scenario/skirmish mode significantly buffed with additional features. You can really tell the people who did this remaster really love the game.
In this day and age where NEW traditional RTS games are few and far between (I am looking at you grey goo) Age of Empires 2 will always be welcome. All we can hope for now is an eventual revival to the core game series and a remaster of the original Age of Empires.

-Teamwork and Communication (This game relies heavily on leadership, cooperation, and communication. Without these, you will not have a successful squad)
-Limited Roles (I like the fact that everyone cannot choose whatever loadout they want. They have to chose the role that is needed in their squad)

"Back with a vengenace; Max Payne lives again." 9/10
"There it was, like a cheap bottle of bourbon at a discount liquor store, on sale and just begging for me to play it; I knew I was in for a long night." And indeed I was, because 'Max Payne 3' is one of the best stories that I've watched unfold in quite a while. Now I know what you're thinking, you're thinking that this game has far too many cut-scenes for anyone to find the story even remotely engrossing, that nobody buys a game to watch it - they buy it to play it, and I probably would have agreed with you early on in the story. But after around the third act, I stopped caring that the cut-scenes were constantly interrupting the gameplay, and sat back and began treating 'Max Payne 3' as a fantastic interactive movie, eagerly awaiting the next scene to move the story along.
"All that is gold does not glitter, or at least that's what I was told before the world decided to stab me in the back and twist the knife." Another aspect that made this game extremely fun to watch is how pretty the graphics are, and how stylized the look feels while maintaining that gritty undertone that made the original 'Max Payne' so enjoyable. The action here is on par with what you would expect from a blockbuster movie, the writing is just as clever as the earlier 'Max Payne' games, and hearing Max speak that drunken philosophy of a man who has it all figured out but just doesn't care is great to hear again. The entire game just feels very reminiscent of the earlier releases, while managing to feel fresh and new at the same time.
"They say it's the small things that make life worth living, funny, I guess I never got that memo." I love how 'Max Payne' takes out some of the most annoying aspects of games these days. Like having to press a button to climb a ladder, or open a door, or interact with anything. Or how Max automatically reloads his gun or begins to walk just before a cut-scene. It's tiny details like this that made this game especially enjoyable for me to play through. Aside from that 'Max Payne 3' stays fairly true to the original, and I know some people really hated the addition of cover, but for me, it still feels like the 'Max Payne' that I grew up loving. If you were a fan of the Max Payne of old, you're sure to like the new and improved one as well. "It was over faster than it began, like an hour with a harlot, the time had come to finish."

This game puts you through so many intense, memorable moments that you'd swear the random strangers you've been fighting alongside had been your comrades for years. Seriously, it's that good.
One thing that really stands out is the sound design. You wouldnt expect it from a non-AAA title, and an early access one at that, but it is incredible. There are, as far as I know, no ambient war sounds. Everything you hear, whether it be distant explosions or a machine gun going off over the hill nearby, is all happening in real time, making this game that much more immersive.
This is the war game I always dreamed about when I was younger. I watched it get funded on kickstarter, and now I regret not pitching in some money when I had the chance. I am normally not big in to pvp games, but this one is an exception.
A few things that make this game so amazing:
- No crosshairs
- Realistic reload times and proper dry reloading
- No name tags above enemies. They are just soldiers, as you are to them.
- No kill feed. This is war, you have to verify your kills, or just hope they don't get back up.
- One of the best communities in any first person shooter I've ever played. Every game I've been in has been full of friendly, fun people who all work together.
- Limited special weapons, meaning you don't have to worry about facing endless snipers *cough* Battlefield *cough"
- Very large maps with varied terrain
- Base building (seriously, taking over a compound and putting up walls and sandbags is amazing)
Right now this game is a definite 9/10, the only thing for holding it back is the lack of vehicles (which are in the works), and some occasional bugs (I. E. Menus not showing up properly, very seldom crashes, it is incredibly stable for how early of a build it is)
If you too enjoy MilSim games, do not hesitate to purchase this. It is worth every penny in my opinion.
(Edit 11/2/2016) Alpha v7 brought on a small selection of basic light vehicles, but also destroyed performance on any servers with about 50 or more people. Yesterday Alpha v8 was released, and now the game plays smooth as silk. I would highly, highly recommend this game with the recent patch. It is pure joy to play.

This is the only game that lets you be:
- a jetpacked commando dropping from an airship, causing mayhem behind enemy lines
- a cloaked predator-style hunter with a crossbow, an unseen menace thinning enemy reinforments.
- a defiant squad captain, quietly leading a ragtag team to glory as the higher-ups squabble.
- a sadistic bomber gunner, looking down on the insects below, laughing maniacally while liberating dozens from the shackles of their puny lives.
- a grizzled war vet forced out of retirement to support the war effort as an engineer/miner/truck driver, dodging enemy tank fire, designing bases and meeting supply deadlines.
Nothing so far in the FPS genre is close to matching Planetside 2's sense of scale. All out infantry, tank and aircraft combat with thousands of other players in a seamless large map. Every so often you'll get that epic 2-hour, 300 man-fight. There's something unique about the feeling of fighting hordes of tanks and endless swarms of infantry, knowing behind each unit is a person controlling, thinking and adapting.  With comms blaring with callouts for aerial bombardment and coordinated pushes into crucial control points, the immersion you get from this game is pretty intense.
The rest of the time, you find yourself looking for ways to be entertained, and still, the game isn't bad at doing so. Each infantry class and vehicle offers a unique playstyle and allows for quite a bit of role play and experimentation.
I've logged around a thousand hours in this game. Sure, the experience has been a bit uneven, and it's definitely not for everyone. Maybe 1/5th of that time was wasted on capping almost empty bases, or mindlessly spawn camping with a zerg that could care less about strategy. Still, this game definitely has its moments, and offers just enough unique thrills to keep coming back.

Short version:
The best and most non-p2w f2p MMOFPS around.
Extended version:
A wonderful online shooter with a great progression ladder, it's definitely a shot if you don't want to spend a buck since only skins and infantry/vehicle sounds are money-only.
To add, all weapons are entirely balanced, the starter weapons are not "better" or "inferior" to any other weapon, only in different situations some weapons have preference (i.e. a shotgun with more range to clear larger rooms easier at the cost of rate of fire for example).
A tip for the starting player would be to search friends or an outfit (a guild/clan), since lone-wolfing will get you killed without revives all-too-often, and thus will halt your cert-gain (currency) considerably.
Here are the pros and cons of the game:
PROS:
- Graphically good for MMOFPS.
- Fun teamgame.
- Big battles with more than 100 players on each side in an area.
- The ability to upgrade your character like you want (you can choose what kind of mods on your weapon and character, for example you can take a suit which allows you to wear more grenades or ammo, a damage reduce-suit or if you feel like it, a sprint speed suit).
- Different weapons on vehicles (this is much fun if you want to convert your light tank to a mobile AA and stuff, also the previous point about mods also applies to vehicles).
- > BALANCED WEAPONS! <  (the struggle of 95% of MMOFPS's)
CONS:
- Need a decent rig to get 60fps on full graphics with more than 30 people and some explosions around.
- By decent in the previous point I mean very-decent, a 700 bucks self-sorted PC with new gen game graphics (like the Nvidia GTX *50 (* meaning 5 to 10) and up to *70) might still have 40 FPS or lower in certain situations.
- Hard to lone-wolf.
- Learning curve if never played big battle games like this or Red Orchestra etc.
SCORE:
8.5/10 Never seen such a well-balanced f2p game before. These devs are doing it RIGHT for a change.

This has to be one of the best games I've played... Ever! I couldn't leave it for long before I had to come back.
Unfortunately my hardware didn't allow me to enjoy it all it's glory. But in 800x600 windowed mode it was still a great experience.
The Talos Principle is a puzzle extravaganza with a philosophical backstory driving it and I loved almost every minute of it. I say almost, because the puzzles are numerous and can sometimes be quite repetitive and tedious. I had more than a few moments of sheer frustration and also great joy when accomplishing various tasks. Also, discovering that certain objects could be placed in locations I hadn't initially realized was possible left me banging my head against the wall on occasions. Ouch!
The atmosphere of being alone in a crumbling reality trying to piece a mystery together is almost flawless in it's execution. The visuals aren't extraordinary but works for this type of game (although that could be due to my limited hardware, so take that with a pinch of salt). The sound design more than makes up for it in any case. And the music is awesome! I'm definitely getting the OST DLC.
Replayability? I'm not sure about that. Maybe after a few months, but for me personally when I've finished the main story of any game it's sort of done for me and I rarely return. But then, this game is different so who knows.
All in all a superb game I would reccomend you pick up and play if you haven't done so already. You won't be disappointed.

I highly recommend this game to anyone who likes games that encourage serious thought. The Talos Principle is often compared to the Portal series, but that's primarily because they fall into roughly the same genre and they both involve AI. It would be like comparing Limbo to Super Mario Brothers because they're both side scrolling platformers that involve a male protagonist seeking after a female character. Otherwise these games are radically different in tone and style. Likewise I really like Portal, but for very different reasons; the mood is altogether different.
I don't know how many games I've ever played that include quotes from everything from Aristotle to William Blake to G. K. Chesterton. The diversity of sources correlates well with the diversity of thought expressed thematically throughout. Through the events of the game, the slowly revealed backstory, and the numerous bits of literature and philosophy scattered about, the game leads you through a long deep musing on life, death, civilization, and the nature of consciousness. Yet, The Talos Principle never comes across (at least to me) as pretentious or smug. (The continuous focus on fun challenging puzzles might have something to do with maintaining an effective balance here.) There is definitely a coherent story with a very satisfying ending, but there's still a good bit of unanswered questions--in a good way. It muses more than it preaches, and through the course of the experience you are invited into that contemplation.
I probably haven't said much more than has already been said, and any more words would continue to fail to express the wonder of this electronic piece of art, but it is truly fascinating, thought-provoking, inspiring, and simply entertaining. There's not much more I could ask for in a game.

Dirty bomb is a free to play shooter that doesn't use the pay to win formula used by a lot of free to play shooters these days.
Dirty bomb opts for the pay to skip model while still giving players a way around the large character prices via "badges" which are awarded for players doing special tasks or tasks that someone would HAVE to do to win. Ex: planting the bomb, escorting the EZ, getting tons of kills, etc.
Dirty bomb's ONLY problem is the randomness of a "loadout card" mechanic.
Basically the loadout cards determine what guns and perks your character gets.
You can recycle loadout cards you don't care about for ones you do in order to get a garunteed level of loadout card.
Dirty bomb actually makes it, however, so that even if you buy the "best" loadout card that you still have to have skill with the character you use in order to be successful.
Overall Dirty Bomb is one of the most solid games for being in beta.
The same 10 or so maps are the only other major problem in the game... and the devs even announced that they are making MANY new ones.
Needless to say if you want to play the lovechild of CS:GO and Overwatch for FREE, then Dirty Bomb is for you

I highly recommend this game to anyone who likes games that encourage serious thought. The Talos Principle is often compared to the Portal series, but that's primarily because they fall into roughly the same genre and they both involve AI. It would be like comparing Limbo to Super Mario Brothers because they're both side scrolling platformers that involve a male protagonist seeking after a female character. Otherwise these games are radically different in tone and style. Likewise I really like Portal, but for very different reasons; the mood is altogether different.
I don't know how many games I've ever played that include quotes from everything from Aristotle to William Blake to G. K. Chesterton. The diversity of sources correlates well with the diversity of thought expressed thematically throughout. Through the events of the game, the slowly revealed backstory, and the numerous bits of literature and philosophy scattered about, the game leads you through a long deep musing on life, death, civilization, and the nature of consciousness. Yet, The Talos Principle never comes across (at least to me) as pretentious or smug. (The continuous focus on fun challenging puzzles might have something to do with maintaining an effective balance here.) There is definitely a coherent story with a very satisfying ending, but there's still a good bit of unanswered questions--in a good way. It muses more than it preaches, and through the course of the experience you are invited into that contemplation.
I probably haven't said much more than has already been said, and any more words would continue to fail to express the wonder of this electronic piece of art, but it is truly fascinating, thought-provoking, inspiring, and simply entertaining. There's not much more I could ask for in a game.

There's a million things i could say about planetside 2, but no one likes reading long reviews, so i'll keep it short.
Basically, if you like first person shooters, you like planetside 2, but there's a few things to keep in mind.
This game in NOT PAY TO WIN. i have put a grand total of $5.99 into this game, only to get weapons i don't use because they don't fit my playstyle. The only items that can only be purchased with real money are purely cosmetic. And the default weapons aren't bad either. in fact, some of the default weapons are considered the best in the game.
This game is not easy for new players. it has a very steep learning curve. it's an issue that the devs are actively trying to fix, but right now it's a bit of a problem. Right now, you'll likely have to look up a few tutorial vids to get to grips with how the game works, as the in game tutorial explains the basics of the mechanics found in all first person shooters, not the ones specific to planetside. once you finish the tutorial, you get thrown into koltyr, a very small map made for new players. i suggest going straight into the real fights on the larger continents. You'll get a much better feel of the massive scale of the game, and in my experience, koltyr is generally quite empty.
i suggest playing medic or engineer for your first few hours, since they are important players in any fight and it's a good way of raking up some cash for weapon attachments.
TO SUMMARISE:
it's not pay2win, it's not easy, play medic for an easy start

In just the short time I played the game, I do have a few pros and cons to point out.
Pros: It's a fun top-down zombie shooter, especially when you can co-op with other players. Endless fun until you're dead, aim to be at the top of the leaderboards.
Cons: Unfortunately, there seems to be some major lag when playing with other people online. =( I think the only way this game can be enjoyable and lag-free is via LAN with some real life friends. Some other notes also, I bought the Auto Turret, thinking it's a machine gun turret that'll fire at zombies if they get too close (dunno if it can rotate 360 degrees or not, or if zombies have to be in front of it, or if it can shoot over barricades). But when I bought it, I watched as the zombies went up to it, bashing it, and destroyed it, and it never fired a single shot. =( Is there something we're supposed to do to get it working? Or is it just a broken item? Another problem also is I found the Flame Thrower to be utterly useless. Short spurt of flame, then reload. Short spurt, reload. Never seen a flame thrower with such a small capacity, and when I played one online game with this person, it was just an utterly useless weapon. The shotgun turned out to be the better option as the spread shots would hit multiple zombies better than the flame thrower (also flame thrower doesn't seem to catch zombies on fire, or you just don't see the fire animation on the zombies, so you can never tell if you got them or not).
So yea, unfortunately the cons outweigh the pros right now, as I can't think of many pros. It is fun though, and I love how it has trading cards too (selling those should cover the cost of buying my copy of the game). I hope the devs work out some bugs, and polish it up abit. After all, it's supposedly a "Zombie Defense" game, where you gotta survive, but at the same time you can build barricades and turrets, you'd think it could be a tower defense game as well. Sadly, what good is a tower defense if the tower (in this case the auto turret) doesn't even work? It's utterly pointless to even have in the game then. =-(
I'd still recommend this game to friends, but only in the hopes that this game gets some free updates or even free extra content, then it'd be all worth it.
*EDIT* Ha, ironic, I didn't realize it, but there was this small window still open in the backround after I had exited the game. I looked at it, and it was a thank you from the devs for playing the game. It also said if the game became popular and would earn ratings, they will include extra content free of charge, with new weapons and even game modes. That just made my day, thank you devs! =) Though I won't be editing my review on the cons till all noted issues are resolved. XD But I will recommend the game!

Hi Everybody !
I've been playing since the first alpha release, like 2-3 years ago, and let me tell you that this game is a pure bomb ! As someone who was fond of Dwarves Fortress, but wasn't skilled enough to read into the Matrix, Rimworld was a Messiah for me.
The game bsaics are easy to understand and very intuitive. The first and only true goal you have is surviving. For everything else, it's up to you to decide : Merchant city, wild scavenger, Altruistic township, or even warmongger that feed of the prisoner they capture. The games is not fully completed yet, as I think there is a lot more cool stuff that could possibly be added (Underground Mine, advanced diplomatic with other tribes, and why not, a Multiplayer version of the game without any mean of pausing the game), but you have still a decent amount of items and customization possibility.
The Graphics are nice. It's obviously not GTA5, but it's good at what it aims. You can grasp what is going on in a single look, it's clean enough so you can attach yourself with the character, and it isn't too ressource costly, so your computer isn't gonna Rip into peperonni when lots of stuff are gonna happen (and they will, trust me).
The sounds effects are kinda the same. Good and Distinguishable, and the gunshot, coupled with the fact your characters can die pretty fast, are clean enough to give you some thrill.
The OST is very nice and adapted to the context. it's not something i'm gonna listen to everyday, like the Halo/Civilization OST, but it's pleasant while ingame.

I'll be honest, every week or so, i try to return to this game for what nostalgia i have left for it, for how much love i have for the concept, and how much hope i have for it, but yet, every single time, i am met with absolute terrible netcode, servers kicking me out for no notable reason, matches freezing, and just plain unfair mechanics all around.
Robocraft was a great game. But now its just a painful grindy experience with forced mechanics that should never have been there. Gamemodes are notably poorly planned, mostly the attempt at a MOBA gameplay, and the freedom of building the game might advertise is hidden behind absolute RNG-based grind.
Devs have been working on this game for a VERY long amount of time, and yet, its gameplay was once at its peak and most fun, even if grindy, is now lame, filled with meta-concepts of robots which are over-replicated and the shop system came only to increase that, and now with players constantly advertising their own abominations in the chat constantly, pledging for some in-game currency that will help them surpass the painful grind. Not to mention the plethora of bugs and awkward physics which seem to be on the bottom of the list when it comes to updating and fixing.
I must admit, i love this game, i want it to be good. But its not good. Its terrible. I would go as far as to say it shouldn't be as populated as it currently is, but i guess that those who were able to surpass the unfair grind and managed to amount a good arsenal are now the ones torturing the other players and breaking the only objective-based gamemode which attempts to be a MOBA. They won their right to be the ones crushing poor seal-bots who were built by players who didn't even have enough currency to make their necessary amount of cubes.
This is the Robocraft of now; Win boxes full of disappointment and fruitless effort, play matches where your only hope to have fun is to not take them seriously, and get killed by players in the most bizarre of laggy, messy and buggy situations, all the while suffering from unpolished physics conuundrums, game-breaking bugs and mechanics which are easily abusable.
Endless hours of fun, the RNG really keeps the game interesting.

This game is a gem of first person shooters. It doesn't have a multiplayer, but it does have a fantastic shooter oriented storyline that has you going to a multitude of locations doing what?..... Killing Nazi's!
Just like the other Wolfenstein's that have come before The New Order, the main name of the game is to kill a bunch of Nazi's in order to save the world. The cool part about this storyline is that it exists in a world where the Nazi's won WWII as they completed the A-Bomb first, among other things. The story telling is great, offering about 12 hours of gameplay. I was very satisfied with my gaming experience in a way that it reminds me of a 12 hour long, interactive movie.
The guns in this game feel raw and powerful, even though there isn't a lot of custumization. There is one gun in the game that improves from level to level if you take the time to find the secrets. But for the most part the rest of the weapons are the same throughout the game.
My only complaint is that this game did not challenge me in a way that I was expecting to. I played my first go through on hard with little issues. Basically as long as you don't get railed on by badguys you will be ok. Using the cover system is very important, as well as using the right gun for the encounter. This could be me, since I have played a lot of FPS, but at one point there is armor everywhere in the game and I never get enough badguys to kill where I feel like I need to use all of it.
Besides this, the game offers a fantastic cenematic experience for the player. Along with great action gameplay, and incase you need another reminder... you get to kill a lot of Nazi's!

I've been obsessed with this game since December 2015. I spent the first few months watching footage, not allowing myself to buy it because I didn't want it to consume all of my time. Then I managed to spend an equal amount of time watching gameplay of it everyday. Finally bought the game, so I've been playing and watching gameplay every day since then.
This game is so phenomenal, I don't know if I could accurately put in words how great it is. If you enjoy Banished or Prison Architect, get this game. You have to have it. The learning curve into surviving may be somewhat steep, but once you get it, get ready for hours upon hours of addictive gameplay.
The community surrounding this game is amazing as well: so many passionate players, streamers, youtubers. As well as the modders. If you can think of a feature in the game that you would enjoy, there's probably already been a mod made for it.
One of the most exciting things about this game is that it isn't fully released yet. Each alpha is like a brand new expansion pack full of engaging content that you get for free. And the developer/s seem to be so passionate about providing a thorough game that truly represents their abilities and the game that they and the community want it to be.
My only qualm that I can squander up is that endgame can get a little less engaging and very laggy (folks call them lag colonies when you get upwards of 30 pawns.) But that's only if you manage to make it to endgame. And I believe they intend to develop this bit and change some features regarding it. I've noticed some other reviewers mentioning that this game is actually fun to lose, and there's so much truth to that!
I would be shocked if someone did not recommend this game. The only reason I could think of is if they just didn't enjoy these types of games.
This game is worth every bit of the $30. I paid $30 months ago when I bought it. Older players weren't sure if they would get steamkeys due to Valve's policies, but I was more than willing to pay another $30 to purchase the game on Steam.

I love puzzle games. I like it when i am challenged. BUT THIS GAME TAKES IT TO ANOTHER LEVEL!!! Lets jump into the pros and cons.
Pros:
Beautiful Graphics: For a puzzle game, you wouldn't think that graphics would be top quality, but since my computer is able to run the ultra settings, its awesome to play.
Interesting Mysterious Backstory: Reading the notes and listening to the time capsules really gets you wondering just what you are, where you are, and what you are doing. I love continuing to learn as the game progresses.
Difficult Puzzles: I love puzzle games, and too often today they are much to easy. This game provides a unique new type of puzzle as well as giving you even more different ones later.
Addicting Searches: Part of the game is to find and collect some very hard to find/get to stars. I love trying to figure out just how to get to them.
Cons: To be completely honest I really can't think of any. For people who aren't good at puzzle games or give up easily I wouldn't reccommend this game.
Other than that this game is beautiful, interesting, and fun.

The perfect game for people who loved Portal 2.
I am obsessed with this game.  It is very rare to come across a game with challenging puzzles that also has an intriguing story.  The game is atmospheric--just wandering around the world is a lot of fun.  I still think Portal 2 has a more fun story (there's more humor in that game), whereas this game is more philosophical and rather depressing when you think about it.  But if you are craving a post-apocalyptic single-player puzzle adventure, this is YOUR game. I like the challenges and the way the story is revealed in stages as you make progress through the levels.  I got stuck a few times, but the internet is my friend.
My only negative criticism is that there are elements of the game that require having a smart phone.  I don't have one, so I had to look online for the translations of the qr codes used in the game.  However, these "secret" qr codes were pretty rare, so it wasn't a deal-breaker. There are also lots of cool easter eggs, only a few of which I found on my own (thanks again, internet!).

Rather than keeping you moving forward in the game, the game throws waves of enemies at you instead, keeping you ducking behind cover, rather than running and gunning.
The controls arent very smooth either. Especially the movement/diving controls. You will find yourself getting frustrated at max while you try to get him to do one thing, and he either doesnt respond well, or ends up doing something else. Glitchy things like diving towards and object and the game warping you to the top of the object can happen too. Most of the time when you die, it will be to something absolutely ridiculous and make you go "what the hell???". Other dumb things like headshotting an enemy, watching his body ragdoll to the ground, only to 3 seconds later get up and start shooting you again, will leave you baffled and having to shoot every body that falls the ground a second time just to be certain.
As far as this being a "max payne" game, well... its maybe 50% a max payne game. Sure, it has the bullet time, and the crazy shooting while flying through the air, but Rockstar, in all their creative genious, took too much of what made max payne, max payne... out of the game. No more comic slides for cut scenes, instead replaced by wannabe "Man on fire" cienematic effects that are just annoying. The look and feel of both max, and the settings, just doesnt feel like a max payne game 80% of the game. It feels more like a hybrid GTA game with max payne in it, than a max payne game.
If you are looking for a Max payne 1 or 2 experience... this game wont scratch that itch. At most, it will make you simply remember how good the first 2 games were and give you a desire to go back and play those games.

You create your own sanctuary (or lack thereof), trying to fend of wildlife and other villages/tribes of neerdowells, trying to get it to thrive.
I bought this game a few years ago, and it was stable then, so this early access is a very immersive and complete game. The developers keeps adding to it, and there is a large and thriving modding community, so no game is the same.
Verdict: 10/10 - would lose another sanctuary again.

I'm a shooter. Even in real life I love to go shooting. I've played a lot of Arma, DayZ, Battlefield, Verdun.. You name the FPS and I bet I've played 1k hrs of it.
What really caught me in this game, was the sounds. This game felt very familure in traveling to Arma, and DayZ.. Walking quietly through the woods, stop to take a smoke break.. hear a twig break in the trees and then all hell breaks loose after 20 minutes of strategically walking through a Forest. Nothing more caught my interest than the sounds of those bullets whizzing and crackling by my head. The sheer adrenaline I got from hearing those bullets told me my investment into this Alpha was well worth the ticket price.
The Objectives feel sort of like the Battlefield aspect of the game, with a bit of a twist. If you don't have great communication with your other Squad Leaders of what objectives to take and defend, a game can easily sway into the enemies favor. This is where communication and co-ordination is key. Knowing where to have your squad.
The Environment is beautiful. Every map puts you into the geographical immersion. From the color of the sand, to the fields of poppy, and beyond the teasing fields of sweet sweet Mary Jane. Every map is satisfying.
Now, to the guns.. the guns.. oh my the friggin awesome guns. I myself have not personally shot all of the guns in this game in real life. However the guns I have shot, the guns in game.. they feel 90% real. I say 90% because the other 10 is feeling the heat, smelling the gunpowder, getting the nice bruise from holding on too tight after a few spontanious 10 round sprays, ect. Things you cannot replicate in a game. Other than that, this game has covered all realistic aspects of the weapons by far. They feel oh so sweet, oh and the best way to get an annoying squadmate to stfu.. is to lay down a good suppressive fire and suppress their useless communication with overburdened sounds of gunfire.
If you are a FPS enthusiast.. If you like feeling achieved after confirming a kill, the right way.. by walking up and making sure that enemy is dead with a swift double tap. If you have played Arma, Battlefield, Red Orchestra.. any Military style shooter. Make sure your Mic works, and get SQUAD!
EDIT IN- 5/15/2016 Ok so I feel like a bit of a dummy, I've been playing Squad without even realizing it had a great history, with plenty of players who all enjoy the old version. I found out about Project Reality @
- I've been playing this FREE mod for a week or so now, and wow! After playing Squad and visiting Project Reality I am very excited to see the development of Squad turn into Project Reality V2!
If you really want to try out Squad, but don't want to fork out the money for EA, try out Project Reality, if you end up liking that.. Then you'll end up loving Squad by the time it is finished.

I would say that personally this borders with Portal for how great the story was given,
Simple puzzle mechanics like connecting beams to their respective colored connectors, figruing out how to get around gates/blockades, and using recorded actions to make a clone of your past self aid the present one.
This is not saying the simplified mechanics are bad; they are used in very unique ways. I compared it to Portal only for how it is story driven; both games have superb mechanics to solve their puzzles, but the Portal gun I found more original or different, because it allowed for more stylistic/dynamic gameplay.
For this game, if anything,
I found myself wanting to complete the puzzles to see what more data I could find on my own place in the story, as well as what had occurred causing the game's story.
What I also greatly appreciate in this game was the psychological/philosophical concepts portrayed and given for people to think on from the Terminals themselves.
It is an excellent design choice that I thoroughly enjoyed.
Religious overtones also play a part, but I would say that is in terms of story rather than concept. The game does not ask you questions on religion (or have you fully questioning it), but rather
The religious tones also show how different belief patterns are displayed in the actions and writings of the other characters, how it changes their choices, and shows how this is also a part of one's belief patterns, philosophy and to each their unique humanity.
I highly recommend that anyone would try this game; it challenges the mind in both objective puzzles, as well as philosophically with questions that are not regularly presented to the mind.

So much so, I have put in a lot more hours that it takes to complete the game for sake of just playing it again. The experience is absolutely unique. Wolfenstein: The New Order
Having not played any of the older games from this franchise this was a game that could be hit and miss. However the positive reviews upon release made me make my mind up rather quickly and I must say, this game is not a disappointment.
The game first takes place during WW2, and a fictional attack on the base of the main antagonist of the game is the setting. You should have died several times, but the character we play as (William J. Blazkowicz, a badass in every shape and form) shrugs off injuries that would kill lesser men. Things do not go according to plan, you get faced with a choice early on that actually has a greater impact on the rest of the game (maybe Telltale should take a leaf from Machinegames' book) not only does this pull at the heart strings slightly, it also adds to the replayability of the game.
Fast forward 14 years and the Nazi's have won the war and now control the world, all the while our character has been brain dead from a severe head injury. But of course this is Blazko, a badass. Apparently he is not so dead and makes a quick recovery after an unfortunate event prompts him in to action.
From start to finish the graphics and story are incredible, if you want to see what the Nazi's may have done if they had won WW2 then play this game, albeit with the helping of futuristic technology. The vast character development helps create a bond between the player and the characters themselves, you don't want to lose any of them. It helps create a sense of belonging that campaigns like CoD fail at every time. You want to be a part of the immersive story, you want to be there helping out.
There has been a little controversy with the sexual scenes but I found them to help add to the relationship of two said characters, making it seem more real. There are a variety of weapons to use, upgrades to be found in game, unique maps and diverse enemies requiring different tactics, all in all adding to a thoroughly enjoyable game.
You want to participate in a war killing hundreds of Nazi's like they are dust in the air, then play this game. Every character (good and bad) is fleshed out either through playing with and/or meeting plus the numerous collectibles/journals that can be found.
You want to walk on the moon while killing Nazi's? Play this game.
Plenty of collectibles to find in game that either enhance gameplay, provide background or unlock different game parameters (one life etc.) Each map is highly detailed, plenty of interactables. One part of the game I really liked were the newspaper cuttings that could be found all over the maps that help set the scene of the game.
Thoroughly enjoyable game and I do recommened it. The game runs okay on my laptop. There can be lagg spikes during cutscenes but my laptop can be to blame for that, it isn't that good. Perhaps buying for console would be a better choice if hardware is lacking. But I can still play and enjoy the game.
11/10 do recommened. :)

The Second World War really is the gift that keeps on giving in terms of popular entertainment from the last two decades to the point that I wouldn’t be surprised if every major game and film production company met up in the mid 1930s and somehow engineered the conflict so that they could have a guaranteed source of income forever.
The New Order is the latest entry in a long history of games that ritualise the slaughter of helpless Nazis. You play as William ‘B.J’ Blaskowicz, a man with a head that couldn’t be squarer if it never touched drink or drugs in an alternate timeline in which the Nazi’s have nuked New York and take over the world. You wake from a coma in 1960 and join a small band of resistance fighters as they struggle against the impossibly evil German Empire. It is a simple set-up and a strong one, as the test of a good idea is one’s ability to sum it up in one sentence, and in this case The New Order’s one sentence elevator pitch is “What if the Nazi’s won the Second World War?” an interesting question that the game explores briefly, before becoming bored and turning back to blasting Nazis in the face.
First issue with The New Order: impossibly evil Nazi enemy. I understand the legacy of the Wolfenstein series as essentially inventing the Nazi-em-up, and I understand how an alternative timeline in which the Nazi’s won the Second World War creates tension in your game, but this timeline is so alternate it feels like it’s from another planet. Though I would agree that perhaps the Nazi’s didn’t get everything right, I would also suggest that they weren’t so evil as to engineer giant robotic dogs and a division of mutant super-soldiers stitched into demonic power armour.
I wonder though whether the developers weren’t trying to make a point by pushing the evil meter to eleven when designing their Nazi empire. The game isn’t above the use of caricature; you have the pervy General, the General with the eye-patch, the vaguely homo-sexual General, the General who listens to classical music, and the slightly un-hinged lady General. The characterisation of the low-level grunts is more nuanced however and does portray at least some of the Nazis in the game as vaguely human. You overhear conversations between soldiers talking about their families and children, all the while running a thumb along the edge of your blade and eyeing their jugular hungrily. The New Order exploits the player’s understanding of the Nazis as portrayed in the last five decades or so by juxtaposing the depiction of its characters while simultaneously taking a sideways-glance at the genre it invented, a comment that is well executed when you give the game time do its thing.
If Wolfenstein invented the concept of Nazis as guilt-free bullet and blade storage solutions, it also invented shooting from a first-person perspective, and while I don’t want to get into an argument about ‘the original FPS’, Return to Castle Wolfenstein was the first to marry Nazis and heavy ordinance in a video game experience. There has been over two decades of development in the FPS genre since Castle Wolfenstein, and The New Order references every major milestone along the way; the crowbar from Half-Life, the beach assault section from pretty much every Medal of Honour game, character perks from Borderlands, and Vault 101 from Fallout all make appearances in The New Order. It doesn’t really do anything with these references though, aside from saying ‘look, Half-Life is a game that exists,’ and I can’t help but think that an opportunity has been lost.
If the Wolfenstein games invented shooting, The New Order doesn’t reinvent it. The way the game blends stealth and action is excellently executed – in the first two thirds of the game, almost every situation can be resolved quietly with a knife, or brutally with a shotgun, and you are never penalised for going all-out stealth or all-out action. Instead, The New Order cleverly rewards you in a way that is appropriate for your play-style; it understands that players who prefer to stealth their way through the game are more likely to be interested in collectibles, and so rewards stealthy players by highlighting the locations of collectibles on the in-game map, for instance.
When things do go loud the gameplay is somewhat less satisfying, however. Shooting is competent at best and dual-wielding weapons is a novelty I used a handful of times before returning to wielding one weapon for greater accuracy. Shotguns are also curiously float-y, and, since most of the combat is at mid-range anyway, rather pointless as well. There are also sections in the game where what is meant to be a quick, exciting escape from a powerful enemy turns into tedious trial-and-error. Call me inept but in some instances I only found the way to escape by accident rather than by any intuitive understanding of what I needed to do. I understand what the developers are trying to do with such sequences, but the impact of a sudden heart-stopping struggle in the middle of gameplay will be lost unless you manage to survive it first time.
As the game progresses, an attempt to ratchet up the action to an explosive crescendo means the emphasis leans much more toward action than stealth. The latter third of The New Order is all shooting with very few stealth paths available, and as a result the game suffers. Stealth is really where The New Order shines, but it seems to get bored around about the point you go to the Moon (spoilers) to literally print-off some nuclear deactivation codes and from then on is room after room of Nazis eager to have their faces rearranged with your lead.
The last third of the game in general seems rushed; character relationships are hinted at and then forgotten, some characters are forgotten about entirely, and in one section (if you’ve played the game, you’ll know exactly this point) ripe with potential for some interesting physics-based combat, you walk from one point to another and destroy exactly three drones.
All of this is frustrating because the game starts out so well; it’s alternative history setting is interesting, the blend of stealth and combat is excellent, and B.J’s character is well developed through a combination of cut-scenes and interior monologue. Once The New Order leaves Earth’s atmosphere though, it turns into Call of Duty but with Nazis. And Call of Duty has already done Nazis. So just Call of Duty then.
The difficulty with finding issues with a game like The New Order is in recognising the difference between genuine flaws in the game and flaws in the FPS genre in general, as the game has it’s tongue so firmly in it’s cheek it often isn’t clear whether the game is making a comment or not. Its attitude toward women is certainly taken from the modern-day FPS, with the main female character stepping into her role as boob-appendage with considerable aplomb. The visuals are average, with the occasional muddy texture, and more polish could have been used in cut-scene transitions, with somewhat jarring jumps from and into gameplay being the most common example.
What The New Order signals is an end of the World War Two-themed shooter, which is a shame because I think there are plenty of stories left to tell from that era . The problem is that any future game involving Nazis on any level will have The New Order somewhere in it’s DNA, and as soon as we start referencing games that are already themselves parodies, the space-time continuum will collapse.

I'm a shooter. Even in real life I love to go shooting. I've played a lot of Arma, DayZ, Battlefield, Verdun.. You name the FPS and I bet I've played 1k hrs of it.
What really caught me in this game, was the sounds. This game felt very familure in traveling to Arma, and DayZ.. Walking quietly through the woods, stop to take a smoke break.. hear a twig break in the trees and then all hell breaks loose after 20 minutes of strategically walking through a Forest. Nothing more caught my interest than the sounds of those bullets whizzing and crackling by my head. The sheer adrenaline I got from hearing those bullets told me my investment into this Alpha was well worth the ticket price.
The Objectives feel sort of like the Battlefield aspect of the game, with a bit of a twist. If you don't have great communication with your other Squad Leaders of what objectives to take and defend, a game can easily sway into the enemies favor. This is where communication and co-ordination is key. Knowing where to have your squad.
The Environment is beautiful. Every map puts you into the geographical immersion. From the color of the sand, to the fields of poppy, and beyond the teasing fields of sweet sweet Mary Jane. Every map is satisfying.
Now, to the guns.. the guns.. oh my the friggin awesome guns. I myself have not personally shot all of the guns in this game in real life. However the guns I have shot, the guns in game.. they feel 90% real. I say 90% because the other 10 is feeling the heat, smelling the gunpowder, getting the nice bruise from holding on too tight after a few spontanious 10 round sprays, ect. Things you cannot replicate in a game. Other than that, this game has covered all realistic aspects of the weapons by far. They feel oh so sweet, oh and the best way to get an annoying squadmate to stfu.. is to lay down a good suppressive fire and suppress their useless communication with overburdened sounds of gunfire.
If you are a FPS enthusiast.. If you like feeling achieved after confirming a kill, the right way.. by walking up and making sure that enemy is dead with a swift double tap. If you have played Arma, Battlefield, Red Orchestra.. any Military style shooter. Make sure your Mic works, and get SQUAD!
EDIT IN- 5/15/2016 Ok so I feel like a bit of a dummy, I've been playing Squad without even realizing it had a great history, with plenty of players who all enjoy the old version. I found out about Project Reality @
- I've been playing this FREE mod for a week or so now, and wow! After playing Squad and visiting Project Reality I am very excited to see the development of Squad turn into Project Reality V2!
If you really want to try out Squad, but don't want to fork out the money for EA, try out Project Reality, if you end up liking that.. Then you'll end up loving Squad by the time it is finished.

Age of Empires II HD is an excellent real time strategy game.  Why so?  Well it does many things in a great fashion.  Here is a list of reasons why:
-Simple yet complex resource gathering system
The way you collect resources in this  game is you select one or more villagers and you click on a resource to gather them.  There are a few resources such as food, wood, gold, and stone.  These are not a lot of different resources, yes, but this is actually more difficult than it sounds.  There is a mechanic in the game called a population limit, and if you reach the limit, you cannot product anymore units until a unit is killed or deleted.  This adds some strategy to how many villagers you use to gather each resource, typically for me gold being the bottleneck.
-Still gets updated from time to time
I do not own any of the DLCs, but this game was first released in 1998 i believe, and its still getting updates at the time I am writing this in 2017, so the devs really care about the well-being of the game, and I like that.
-Historically accurate
Personally, I really like history, it is very interesting to me about what has happened in the old days.  Just adds a nice touch to the game, but I guess why it's called Age of Empires.  This also includes the different civilizations in the game.  Each unique in their own way because of the upgrades they have access to and their unique unit.
-Replayable
I'm not really a big fan of buying a game for like 15 dollars and getting like 8 hours of story out of it.  That's like about 2 dollars an hour for a little amount of content.  Not this game.  This game is randomly generated when you start new games, which makes every game different, plus, there are many unique game settings that change things such as the goal objective, like Wonder Race, first one to build a wonder wins.
-Campaigns
You are given several different campaigns when you but the game, and I actually think that some of the missions are difficult, which makes them fun.  Some of the missions just really stress you out and force you to try things that are not part of your usual techniques, but that just adds to the experience.
-Soundtrack
This is possibly one of the best soundtracks I've ever heard.  When I play the game, I always look forward to hearing some of the songs.

I would  highly recommend it to anyone looking for a  strong puzzle game akin to portal, but much more serious in tone and pretty heavy in some side reading to get the full story (the side reading is in the game itself in video logs and text logs as you move along, you won't be doing much hunting for them although a few are hidden). It stands out as its own game from portal, but there are some comparisons to be made between the two (both are first person games that will require dodging turrents, bombs, etc. all while setting up puzzles with a variety of tools). It definitely isn't a clone though and has its own set of mechanics that set it far apart from portal. Definitely worth a look and a couple hours play time.

The good:
This game started off as an awesome game.  I love to play stealth FPS games.  This game started off giving me many approaches and a the full stealth experience of sneaking up or by enemies in the first few levels. The graphics were great and so was the game play.
The bad:
After the first few levels the quality of the levels noticeably deminished.  The levels were still a bit non-linear, but I no longer had the full freedom of the first few levels. There was a fair amount of unavoidable combat.
The Ugly:
A little past the half-way mark, any semblance of stealth and non-lineral levels dissapeared.  You were essently in a tube with no real choice on how to proceed and enemies always were in an alerted state. In quit this game in some level (I presume was a few levels from the end of the game) and everything wa super-scripted.  You could see a group of enemies from a great distance, and even if you stayed hidden and never moved, they would aggro you.  Stealth was 100% gone.  All the encounters past the prsion level (where you recruit some scientist guy) were nothing but scripted waves of enemies you fought and inearly 100%  lineral levels with no real choice in where you could go.
Unfortunatly this is a common problem in FPS games where they supposidly offer choicies of stealth and guns blazing.  The whole stealthy party goes by the wayside in leu of levels that are nothing buy hitting some trigger which causes waves of enemies to spawn.  Then each level is just about the same thing over and over.  It is like the developer needs another 4 or 5 levels but has run out of ideas.
Unless that appeals to you, I would advise you to stay away from this game.  It could have been great, but the only really good part is the early part of this game.
